d732b6f7eefd.section: Fossils as a basis for stratigraphic subdivision > Concept of zone > Index fossils
d732b6f7eefd.sentence: For instance, the presence of the trace fossil Treptichnus pedum was used to define the base of the Cambrian period, but it has since been found in older strata.

5855c7ccf7de.title: Geologic time scale
5855c7ccf7de.sentence: For example, in early 2022, the base of the Cambrian Period (a geochronologic unit) was revised from 541 Ma to 538.8 Ma but the rock definition of the boundary (GSSP) at the base of the Cambrian, and thus the boundary between the Ediacaran and Cambrian systems (chronostratigraphic units) has not been changed; rather, the absolute age has merely been refined.

7ecdbad64703.title: Paleozoic
7ecdbad64703.sentence: The base of the Paleozoic is one of the major divisions in geological time representing the divide between the Proterozoic and Phanerozoic eons, the Neoproterozoic and Paleozoic eras, and the Ediacaran and Cambrian periods.

632a4f0b9176.title: Paleozoic
632a4f0b9176.sentence: The base of the Phanerozoic, Paleozoic and Cambrian is dated at 538.8 ± 0.6 Ma and now lies below both the first appearance of trilobites and SSF.

fdd685efd320.title: Cambrian explosion
fdd685efd320.sentence: Several chemical markers indicate a drastic change in the environment around the start of the Cambrian.

33d06ce946a5.title: Cambrian explosion
33d06ce946a5.sentence: The Cambrian explosion (also known as the Cambrian radiation or Cambrian diversification) is a major evolutionary radiation event of the Earth's lifeforms beginning approximately 538.8 million years ago in the early Cambrian period of the Paleozoic era, during which a sudden diversification of complex life occurred in the fossil record.

c33f8f61d57e.title: Paleozoic
c33f8f61d57e.sentence: The Cambrian witnessed the most rapid and widespread diversification of life in Earth's history, known as the Cambrian explosion, in which most modern phyla first appeared.

c18b3d100611.title: Cambrian explosion
c18b3d100611.sentence: The early Cambrian interval of diversification lasted for about the next 20–25 million years, and its elevated rates of evolution had ended by the base of Cambrian Series 2, 521 million years ago, coincident with the first trilobites in the fossil record.

21688e590476.title: Cambrian explosion
21688e590476.sentence: The Cambrian explosion coincided with the evolution of mineralized tissues and skeletons, which are fossilizable and thus contributed greatly to the "explosive" abundance of fossil evidence in the early Cambrian while earlier Precambrian fossils are mostly mold, trace or chemical fossils instead of fossils proper.

92202d63abe0.title: Cambrian explosion
92202d63abe0.section: Possible causes > Changes in the environment > Increase in oxygen levels
92202d63abe0.sentence: Molybdenum isotopes show that increases in biodiversity were strongly correlated with expansion of oxygenated bottom waters in the Early Cambrian, lending support for oxygen as a driver of the Cambrian evolutionary radiation.

86fdbc34ecd8.title: Cambrian explosion
86fdbc34ecd8.section: Uniqueness of the early Cambrian biodiversification
86fdbc34ecd8.sentence: The rate of diversification seen in the Cambrian phase of the explosion is unparalleled among marine animals: it affected all metazoan clades of which Cambrian fossils have been found.

4e5d33ac0e07.title: History of life
4e5d33ac0e07.sentence: Nevertheless, there is still much debate about whether the Cambrian explosion was really explosive and, if so, how and why it happened and why it appears unique in the history of animals.

c966d2d014d9.title: History of Earth
c966d2d014d9.sentence: Life remained mostly small and microscopic until about 580 million years ago, when complex multicellular life arose, developed over time, and culminated in the Cambrian Explosion about 538.8 million years ago.

a6aa2d0fdfae.title: Cambrian explosion
a6aa2d0fdfae.sentence: Fossils known as "small shelly fauna" have been found in many parts on the world, and date from just before the Cambrian to about 10 million years after the start of the Cambrian (the Nemakit-Daldynian and Tommotian ages; see timeline).

b0f6028e908a.title: Cambrian explosion
b0f6028e908a.sentence: Graham Budd synthesises various schemes to produce a compatible view of the SSF record of the Cambrian explosion, divided slightly differently into four intervals: a "Tube world", lasting from 550 to 536 million years ago, spanning the Ediacaran-Cambrian boundary, dominated by Cloudina, Namacalathus and pseudoconodont-type elements; a "Sclerite world", seeing the rise of halkieriids, tommotiids and hyoliths, lasting to the end of the Fortunian (c. 525 Ma); a brachiopod world, perhaps corresponding to the as yet unratified Cambrian Stage 2; and Trilobite World, kicking off in Stage 3.

c9e20b8f182a.title: Paleozoic
c9e20b8f182a.sentence: The early Cambrian climate was probably moderate at first, becoming warmer over the course of the Cambrian, as the second-greatest sustained sea level rise in the Phanerozoic got underway.

6e53f66550e2.title: Sub-Cambrian peneplain
6e53f66550e2.sentence: The flatness of the peneplain meant that during the Cambrian transgression very large areas were swiftly flooded forming large and shallow inland seas in changing configurations.

c343296c16d2.title: History of Earth
c343296c16d2.sentence: There is also unconfirmed evidence that arthropods may have appeared on land as early as 530 Ma.

c1cce4cdbe24.title: History of life
c1cce4cdbe24.sentence: Trace fossils from the early Cambrian suggests mollusc-like animals could spend at least 15 minutes on land.

4f2e983bfe15.title: History of life
4f2e983bfe15.sentence: However, some earlier trace fossils from the Cambrian-Ordovician boundary about 490 Ma are interpreted as the tracks of large amphibious arthropods on coastal sand dunes, and may have been made by euthycarcinoids, which are thought to be evolutionary "aunts" of myriapods.

4867a9510bc7.title: History of life
4867a9510bc7.section: Emergence of animals > Deuterostomes and the first vertebrates
4867a9510bc7.sentence: Other deuterostome groups are soft-bodied, and most of the significant Cambrian deuterostome fossils come from the Chengjiang fauna, a lagerstätte in China.

756b5940e0e6.title: Vertebrate
756b5940e0e6.sentence: The earliest known vertebrates belong to the Chengjiang biota and lived about 518 million years ago.

1d5f0dec26ea.title: Vertebrate
1d5f0dec26ea.sentence: The first vertebrates appeared in the Cambrian explosion some 518 million years ago.

93851702095e.title: History of life
93851702095e.section: Emergence of animals > Deuterostomes and the first vertebrates
93851702095e.sentence: While tunicate fossils predate the Cambrian explosion, the Chengjiang fossils Haikouichthys and Myllokunmingia appear to be true vertebrates, and Haikouichthys had distinct vertebrae, which may have been slightly mineralized.

4734eec3706d.title: Vertebrate
4734eec3706d.sentence: Metaspriggina is another early vertebrate, known from the somewhat younger Burgess Shale of Canada, dating to around 505 million years ago.

3b2433c6b289.title: Crustacean
3b2433c6b289.sentence: The earliest crustaceans had already appeared in the fossil record by 517 million years ago during Cambrian Stage 3 in the Chengjiang biota, which represent relatives of living crustacean lineages, indicating that they had already substantially cryptically diversified by the mid-Cambrian, despite their sparse fossil record during this time.

457fe766927b.title: Cambrian explosion
457fe766927b.sentence: Crustaceans, one of the four great modern groups of arthropods, are very rare throughout the Cambrian.

d9eb5e32b85e.title: Crustacean
d9eb5e32b85e.sentence: Crustaceans have a rich and extensive fossil record, most of the major groups of crustaceans appear in the fossil record before the end of the Cambrian, namely the Branchiopoda, Maxillopoda (including barnacles and tongue worms) and Malacostraca; there is some debate as to whether or not Cambrian animals assigned to Ostracoda are truly ostracods, which would otherwise start in the Ordovician.

ff9a2c86d548.title: Cambrian explosion
ff9a2c86d548.sentence: Medusozoans developed complex life cycles with a medusa stage during the Cambrian explosion, as evidenced by the discovery of Burgessomedusa phasmiformis.

9047b7a46a72.title: Vertebrate
9047b7a46a72.sentence: A vertebrate group of uncertain phylogeny, small eel-like conodonts, are known from microfossils of their paired tooth segments from the late Cambrian to the end of the Triassic.

a1f505540653.title: Mollusca
a1f505540653.sentence: The Late Cambrian fossil Plectronoceras is now thought to be the earliest undisputed cephalopod fossil, as its shell had septa and a siphuncle, a strand of tissue that Nautilus uses to remove water from compartments it has vacated as it grows, and which is also visible in fossil ammonite shells.

f827e5874af0.title: Cambrian explosion
f827e5874af0.section: Relationship with the Great Ordovician Biodiversification Event
f827e5874af0.sentence: After an extinction at the Cambrian–Ordovician boundary, another radiation occurred, which established the taxa that would dominate the Palaeozoic.

ad8bb5343773.title: Paleozoic
ad8bb5343773.sentence: By the end of the Ordovician, Gondwana was at the south pole, early North America had collided with Europe, closing the intervening ocean.

bf32710e80c0.title: History of Earth
bf32710e80c0.section: Phanerozoic Eon > Tectonics, paleogeography and climate
bf32710e80c0.sentence: The continents Laurentia and Baltica collided between 450 and 400 Ma, during the Caledonian Orogeny, to form Laurussia (also known as Euramerica).

36e941093734.title: Geologic time scale
36e941093734.sentence: Phanerozoic | Paleozoic | Silurian | Pridoli | Laurentia and Avalonia-Baltica collide as Iapetus Ocean closes, Caledonian - Scandian orogeny, and formation of Laurussia. Other orogenies: Salinic (Appalachians); Famatinian (South America) tapers off; Lachlan (Australia). Series of microcontinents and North China separate opening Paleo-Tethys and closing Paleoasian Ocean. Rheic Ocean widens between Gondwana and Laurussia. Siberia drifts north of equator. Temperatures increase as Hirnantian glaciation ends. Sea levels rise. Deposition of black shales, North Africa and Arabia, major hydrocarbon source rocks. Fluctuating climate with glacial advances results in changing ocean conditions causes extinction events, followed by ecological recoveries. Widespread evaporite deposition and hothouse climate by late Silurian. After end-Ordovician mass extinction, major radiation of graptolites, bivalves, gastropods, nautiloids, brachiopods, and crinoids. Increase in trilobites, but never fully recover. Corals and stromatoporiods diversify to produce large reefs. Proliferation of eurypterid arthropods. Earliest jawed fish (acanthodians). Appearance of ostracoderms. Appearance of vascular plants. First land animals including myriapods. First freshwater fish. | 422.7 ± 1.6 *

13bfd93f5f6f.title: Fossil
13bfd93f5f6f.sentence: The connection between grazer and stromatolite abundance is well documented in the younger Ordovician evolutionary radiation; stromatolite abundance also increased after the end-Ordovician and end-Permian extinctions decimated marine animals, falling back to earlier levels as marine animals recovered.

63d53b0628fd.title: Starfish
63d53b0628fd.sentence: The fossil record for starfish is ancient, dating back to the Ordovician period around 450 million years ago, but it is rather sparse, as starfish tend to disintegrate after death.

a09ad8da986e.title: Chitinozoan
a09ad8da986e.sentence: Since Alfred Eisenack first recognised and named the group in 1930, the Chitinozoa have proven incredibly useful as a stratigraphic markers in biostratigraphy during the Ordovician, Silurian and Devonian periods.

7a4c018939bc.title: Trace fossil
7a4c018939bc.sentence: Trackways from the Ordovician Tumblagooda sandstone allow the behaviour of other terrestrial organisms to be determined.

9ab2cde82905.title: Vertebrate
9ab2cde82905.sentence: During the Ordovician, the armoured jawless "ostracoderms" rose to prominence, and remained the predominant groups of vertebrates until the Devonian.

4d7b426a6704.title: Geologic time scale
4d7b426a6704.sentence: Phanerozoic | Paleozoic | Ordovician | Upper/Late | Hirnantian | Most continents lay in equatorial regions. Gondwana stretched to south pole. Panthalassic Ocean covered northern hemisphere. Avalonia rifted from Gondwana closing Iapetus Ocean in front, opening Rheic Ocean behind. South China close to Gondwana; North China between Siberia and Gondwana. Orogenies: Famatinian (South America); Benambran (Australia); Taconic (Laurentia). Baltica and Siberia drift north. Early greenhouse climate, cooling to icehouse conditions during Hirnantian Ice Age. Increase in atmospheric O 2. Great Ordovician Biodiversification Event, major increase in new genera e.g. brachiopods, trilobites, corals, echinoderms, bryozoans, gastropods, bivalves, nautiloids, graptolites, and conodonts. Very high sea levels expand shallow continental seas, increase range of ecological niches. Modern marine ecosystems established. Earliest jawless fish. Tabulate corals and stromatoporoids dominant reef builders. Nautiloids main predators. Appearance of eurypterids and asteroids. Spread of early land plants. Late Ordovician mass extinction, loss of ~85 % of marine invertebrate species. Two pulses: first with onset of glaciation affects tropical fauna; second at end of ice age, warming climate impacts cool water species. Drastic reduction in trilobite, brachiopod, graptolite, echinoderm, conodont, coral, and chitinozoan genera. | 445.2 ± 0.9 *

f8a99c60fd5c.title: History of life
f8a99c60fd5c.sentence: Land plants evolved from green algae, with fossil evidence dating to the Ordovician period, about 470 million years ago.

4c346a88f011.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
4c346a88f011.sentence: The earliest radiations of the first land plants, also known as embryophytes, were bryophytes, which began to transform terrestrial environments and the global climate in the Ordovician.

6ad806e95e61.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
6ad806e95e61.sentence: Plants, which had been on land in forms similar to mosses and liverworts since the Ordovician, had just developed roots, seeds, and water transport systems that allowed them to survive away from places that were constantly wet—and so grew huge forests on the highlands.

b5a455e9250b.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
b5a455e9250b.sentence: Baltica was a particularly important cradle for early land plant evolution, with it having a diverse flora by the Darriwilian. ∆199Hg and ∆200Hg excursions reveal that land plants had already spread across much of the Earth's land surface by the Early Silurian.

9f5941819fdc.title: Paleozoic
9f5941819fdc.sentence: The increase in atmospheric oxygen between 470 Ma to 400 Ma is known as the Paleozoic Oxidation Event and is explained by the colonisation of land by the first plants (from about 470 Ma to 445 Ma) which trapped organic carbon within sedimentary rocks, reducing the oxygen sink.

50039b0a88d3.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
50039b0a88d3.sentence: Early non-vascular plants that began colonizing land during the Ordovician and early Silurian had limited bioengineering effects due to the lack of deep roots that could break up solid rocks into regolith and soil.

cfcf91eed1cb.title: Ice age
cfcf91eed1cb.sentence: The Andean-Saharan occurred from 460 to 420 million years ago, during the Late Ordovician and the Silurian period.

3cfc92aa34ba.title: History of Earth
3cfc92aa34ba.sentence: The timing of the first animals to leave the oceans is not precisely known: the oldest clear evidence is of arthropods on land around 450 Ma, perhaps thriving and becoming better adapted due to the vast food source provided by the terrestrial plants.

1f13cd4c6c22.title: Devonian
1f13cd4c6c22.sentence: The earliest land animals, predominantly arthropods such as myriapods, arachnids and hexapods, also became well-established early in this period, after beginning their colonization of land at least from the Ordovician Period.

c8870d54b0b7.title: History of life
c8870d54b0b7.sentence: Other trace fossils from the Late Ordovician a little over 445 Ma probably represent land invertebrates, and there is clear evidence of numerous arthropods on coasts and alluvial plains shortly before the Silurian-Devonian boundary, about 415 Ma, including signs that some arthropods ate plants.

78a29554c01b.title: History of Earth
78a29554c01b.section: Phanerozoic Eon > Tectonics, paleogeography and climate
78a29554c01b.sentence: Early Paleozoic climates were warmer than today, but the end of the Ordovician saw a short ice age during which glaciers covered the south pole, where the huge continent Gondwana was situated.

ad606ba34c25.title: Vertebrate
ad606ba34c25.sentence: The first jawed vertebrates (which emerged within the "ostracoderms") may have appeared in the late Ordovician (~445 mya) or Silurian, and became common in the Devonian period, often known as the "Age of Fishes".

50e314d68f40.title: History of life
50e314d68f40.section: Emergence of animals > Deuterostomes and the first vertebrates
50e314d68f40.sentence: Vertebrates with jaws, such as the acanthodians, first appeared in the Late Ordovician.

e9fcd4ddfb25.title: Silurian
e9fcd4ddfb25.sentence: The base of the Silurian is set at a series of major Ordovician–Silurian extinction events when up to 60% of marine genera were wiped out.

b87e8abcc806.title: Paleozoic
b87e8abcc806.sentence: Glaciation may have caused the Ordovician–Silurian extinction events, in which 60% of marine invertebrates and 25% of families became extinct, and is considered the first Phanerozoic mass extinction event, and the second deadliest.

970ad110a020.title: History of Earth
970ad110a020.section: Phanerozoic Eon > Tectonics, paleogeography and climate
970ad110a020.sentence: During the Late Ordovician ice age, a few mass extinctions took place, in which many brachiopods, trilobites, Bryozoa and corals disappeared.

24018eb47287.title: Devonian
24018eb47287.section: Paleogeography > Closure of the Rheic Ocean
24018eb47287.sentence: These continental blocks, collectively known as the Armorican Terrane Assemblage, split away from Gondwana in the Silurian and drifted towards Laurussia through the Devonian.

71af23912622.title: Silurian
71af23912622.sentence: Another significant evolutionary milestone during the Silurian was the diversification of jawed fish, which include placoderms, acanthodians (which gave rise to cartilaginous fish) and osteichthyan (bony fish, further divided into lobe-finned and ray-finned fishes), although this corresponded to sharp decline of jawless fish such as conodonts and ostracoderms.

f62f83dbe8ee.title: Paleozoic
f62f83dbe8ee.sentence: The first vertebrates appeared in the form of primitive fish, which greatly diversified in the Silurian and Devonian Periods.

d99485668de5.title: Cambrian explosion
d99485668de5.section: Uniqueness of the early Cambrian biodiversification
d99485668de5.sentence: Later radiations, such as those of fish in the Silurian and Devonian periods, involved fewer taxa, mainly with very similar body plans.

17ae2454aaec.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
17ae2454aaec.sentence: Nematophytes towered over even the largest land plants during the Silurian and Early Devonian, only being truly surpassed in size in the Early Carboniferous.

517831e5fbf6.title: Silurian
517831e5fbf6.sentence: The Silurian was the first period to see megafossils of extensive terrestrial biota in the form of moss-like miniature forests along lakes and streams and networks of large, mycorrhizal nematophytes, heralding the beginning of the Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution.

b511c79ac0a6.title: Silurian
b511c79ac0a6.sentence: The most abundant brachiopods were atrypids and pentamerides; atrypids were the first to recover and rediversify in the Rhuddanian after LOME, while pentameride recovery was delayed until the Aeronian.

9a7722c3ec3e.title: Silurian
9a7722c3ec3e.sentence: Trilobites started to recover in the Rhuddanian, and they continued to enjoy success in the Silurian as they had in the Ordovician despite their reduction in clade diversity as a result of LOME.

7c12b3fe179b.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
7c12b3fe179b.sentence: Palynological evidence points to Silurian terrestrial floras exhibiting little provincialism relative to present day floras that vary significantly by region, instead being broadly similar across the globe.

de239f871435.title: Silurian
de239f871435.sentence: Photosymbiotic scleractinians made their first appearance during the Middle Silurian.

da9b22a256a0.title: Silurian
da9b22a256a0.sentence: Hederelloids enjoyed significant success in the Silurian, with some developing symbioses with the colonial rugose coral Entelophyllum.

fa340f6d4a89.title: Silurian
fa340f6d4a89.sentence: During the Silurian, Gondwana continued a slow southward drift to high southern latitudes, but there is evidence that the Silurian icecaps were less extensive than those of the late-Ordovician glaciation.

5bc9053e2047.title: Silurian
5bc9053e2047.sentence: Early in the Silurian, glaciers retreated back into the South Pole until they almost disappeared in the middle of Silurian.

7aff0b04dcf4.title: Silurian
7aff0b04dcf4.sentence: The climate fluctuations are best explained by a sequence of glaciations, but the lack of tillites in the middle to late Silurian make this explanation problematic.

f04d8da006db.title: Vertebrate
f04d8da006db.sentence: The bony fishes appeared in the Silurian; they became common in the Devonian.

b872064cd5ea.title: Vertebrate
b872064cd5ea.sentence: Jawed vertebrates evolved in the Ordovician or Silurian; bony fishes appeared in the Silurian and diversified widely in the Devonian.

c2bea047949f.title: Silurian
c2bea047949f.sentence: The continents of Avalonia, Baltica, and Laurentia drifted together near the equator, starting the formation of a second supercontinent known as Euramerica.

30698babe425.title: Silurian
30698babe425.sentence: This event is the Caledonian orogeny, a spate of mountain building that stretched from New York State through conjoined Europe and Greenland to Norway.

bd209a0627cc.title: Silurian
bd209a0627cc.sentence: When the proto-Europe collided with North America, the collision folded coastal sediments that had been accumulating since the Cambrian off the east coast of North America and the west coast of Europe.

e1b2f3db2042.title: Silurian
e1b2f3db2042.sentence: Wenlock | Sheinwoodian | 433.4 | Sheinwood village, Much Wenlock and Wenlock Edge, Shropshire, England | During the Wenlock, the oldest-known tracheophytes of the genus Cooksonia, appear. The complexity of slightly later Gondwana plants like Baragwanathia, which resembled a modern clubmoss, indicates a much longer history for vascular plants, extending into the early Silurian or even Ordovician. The first terrestrial animals also appear in the Wenlock, represented by air-breathing millipedes from Scotland.

8856b8c092cf.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
8856b8c092cf.sentence: During the Wenlock epoch of the Silurian, the first fossils of vascular plants appear in the fossil record in the form of sporophytes of polysporangiophytes.

5f07c46ab681.title: Silurian
5f07c46ab681.sentence: Most of the sediments containing Cooksonia are marine in nature.

1326fe326165.title: Silurian
1326fe326165.sentence: Preferred habitats were likely along rivers and streams.

6c02cedb373c.title: Silurian
6c02cedb373c.sentence: The Ireviken event, Mulde event, and Lau event each represent isotopic excursions following a minor mass extinction and associated with rapid sea-level change.

6163d6c94799.title: Silurian
6163d6c94799.sentence: The climate and carbon cycle appear to be rather unsettled during the Silurian, which had a higher frequency of isotopic excursions (indicative of climate fluctuations) than any other period.

0ceec166a3d5.title: Paleozoic
0ceec166a3d5.sentence: Fall of CO2 levels (with O2 being freed up into the atmosphere and carbon being trapped in rocks) also caused climate cooling.

25457fd988f0.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
25457fd988f0.sentence: The Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution (SDTR), also known as the Devonian Plant Explosion (DePE) and the Devonian explosion, was a period of rapid colonization, diversification and radiation of land plants (particularly vascular plants) and fungi (especially dikaryans) on dry lands that occurred 428 to 359 million years ago (Mya) during the Silurian and Devonian periods, with the most critical phase occurring during the Late Silurian and Early Devonian.

cbb04feee04f.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
cbb04feee04f.section: Probable causes > Anoxia > Weathering aided by land plants
cbb04feee04f.sentence: During the Late Silurian and Devonian, land plants, assisted by fungi, underwent a hugely significant phase of evolution known as the Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution.

d3a635c30497.title: Devonian
d3a635c30497.sentence: This rapid evolution and colonization process, which had begun during the Silurian, is known as the Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution.

bf2c94de774a.title: Silurian
bf2c94de774a.sentence: One important event in this period was the initial establishment of terrestrial life in what is known as the Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution: vascular plants emerged from more primitive land plants, dikaryan fungi started expanding and diversifying along with glomeromycotan fungi, and three groups of arthropods (myriapods, arachnids and hexapods) became fully terrestrialized.

a280faeb3f38.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
a280faeb3f38.sentence: Through fierce competition for sunlight, soil nutrients and available land space, phenotypic diversity of plants increased greatly during the Silurian and Devonian periods, comparable in scale and effect to the explosion in diversity of animal life during the Cambrian explosion, especially in vertical growth of lignified vascular plants, which allowed for expansive canopies to develop, and forever altering the plant evolutions that followed.

3f10cff58d5f.title: Devonian
3f10cff58d5f.section: Life > Terrestrial biota > The greening of land
3f10cff58d5f.sentence: This rapid appearance of many plant groups and growth forms has been referred to as the Devonian Explosion or the Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution.

83e3667ec9ce.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
83e3667ec9ce.sentence: Plant diversification in the Silurian was aided by the presence of numerous small, rapidly changing volcanic islands in the Rheic Ocean that acted as natural laboratories accelerating evolutionary changes and enabling distinct, endemic floral lineages to arise.

3968d844a4f3.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
3968d844a4f3.sentence: The floral activities following the Silurian-Devonian plant revolution also exerted significant influences on changes in the water cycle and global climate, as well as driving the biosphere by creating diverse layers of vegetations that provide both sustenance and refuge for both upland and wetland habitats, paving the way for all terrestrial and aquatic biomes that would follow.

e79ae4d8bacd.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
e79ae4d8bacd.sentence: The Devonian Plant Explosion had global consequences on oceanic nutrient content and sediment cycling, which likely had led to harmful plankton blooms and consequently the Late Devonian extinction of the freshwater and marine ecosystems.

788f292d6c39.title: Cambrian explosion
788f292d6c39.sentence: The Devonian colonization of land had planet-wide consequences for sediment cycling and ocean nutrients, and was likely linked to the Devonian mass extinction.

1ceca616ae5a.title: Extinction event
1ceca616ae5a.section: Causes > Most widely supported explanations > Anoxic events
1ceca616ae5a.sentence: It has been suggested that anoxic events caused or contributed to the Ordovician–Silurian, late Devonian, Capitanian, Permian–Triassic, and Triassic–Jurassic extinctions, as well as a number of lesser extinctions (such as the Ireviken, Lundgreni, Mulde, Lau, Smithian-Spathian, Toarcian, and Cenomanian–Turonian events).

b56c1975df47.title: Lycophyte
b56c1975df47.sentence: They are one of the oldest lineages of extant (living) vascular plants; the group contains extinct plants that have been dated from the Silurian (ca. 425 million years ago).

58342a91012f.title: Silurian
58342a91012f.sentence: Baragwanathia appears to be almost as old, dating to the Přídolí (420 Ma) and has branching stems and needle-like leaves of 10–20 centimetres (3.9–7.9 in).

3ffc2413bf20.title: Silurian
3ffc2413bf20.sentence: The plant shows a high degree of development in relation to the age of its fossil remains.

9a4967e939b9.title: Silurian
9a4967e939b9.sentence: Fossils of this plant have been recorded in Australia, Canada, and China.

eba6ce6bf159.sentence: Middle Silurian rocks from 430 Ma contain fossils of true plants, including clubmosses such as Baragwanathia; most were under 10 centimetres (3.9 in) high, and some appear closely related to vascular plants, the group that includes trees.

d67b17206e6b.title: Silurian
d67b17206e6b.sentence: The definitive oldest record of millipede ever known is Kampecaris obanensis and Archidesmus sp. from the late Silurian (425 Ma) of Kerrera.

7c5cdd519c65.title: Millipede

d8c84f3d839a.title: Millipede
d8c84f3d839a.sentence: First appearing in the Silurian period, millipedes are some of the oldest known land animals.

ec782e83949e.title: Millipede
ec782e83949e.sentence: Millipedes are among the first animals to have colonised land during the Silurian period.

7a02dddd95d2.title: Silurian
7a02dddd95d2.sentence: However, the land fauna did not have a major impact on the Earth until it diversified in the Devonian.

13341e370761.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
13341e370761.sentence: The later glaciation during the middle Ludfordian, corresponding to the Lau event, led to a major marine regression, creating significant areas of new dry land habitat that were colonised by plants, along with cyanobacterial mats.

d3991eb139cb.title: History of life
d3991eb139cb.section: Colonization of land > Evolution of soil
d3991eb139cb.sentence: The earliest known ascomycete fossils date from 423 to 419 Ma in the Silurian.

8868086feb67.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
8868086feb67.section: Environmental impact > Effects on atmosphere and climate
8868086feb67.sentence: With increased atmospheric oxygenation also came increased spontaneous wildfires, and the Earth's atmosphere first became sufficiently high in oxygen to produce wildfires during the Pridoli, when the first charcoal evidence of wildfires is recorded.

9324b1db5ec1.title: Paleozoic
9324b1db5ec1.sentence: This also marks the first time fire could be supported by Earth's atmosphere (as evidenced by charcoal deposits from the Silurian Period) with O2 levels crossing the 15% mark.

947dcbabafff.title: Millipede
947dcbabafff.sentence: Pneumodesmus newmani was once argued to be the earliest member of the millipedes from the late Wenlock epoch of the late Silurian around 428 million years ago, but recent studies indicate that the dating method was erroneous, and that the taxon most likely originated during the Pridoli Epoch of the late Silurian or the Lochkovian of the early Devonian.

54b8d9c17a11.title: Silurian
54b8d9c17a11.sentence: There are also other millipedes, centipedes, and trigonotarbid arachnoids known from Přídolí (420 Ma).

5310cc7b2ed9.title: Silurian
5310cc7b2ed9.sentence: Predatory invertebrates would indicate that simple food webs were in place that included non-predatory prey animals.

5c46ddf67004.title: Silurian
5c46ddf67004.sentence: At the end of the Silurian, sea levels dropped again, leaving telltale basins of evaporites extending from Michigan to West Virginia, and the new mountain ranges were rapidly eroded.

68688b16cd48.title: Silurian
68688b16cd48.sentence: Sea levels rose from their Hirnantian low throughout the first half of the Silurian; they subsequently fell throughout the rest of the period, although smaller scale patterns are superimposed on this general trend; fifteen high-stands (periods when sea levels were above the edge of the continental shelf) can be identified, and the highest Silurian sea level was probably around 140 metres (459 ft) higher than the lowest level reached.

33f24c1abf1c.title: Devonian
33f24c1abf1c.sentence: The great diversity of fish around at the time has led to the Devonian being given the name "The Age of Fishes" in popular culture.

10a9c58227ab.title: Devonian
10a9c58227ab.sentence: Early cartilaginous (Chondrichthyes) and bony fishes (Osteichthyes) also become diverse and played a large role within the Devonian seas.

b206ee0769b8.title: Hangenberg event
b206ee0769b8.sentence: If the Hangenberg event was influenced by volcanic activity, the Kola and Timan-Pechora magmatic provinces of northwest Russia are potential candidates for massive volcanism at the end of the Devonian.

3d7739789ac3.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
3d7739789ac3.sentence: The Viluy and Pripyat-Dnieper-Donets large igneous provinces were suggested to correlate with the Frasnian / Famennian extinction, with the Kola and Timan-Pechora magmatic provinces being suggested to be related to the Hangenberg event at the Devonian-Carboniferous boundary.

20c43fff0d49.title: Devonian
20c43fff0d49.sentence: CO2 levels dropped steeply throughout the Devonian Period.

69fd80f71a04.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
69fd80f71a04.sentence: The revolutionary spread of land plants during the Devonian corresponds to a long-term drop in CO2 levels in the atmosphere.

1e78b2e96316.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
1e78b2e96316.sentence: Expansion of terrestrial Devonian flora modified soil properties, increasing silicate weathering by way of rhizosphere development as evidenced by pedogenic carbonates.

89d49d8b1dca.title: Ice age
89d49d8b1dca.sentence: The evolution of land plants at the onset of the Devonian period caused a long term increase in planetary oxygen levels and reduction of CO2 levels, which resulted in the late Paleozoic icehouse.

e52a4ca8563e.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
e52a4ca8563e.section: Environmental impact > Effects on atmosphere and climate
e52a4ca8563e.sentence: Atmospheric O2 concentration oscillated between about 2% and 11% atm during the Cambrian to mid-Ordovician and around 13% atm during early Silurian, but rose to near modern-day levels (1 atm, about 21% mole fraction) in the Devonian and subsequently to a peak of over 1.6 atm (around 35% mole fraction) during the late Carboniferous and most of the Permian periods.

1467030b795e.title: Vertebrate
1467030b795e.sentence: Reaching a high point of diversity during the Early Devonian, "ostracoderms" subsequently declined, becoming extinct by the end of the period.

663b1632d3c5.title: Carboniferous
663b1632d3c5.sentence: South China and Annamia (Southeast Asia) rifted from Gondwana during the Devonian.

bcd96e974101.title: Devonian
bcd96e974101.sentence: Nevertheless, they remained close enough to Gondwana that their Devonian fossils were more closely related to Australian species than to north Asian species.

7c673bb86346.title: Devonian
7c673bb86346.section: Paleogeography > Closure of the Rheic Ocean
7c673bb86346.sentence: The Rheic Ocean, which separated Laurussia from Gondwana, was wide at the start of the Devonian, having formed after the drift of Avalonia away from Gondwana.

e11327559407.title: Devonian
e11327559407.section: Paleogeography > Closure of the Rheic Ocean
e11327559407.sentence: Franconia and Saxothuringia collided with Laurussia near the end of the Early Devonian, pinching out the easternmost Rheic Ocean.

a4bf183c908f.title: Devonian
a4bf183c908f.section: Paleogeography > Closure of the Rheic Ocean
a4bf183c908f.sentence: The closure of the Rheic Ocean began in the Devonian and continued into the Carboniferous.

ec3a1855814c.title: Devonian
ec3a1855814c.sentence: The moss forests and bacterial and algal mats of the Silurian were joined early in the period by primitive rooted plants that created the first stable soils and harbored arthropods like mites, scorpions, trigonotarbids and myriapods (although arthropods appeared on land much earlier than in the Early Devonian and the existence of fossils such as Protichnites suggest that amphibious arthropods may have appeared as early as the Cambrian).

bf7fccf31401.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
bf7fccf31401.sentence: Basal members of Euphyllophytina, the clade that includes trimerophytes, ferns, progymnosperms, and seed plants, are known from Early Devonian fossils.

8a63ff1be461.title: Devonian
8a63ff1be461.sentence: Bactritoids make their first appearance in the Early Devonian as well; their radiation, along with that of ammonoids, has been attributed by some authors to increased environmental stress resulting from decreasing oxygen levels in the deeper parts of the water column.

0508d1c7d0b6.title: History of life
0508d1c7d0b6.sentence: The earliest fossils of insects have been found in Early Devonian rocks from about 400 Ma, which preserve only a few varieties of flightless insect.

270872931c38.title: Devonian
270872931c38.sentence: Also, the first possible fossils of insects appeared around 416 Ma, in the Early Devonian.

78df32054e55.title: Devonian
78df32054e55.sentence: By the early Devonian, the continent Laurussia (also known as Euramerica) was fully formed through the collision of the continents Laurentia (modern day North America) and Baltica (modern day northern and eastern Europe).

a06d5c9f461e.title: Carboniferous
a06d5c9f461e.sentence: The Laurussian continent was formed by the collision between Laurentia, Baltica and Avalonia during the Devonian.

cc1d47d8b6eb.title: Devonian
cc1d47d8b6eb.sentence: Most of Laurussia was located south of the equator, but in the Devonian it moved northwards and began to rotate counterclockwise towards its modern position.

326d527a39fc.title: Devonian
326d527a39fc.sentence: The tectonic effects of this collision continued into the Devonian, producing a string of mountain ranges along the southeastern coast of the continent.

2a73a16c25fe.title: Devonian

2a73a16c25fe.sentence: In Eifelian age, cladoxylopsid trees formed the first forests in Earth history.

d71f40b85d99.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
d71f40b85d99.sentence: The first true forest environments featuring trees exceeding eight metres in height emerged by the Middle Devonian, with the earliest known fossil forest dating to the Eifelian.

ecb8d57270a6.title: Devonian
ecb8d57270a6.section: Life > Terrestrial biota > The greening of land
ecb8d57270a6.sentence: The earliest-known trees appeared in the Middle Devonian.

1e27559f1378.sentence: By the Middle Devonian, shrub-like forests of primitive plants existed: lycophytes, horsetails, ferns, and progymnosperms evolved.

acdd96c63ad6.title: Late Devonian mass extinction

fb27edbf13c7.title: Devonian

375e204027b9.title: Devonian
375e204027b9.sentence: A now-dry barrier reef, located in present-day Kimberley Basin of northwest Australia, once extended 350 km (220 mi), fringing a Devonian continent.

cf0181542dc9.title: Devonian
cf0181542dc9.sentence: Devonian reefs also extended along the southeast edge of Laurussia, a coastline now corresponding to southern England, Belgium, and other mid-latitude areas of Europe.

080b4a6d76da.title: Devonian
080b4a6d76da.sentence: The climate would have affected the dominant organisms in reefs; microbes would have been the main reef-forming organisms in warm periods, with corals and stromatoporoid sponges taking the dominant role in cooler times.

7fa84b7e47ac.title: Devonian
7fa84b7e47ac.sentence: The newly evolved forests drew carbon out of the atmosphere, which were then buried into sediments.

4a3bef59c485.title: Devonian
4a3bef59c485.sentence: This may be reflected by a Mid-Devonian cooling of around 5 °C (9 °F).

974d7218b919.sentence: The rest of the Armorican terranes followed, and by the end of the Devonian they were fully connected with Laurussia.

0ade26bbd6ab.title: Tetrapod
0ade26bbd6ab.sentence: The oldest evidence for the existence of tetrapods comes from trace fossils: tracks (footprints) and trackways found in Zachełmie, Poland, dated to the Eifelian stage of the Middle Devonian, 390 million years ago, although these traces have also been interpreted as the ichnogenus Piscichnus (fish nests/feeding traces).

80477b56e63c.sentence: Evidence for the earliest tetrapods takes the form of trace fossils in shallow lagoon environments within a marine carbonate platform/shelf during the Middle Devonian, although these traces have been questioned and an interpretation as fish feeding traces (Piscichnus) has been advanced.

f0821b4c8c30.title: Tetrapod
f0821b4c8c30.sentence: The second oldest evidence for tetrapods, also tracks and trackways, date from ca. 385 Mya (Valentia Island, Ireland).

c8e07438437e.title: History of life
c8e07438437e.sentence: Although the earliest good evidence of land plants and animals dates back to the Ordovician period (488 to 444 Ma), and a number of microorganism lineages made it onto land much earlier, modern land ecosystems only appeared in the Late Devonian, about 385 to 359 Ma.

8659a6f0ab2e.title: Carboniferous

61cfb64a8b28.title: Devonian
61cfb64a8b28.sentence: The Late Devonian warmed to levels equivalent to the Early Devonian; while there is no corresponding increase in CO2 concentrations, continental weathering increases (as predicted by warmer temperatures); further, a range of evidence, such as plant distribution, points to a Late Devonian warming.

dd9c5309f87e.title: Devonian
dd9c5309f87e.sentence: In the Late Devonian, by contrast, arid conditions were less prevalent across the world and temperate climates were more common.

8946b9c78bb0.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
8946b9c78bb0.sentence: The extinction event was accompanied by widespread oceanic anoxia; that is, a lack of oxygen, prohibiting decay and allowing the preservation of organic matter.

df4461ac6e57.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
df4461ac6e57.sentence: This, combined with the ability of porous reef rocks to hold oil, has led to Devonian rocks being an important source of oil, especially in Canada and the United States.

a71fe10cb58a.title: Hangenberg event
a71fe10cb58a.sentence: Chemical analysis of cores in the Bakken Shale suggest that while it was being formed, successive eras of higher sea level corresponded with euxinic (high in toxic hydrogen sulfide and low in oxygen) water in the shallow ocean basin, which could kill animals in the ocean and near the shoreline.

c5af3ff73907.title: Devonian
c5af3ff73907.sentence: Although Siberia's margins were generally tectonically stable and ecologically productive, rifting and deep mantle plumes impacted the continent with flood basalts during the Late Devonian.

ba0f4ab565f9.title: Devonian

889b6ec4609c.title: Late Devonian mass extinction

af9d55b26a1c.sentence: The Acadian orogeny was caused by a series of collisions of pieces of crust from the Avalonia Terrane, sections broken off from continent of Gondwana, with the North American Plate.

3a50dbe74066.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
3a50dbe74066.sentence: The Late Devonian mass extinction, also known as the Kellwasser event, was a mass extinction event which occurred around 372.15 million years ago, at the boundary between the Frasnian and Famennian ages of the Late Devonian period.

eb97b4fde349.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
eb97b4fde349.sentence: The Kellwasser event, named for its type locality, the Kellwassertal in Lower Saxony, Germany, is the term given to the extinction pulse that occurred near the Frasnian–Famennian boundary (372.2 ± 1.6 Ma).

587c502a3615.title: Extinction event
587c502a3615.section: The "Big Five" mass extinction events > Late Devonian mass extinction, 372 Ma
587c502a3615.sentence: The larger of the two was the Kellwasser Event at the Frasnian-Famennian boundary (F-F, 372 Ma), about midway through the Late Devonian.

12ae62c512ec.title: Hangenberg event
12ae62c512ec.sentence: However, late Famennian extinction rates were typically considered to be of lesser taxonomic severity than those in the Kellwasser Event, one of the "big five" mass extinctions.

01d57efa896d.title: Devonian
01d57efa896d.sentence: The Late Devonian extinction is not a single event, but rather is a series of pulsed extinctions at the Givetian-Frasnian boundary, the Frasnian-Famennian boundary, and the Devonian-Carboniferous boundary.

ddfc2201fef0.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
ddfc2201fef0.sentence: Although it is well established that there was a massive loss of biodiversity in the Late Devonian, the timespan of this event is uncertain, with estimates ranging from 500,000 to 25 million years, extending from the mid-Givetian to the end-Famennian.

4ed70d159322.title: Paleozoic
4ed70d159322.sentence: Earth's second Phanerozoic mass extinction event (a group of several smaller extinction events), the Late Devonian extinction, ended 70% of existing species.

bcf1ecb31ebb.title: Devonian
bcf1ecb31ebb.sentence: The Devonian extinction crisis primarily affected the marine community, and selectively affected shallow warm-water organisms rather than cool-water organisms.

62beb63aed80.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
62beb63aed80.sentence: The most hard-hit biological category affected by the Kellwasser event were the calcite-based reef-builders of the great Devonian reef-systems, including the stromatoporoid sponges and the rugose and tabulate corals.

e25f1f3a1031.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
e25f1f3a1031.sentence: Most lingering agnathan (jawless fish) groups, such as osteostracans, galeaspids, and heterostracans, also went extinct by the end of the Frasnian.

bdde589a697f.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
bdde589a697f.sentence: This left only two trilobites orders in the Famennian: Phacopida and Proetida.

9e592f2a7105.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
9e592f2a7105.sentence: There is good evidence for high-frequency sea-level changes around the Frasnian–Famennian Kellwasser event, with one transgression (sea-level rise) associated with the onset of anoxic deposits; marine transgressions likely helped spread deoxygenated waters onto the continental shelf.

f05f7656a45e.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
f05f7656a45e.sentence: A positive δ18O excursion is observed across the Frasnian-Famennian boundary in brachiopods from North America, Germany, Spain, Morocco, Siberia, and China; conodont apatite δ18O excursions also occurred at this time.

174f293a4cc4.title: History of life
174f293a4cc4.sentence: The subsequent spread of plants may have contributed to the Late Devonian extinction event: early trees such as Archaeopteris drew down atmospheric CO2, contributing to global cooling and lower sea levels, while their roots increased rock weathering and nutrient runoff, potentially triggering algal blooms and anoxic events.

b1737c43f51f.sentence: The first vertebrates with limbs and digits evolved in the Devonian, including the Late Devonian-age Ichthyostega and Acanthostega, as well as the trackmakers of the Middle Devonian-age Zachelmie trackways.

556751ccd6f9.title: History of life
556751ccd6f9.sentence: However, in 1987, nearly complete fossils of Acanthostega from about 363 Ma showed that this Late Devonian transitional animal had legs and both lungs and gills, but could never have survived on land: its limbs and its wrist and ankle joints were too weak to bear its weight; its ribs were too short to prevent its lungs from being squeezed flat by its weight; its fish-like tail fin would have been damaged by dragging on the ground.

77aac3aa53b4.title: Vertebrate
77aac3aa53b4.sentence: The fins, already possessing bones and joints, evolved into the two pairs of walking legs of the first tetrapods in the Famennian stage of the Devonian.

6adef16a15cc.title: Tetrapod
6adef16a15cc.sentence: The publication in 2018 of Tutusius umlambo and Umzantsia amazana from high latitude Gondwana setting indicate that the tetrapods enjoyed a global distribution by the end of the Devonian and even extended into the high latitudes.

48349523d267.title: Tetrapod
48349523d267.sentence: The oldest fossils of four-limbed vertebrates (tetrapods in the broad sense of the word) are trackways from the Middle Devonian, and body fossils became common near the end of the Late Devonian, around 370–360 million years ago.

26a9d9b4df02.title: Tetrapod
26a9d9b4df02.sentence: The Devonian stem-tetrapods went through two major population bottlenecks during the Late Devonian extinctions, also known as the end-Frasnian and end-Fammenian extinctions.

3e7ee7fa9abb.title: Permian
3e7ee7fa9abb.sentence: At the start of the Permian, the Earth was still in the Late Paleozoic icehouse (LPIA), which began in the latest Devonian and spanned the entire Carboniferous period, with its most intense phase occurring during the latter part of the Pennsylvanian epoch.

dee444b6b0f6.title: Carboniferous
dee444b6b0f6.sentence: Temperatures began to drop during the late Devonian with a short-lived glaciation in the late Famennian through Devonian–Carboniferous boundary, before the Early Tournaisian Warm Interval.

5f1f962ff71c.title: Hangenberg event
5f1f962ff71c.sentence: Evidence such as glacial deposits in northern Brazil (near the Devonian South Pole) suggests widespread glaciation at the end of the Devonian, as a broad continental mass covered the polar region.

938df0befc3c.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
938df0befc3c.sentence: The continued drawdown of organic carbon eventually pulled the Earth out of its greenhouse state during the Famennian into the icehouse that continued throughout the Carboniferous and Permian.

66d927eff263.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
66d927eff263.sentence: The biological sequestration of carbon dioxide may have ultimately led to the beginning of the Late Palaeozoic Ice Age during the Famennian, which has been suggested as a cause of the Hangenberg event.

f73f6d9e3275.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
f73f6d9e3275.section: Environmental impact > Effects on atmosphere and climate
f73f6d9e3275.sentence: The biological sequestration of so much atmospheric carbon dioxide resulted in the beginning of the Late Paleozoic icehouse at the end of the Devonian, together with the tectonic uplift of the continent Gondwana.

e33424bb9c92.title: Impact event
e33424bb9c92.section: Impacts and the Earth > Earth impacts in history > Paleozoic and Mesozoic
e33424bb9c92.sentence: Two 10-kilometre sized (6.2 mi) asteroids may have struck Australia between 360 and 300 million years ago at the West Warburton and East Warburton Basins, creating a 400-kilometre impact zone (250 mi).

712f0027f5d0.title: Devonian
712f0027f5d0.sentence: The subsequent end-Devonian extinction, which occurred at around 359 Ma, further impacted the ecosystems and completed the extinction of all calcite sponge reefs and placoderms.

74b823dc1709.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
74b823dc1709.sentence: More diverse placoderm families survived the event only to succumb in the Hangenberg event at the end of the Devonian.

a81c290419df.title: Hangenberg event
a81c290419df.sentence: Placoderm diversity had already decreased in the Kellwasser Event, and all remaining subgroups (arthrodires, antiarchs, phyllolepids, and ptychodontids) died out abruptly at the end of the Devonian.

2128d1e3e75e.title: Carboniferous
2128d1e3e75e.sentence: It is believed that this evolutionary radiation occurred because the decline of the placoderms at the end of the Devonian caused many environmental niches to become unoccupied and allowed new organisms to evolve and fill these niches.

6c1595d2c950.title: Hangenberg event
6c1595d2c950.sentence: The Hangenberg event, also known as the Hangenberg crisis or end-Devonian extinction, is a mass extinction that occurred at the end of the Famennian, the last stage in the Devonian Period (roughly 358.9 ± 0.4 million years ago).

9c4c801a99c3.title: Hangenberg event
9c4c801a99c3.section: Geological evidence > Prelude and extinction – the lower crisis interval
9c4c801a99c3.sentence: Uranium-Lead dating of ash beds in Poland provide dates of 358.97 ± 0.11 Ma and 358.89 ± 0.20 Ma below and above the black shale.

78ccf0a5e7fe.title: Hangenberg event
78ccf0a5e7fe.sentence: The event is named after the Hangenberg Shale, which is part of a sequence that straddles the Devonian-Carboniferous boundary in the Rhenish Massif of Germany.

c9cce2f6dc33.title: Hangenberg event
c9cce2f6dc33.sentence: The last true stromatoporoid sponges, a major group of Devonian reef builders, completely died out in the Hangenberg Event.

2a138ae84faf.title: Hangenberg event
2a138ae84faf.sentence: The Hangenberg event has been associated with sea-level rise followed swiftly by glaciation-related sea-level fall, and thus a cause of the extinctions may have been an episode of severe global cooling and glaciation at the end of the Famennian, marking the dawn of the Late Palaeozoic Ice Age.

486a8e9069a7.title: Hangenberg event
486a8e9069a7.sentence: One hypothesis for the cause of the last pulse of the extinction notes the abundance of malformed plant spores at the Devonian–Carboniferous boundary.

a095d192cf34.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
a095d192cf34.sentence: A recent explanation suggests that a nearby supernova explosion was the cause for the specific Hangenberg event, which marks the boundary between the Devonian and Carboniferous periods.

190b4cdd5683.title: Hangenberg event
190b4cdd5683.sentence: This estimate would rank the end-Famennian extinction as the fourth-deadliest mass extinction, ahead of the end-Frasnian extinction.

ccc76060b274.title: Extinction event
ccc76060b274.sentence: Some mass extinctions (such as the end-Permian) were equally catastrophic for plants, whereas others, such as the end-Devonian, did not affect the flora.

6285e9fb5ef5.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
6285e9fb5ef5.sentence: A second mass extinction called the Hangenberg event, also known as the end-Devonian extinction, occurred 13 million years later around 358.86 million years ago, bringing an end to the Famennian and Devonian, as the world transitioned into the Carboniferous Period.

93ed66f29d44.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
93ed66f29d44.sentence: The jawless thelodonts only barely survived, succumbing early in the Famennian.

6109da553307.title: Chitinozoan
6109da553307.sentence: Chitinozoans appear to have become extinct at the end of the Devonian; rare Carboniferous and Permian remains may represent reworked fossils or fungal spores.

95ab6c1a7dfe.title: Hangenberg event
95ab6c1a7dfe.sentence: For the end-Famennian, these were chitinozoans within the pelagic filter-feeder megaguild, and stromatoporoids within the attached epifaunal (seabed-living) filter-feeder megaguild.

e79a3c1c376d.title: Carboniferous
e79a3c1c376d.sentence: Subduction along the Kazakhstanian margin of the Turkestan Ocean resulted in collision between northern Tarim and Kazakhstania during the mid Carboniferous as the ocean closed.

2050b11f6d1f.title: Carboniferous
2050b11f6d1f.sentence: As Kazakhstania had already accreted to Laurussia, Siberia was effectively part of Pangea by 310 Ma, although major strike-slip movements continued between it and Laurussia into the Permian.

5fb66d320558.title: Carboniferous
5fb66d320558.sentence: The GSSP for the base of the Carboniferous System, Mississippian Subsystem and Tournaisian Stage is located at the La Serre section in Montagne Noire, southern France.

c9cf12baeede.title: Carboniferous
c9cf12baeede.sentence: It is defined by the first appearance of the conodont Siphonodella sulcata within the evolutionary lineage from Siphonodella praesulcata to Siphonodella sulcata.

63fedd625c4c.title: Carboniferous
63fedd625c4c.sentence: However, in 2006 further study revealed the presence of Siphonodella sulcata below the boundary, and the presence of Siphonodella praesulcata and Siphonodella sulcata together above a local unconformity.

243b5f7232e8.title: Carboniferous
243b5f7232e8.sentence: The Carboniferous (/ˌkɑːrbəˈnɪfərəs/ KAR-bə-NIF-ər-əs) is a geologic period and system of the Paleozoic era that spans 60 million years, from the end of the Devonian Period 358.86 Ma (million years ago) to the beginning of the Permian Period, 298.9 Ma.

45e00ee99993.title: Tetrapod
45e00ee99993.sentence: By the very beginning of the Carboniferous, the stem-tetrapods had radiated into two branches of true ("crown group") tetrapods, one ancestral to modern amphibians and the other ancestral to amniotes.

88350041495d.title: Tetrapod
88350041495d.sentence: The first crown-tetrapods (those descended from the last common ancestors of extant tetrapods) appeared by the Tournaisian age of the Early Carboniferous.

9cc01ea82432.title: Tetrapod
9cc01ea82432.sentence: During the early Carboniferous, the number of digits on hands and feet of stem-tetrapods became standardized at no more than five, as lineages with more digits died out (exceptions within crown-group tetrapods arose among some secondarily aquatic members).

9495f393814c.title: Carboniferous
9495f393814c.sentence: Stegocephalia (four-limbed vertebrates including true tetrapods), whose forerunners (tetrapodomorphs) had evolved from lobe-finned fish during the preceding Devonian period, became pentadactylous during the Carboniferous.

c7ed12f5fe74.title: Carboniferous
c7ed12f5fe74.sentence: The gap saw the demise of the Devonian fish-like ichthyostegalian labyrinthodonts and the rise of the more advanced temnospondylian and reptiliomorphan amphibians that so typify the Carboniferous terrestrial vertebrate fauna.

591c6b862466.title: Carboniferous
591c6b862466.sentence: The similarity in successions between the British Isles and Western Europe led to the development of a common European timescale with the Carboniferous System divided into the lower Dinantian, dominated by carbonate deposition and the upper Silesian with mainly siliciclastic deposition.

40181438748a.title: Carboniferous
40181438748a.sentence: The Dinantian was divided into the Tournaisian and Viséan stages.

cfaa1a7b7f91.title: Carboniferous
cfaa1a7b7f91.sentence: Crinoids were highly numerous during the Carboniferous, though they suffered a gradual decline in diversity during the Middle Mississippian.

8c814e28b3a1.title: Carboniferous
8c814e28b3a1.sentence: The Cladoxylopsids were large trees, that were ancestors of ferns, first arising in the Carboniferous.

e3123f0fea10.title: Hangenberg event
e3123f0fea10.sentence: Among the most major ecological changes associated with the extinction are the rise of chondrichthyans (sharks and kin) and actinopterygians (ray-finned fish), which took over in diversity and relative abundance during the Early Carboniferous.

28c57ce39c9e.title: Hangenberg event
28c57ce39c9e.sentence: Even so, few Devonian chondrichthyan and actinopterygian species survived into the Carboniferous, indicating that these groups also experienced extinctions.

d55d274a791a.title: Carboniferous
d55d274a791a.sentence: Chondrichthyes (especially holocephalans like the Stethacanthids) underwent a major evolutionary radiation during the Carboniferous.

964315035d85.title: Carboniferous
964315035d85.sentence: The first members of the helicoprionidae, a family eugeneodonts that were characterized by the presence of one circular tooth whorl in the lower jaw, appeared during the early Carboniferous.

69d0688fe5ca.title: Carboniferous
69d0688fe5ca.sentence: At the extremes, during the Permo-Carboniferous Glacial Maximum (299–293 Ma) the global average temperature (GAT) was c. 13 °C (55 °F), the average temperature in the tropics c. 24 °C (75 °F) and in polar regions c. -23 °C (-10 °F), whilst during the Early Tournaisian Warm Interval (358–353 Ma) the GAT was c. 22 °C (72 °F), the tropics c. 30 °C (86 °F) and polar regions c. 1.5 °C (35 °F).

a0db1d614ed0.title: Hangenberg event
a0db1d614ed0.section: Geological evidence > Glaciation – the middle crisis interval
a0db1d614ed0.sentence: The Late Famennian glacial phase, along with other short glacial phases in the Tournaisian and Visean, acted as a prelude to the far larger and more prolonged Late Paleozoic Ice Age which stretched across much of the Late Carboniferous and Early Permian.

40d702a1bf73.title: Carboniferous
40d702a1bf73.sentence: The period is sometimes called the Age of Amphibians because of the diversification of early amphibians such as the temnospondyls, which became dominant land vertebrates, as well as the first appearance of amniotes including synapsids (the clade to which modern mammals belong) and sauropsids (which include modern reptiles and birds) during the late Carboniferous.

e8a72502dc16.title: Geologic time scale
e8a72502dc16.sentence: Phanerozoic | Paleozoic | Carboniferous | Pennsylvanian | Gzhelian | Continuation of the Variscan orogeny (Ouachita and Alleghanian orogenies) with growth of the Central Pangean Mountains. Ural orogeny continues with continental collision between Kazakhstania and Laurussia. Humid, coal swamps form in foreland basins of the Central Pangean Mountains and around North and South China cratons. As the Late Paleozoic icehouse (LPIA) continues, waxing and waning of ice sheets causes rapid changes in global sea level, flooding these regions and depositing cyclothem sequences. Atmospheric oxygen levels rise to over 25% before decreasing again. Appearance of aragonite reef builders, including algae and sponges. Freshwater Eurypterids (sea scorpions). On land, Neoptera appear, and Miomoptera show earliest evidence for complete metamorphosis. First true terrestrial amphibians. Amniotes appear and split into two groups: sauropsids (reptiles) and synapsids (mammals). Lepidodendron and Sigillaria lycopod trees dominate coal swamps, with smaller sphenopsids (horsetails) and seed ferns between. Gymnosperms, including conifers and cycads grow on drier ground. LPIA peaks at Carboniferous-Permian boundary. A drop in CO 2 levels and increase in arid conditions leads to change in woodland vegetation (Carboniferous rainforest collapse). | 303.7

7ddaf90a6bbe.title: Carboniferous
7ddaf90a6bbe.section: Geochemistry > Magnesium/calcium isotope ratios in seawater
7ddaf90a6bbe.sentence: During the early Carboniferous, the Mg2+/Ca2+ ratio in seawater began to rise and by the Middle Mississippian aragonite seas had replaced calcite seas.

e9ce3e22310e.title: Carboniferous
e9ce3e22310e.sentence: In the mid-Mississippian the oldest known winged insects appears, followed by the huge predatory Protodonata (griffinflies), which includes Meganeura, a giant dragonfly-like insect and with a wingspan of ca. 75 cm (30 in)—the largest flying insect ever to roam the planet.

e870c34317b6.title: Permian
e870c34317b6.sentence: Palaeodictyopteroidea, which had represented the dominant group of insects during the Carboniferous, declined during the Permian.

8bf46c425be8.title: Carboniferous
8bf46c425be8.sentence: Further groups are the Syntonopterodea (relatives of present-day mayflies), the abundant and often large sap-sucking Palaeodictyopteroidea, the diverse herbivorous Protorthoptera, and numerous basal Dictyoptera (ancestors of cockroaches).

d983fdca0041.title: Carboniferous
d983fdca0041.sentence: During the Visean Warm Interval glaciers nearly vanished retreating to the proto-Andes in Bolivia and western Argentina and the Pan-African mountain ranges in southeastern Brazil and southwest Africa.

a1e1a98cf8d2.title: Carboniferous
a1e1a98cf8d2.sentence: This evolutionary radiation was known as the Carboniferous-Earliest Permian Biodiversification Event.

b4ae2765ceef.title: Carboniferous
b4ae2765ceef.sentence: The diversity of brachiopods and fusilinid foraminiferans, surged beginning in the Visean, continuing through the end of the Carboniferous, although cephalopod and nektonic conodont diversity declined.

ec317ee6dba9.title: Hangenberg event
ec317ee6dba9.sentence: The Hangenberg event effectively "refreshed" bryozoan diversity, eliminating old clades and allowing new forms to radiate and eventually reach a diversity peak in the Visean stage.

5836013f4bbe.title: Carboniferous
5836013f4bbe.sentence: The resulting Variscan orogeny involved a complex series of oblique collisions with associated metamorphism, igneous activity, and large-scale deformation between these terranes and Laurussia, which continued into the Carboniferous.

f7a045e35866.title: Permian
f7a045e35866.sentence: The world at the time was dominated by the supercontinent Pangaea, which had formed with the collision of Euramerica and Gondwana, during the Carboniferous.

c535038299d0.title: Carboniferous
c535038299d0.sentence: During the Carboniferous, there was an increased rate in tectonic plate movements as the supercontinent Pangea assembled.

202fb86c7d54.title: Carboniferous
202fb86c7d54.sentence: The main phase of the LPIA (c. 335–290 Ma) began in the late Visean, as the climate cooled and atmospheric CO2 levels dropped.

3b46e77bf037.title: Carboniferous
3b46e77bf037.sentence: Its onset was accompanied by a global fall in sea level and widespread multimillion-year unconformities.

5eec9dd9cb89.title: Carboniferous
5eec9dd9cb89.sentence: This main phase consisted of a series of discrete several million-year-long glacial periods during which ice expanded out from up to 30 ice centres that stretched across mid- to high latitudes of Gondwana in eastern Australia, northwestern Argentina, southern Brazil, and central and Southern Africa.

a9f50b0800ab.title: Carboniferous
a9f50b0800ab.sentence: Warmer periods with reduced ice volume within the Bashkirian, the late Moscovian and the latest Kasimovian to mid-Gzhelian are inferred from the disappearance of glacial sediments, the appearance of deglaciation deposits and rises in sea levels.

e30d07899617.title: Carboniferous
e30d07899617.sentence: During the mid Carboniferous, the South American sector of Gondwana collided obliquely with Laurussia's southern margin resulting in the Ouachita orogeny.

4b17383244b2.title: Carboniferous
4b17383244b2.sentence: The Visean-Serpukhovian boundary coincides with a major period of glaciation.

ef7d1f2c8b70.title: Hangenberg event
ef7d1f2c8b70.sentence: By this metric, the Hangenberg Event was the joint seventh-worst post-Cambrian mass extinction, tied with the poorly-studied early Serpukhovian extinction in the Carboniferous.

0156d7fbe21f.title: Pennsylvanian (geology)
0156d7fbe21f.sentence: - Namurian (corresponding to Serpukhovian and early Bashkirian)

1fa846f0047c.title: Vertebrate
1fa846f0047c.sentence: A group of vertebrates, the amniotes, with membranes around the embryo allowing it to survive on dry land, branched from amphibious tetrapods in the Carboniferous.

6d1b6a71e359.title: Tetrapod
6d1b6a71e359.sentence: The earliest fossils attributed to crown-group tetrapods are clawed footprints from the earliest Carboniferous (Tournaisian) Snowy Plains Formation of Australia, which were claimed to belong to early amniotes or potentially even sauropsids.

e7f4b266721b.title: Paleozoic
e7f4b266721b.sentence: Amphibians were the dominant tetrapods until the mid-Carboniferous, when climate change greatly reduced their diversity, allowing amniotes to take over.

00031814d1a3.title: Carboniferous
00031814d1a3.sentence: As the West African sector of Gondwana collided with Laurussia during the Late Pennsylvanian, deformation along the Alleghanian orogen became northwesterly-directed compression.

6cd1b3d0074a.title: Carboniferous
6cd1b3d0074a.sentence: The GSSP for the base of the Pennsylvanian Subsystem and Bashkirian Stage is located at Arrow Canyon in Nevada, US and was ratified in 1996.

15b2cfbacdde.title: Carboniferous
15b2cfbacdde.section: Geochemistry > Oxygen and carbon isotope ratios in seawater
15b2cfbacdde.sentence: The Mississippian-Pennsylvanian boundary positive δ18O excursion occurred at the same time as global sea level falls and widespread glacial deposits across southern Gondwana, indicating climate cooling and ice build-up.

a8251e8ae6f8.title: Carboniferous
a8251e8ae6f8.sentence: Closure of the oceanic gateway between the Rheic and Tethys oceans in the early Bashkirian also contributed to climate cooling by changing ocean circulation and heat flow patterns.

dc742b95820a.title: Carboniferous
dc742b95820a.sentence: All modern classes of fungi were present in the late Carboniferous.

c10b23700ebd.title: Pennsylvanian (geology)
c10b23700ebd.sentence: All modern classes of fungi have been found in rocks of Pennsylvanian age.

64450222b444.title: Carboniferous
64450222b444.sentence: However, whilst exact numbers vary, all models show an overall increase in atmospheric oxygen levels from a low of between 15 and 20% at the beginning of the Carboniferous to highs of 25–30% during the Period.

7a470964a822.title: Carboniferous
7a470964a822.sentence: Atmospheric oxygen levels, originally thought to be consistently higher than today throughout the Carboniferous, have been shown to be more variable, increasing from low levels at the beginning of the Period to highs of 25–30%.

0b0bcaebd22e.title: Paleoclimatology
0b0bcaebd22e.section: History of the atmosphere > Third atmosphere
0b0bcaebd22e.sentence: The amount of oxygen in the atmosphere has fluctuated over the last 600 million years, reaching a peak of 35% during the Carboniferous period, significantly higher than today's 21%.

4502139d300a.title: Carboniferous
4502139d300a.sentence: For example: the increasing occurrence of charcoal produced by wildfires from the Late Devonian into the Carboniferous indicates increasing oxygen levels, with calculations showing oxygen levels above 21% for most of the Carboniferous; halite gas inclusions from sediments dated 337–335 Ma give estimates for the Visean of c. 15.3%, although with large uncertainties; and, pyrite records suggest levels of c. 15% early in the Carboniferous, to over 25% during the Pennsylvanian, before dropping back below 20% towards the end.

110ca5311876.title: Coal forest
110ca5311876.sentence: Much of the carbon in the peat deposits produced by coal forests came from photosynthetic fixation of atmospheric carbon dioxide, which released the accompanying split-off oxygen into the atmosphere.

70fd0b9ae7ff.title: Carboniferous
70fd0b9ae7ff.sentence: How the atmospheric oxygen concentrations influenced the large body size of arthropods and other fauna and flora during the Carboniferous is also a subject of ongoing debate.

1bfbb8cefc88.title: Carboniferous rainforest collapse
1bfbb8cefc88.sentence: The concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere crashed to one of its all time global lows in the Pennsylvanian and early Permian.

cf1adabc6788.title: Carboniferous
cf1adabc6788.sentence: Following this, a reduction in atmospheric CO2 levels, caused by the increased burial of organic matter and widespread ocean anoxia led to climate cooling and glaciation across the south polar region.

7fc14e97bfa2.title: Carboniferous
7fc14e97bfa2.section: Geochemistry > Oxygen and carbon isotope ratios in seawater
7fc14e97bfa2.sentence: These changes in seawater geochemistry are interpreted as a decrease in atmospheric CO2 due to increased organic matter burial and widespread ocean anoxia triggering climate cooling and onset of glaciation.

33d76dbe158e.title: Carboniferous
33d76dbe158e.sentence: Isotope records indicate this drop in CO2 levels was triggered by tectonic factors with increased weathering of the growing Central Pangean Mountains and the influence of the mountains on precipitation and surface water flow.

bae31b30cef2.title: Carboniferous
bae31b30cef2.sentence: Together these two factors significantly increased CO2 drawdown from the atmosphere, lowering global temperatures, increasing ocean pH and triggering the Late Paleozoic Ice Age.

376db98c68e1.title: Coal forest
376db98c68e1.sentence: This resurgence of the forests in very late Carboniferous caused lowering of global temperatures and a return of extensive polar ice in southern Gondwana as the forests' rapid rate of growth sequestered carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.

4842587a5f87.title: Carboniferous
4842587a5f87.sentence: In response to the uplift and erosion of the more mafic basement rocks of the Central Pangea Mountains at this time, CO2 levels dropped as low as 175 ppm and remained under 400 ppm for 10 Ma.

057610947387.title: Carboniferous
057610947387.sentence: The LPIA peaked across the Carboniferous-Permian boundary.

47f8d7d7e4dc.title: Carboniferous
47f8d7d7e4dc.sentence: Towards the end of the Carboniferous, extension and rifting across the northern margin of Gondwana led to the breaking away of the Cimmerian terrane during the early Permian and the opening of the Neo-Tethys Ocean.

42e40f58ebbe.title: Coal forest
42e40f58ebbe.sentence: Coal forests or coal swamps were the vast swathes of freshwater swamp and riparian forests that covered much of the lands on Earth's tropical regions during the late Carboniferous (Pennsylvanian) and Permian periods.

f5f7011d0843.title: Paleozoic
f5f7011d0843.sentence: Terrestrial flora reached its climax in the Carboniferous, when towering lycopsid rainforests dominated the tropical belt of Euramerica.

d8e211b98661.title: Carboniferous
d8e211b98661.sentence: During the Pennsylvanian, vast amounts of organic debris accumulated in the peat mires that formed across the low-lying, humid equatorial wetlands of the foreland basins of the Central Pangean Mountains in Laurussia, and around the margins of the North and South China cratons.

619e61d6f63e.title: Coal forest
619e61d6f63e.sentence: As plant matter from these wetland forests decayed, enormous deposits of peat accumulated, which later became buried and converted into coal over the subsequent geologic eras.

9a51df7ecbb1.title: Carboniferous
9a51df7ecbb1.sentence: The majority of Earth's coal deposits were formed during the late Carboniferous and early Permian.

7507f8b1ad8d.title: Carboniferous
7507f8b1ad8d.sentence: There is ongoing debate as to why this peak in the formation of Earth's coal deposits occurred during the Carboniferous.

ccd29420c566.title: Carboniferous
ccd29420c566.sentence: The first theory, known as the delayed fungal evolution hypothesis, proposes that a delay between the development of trees with the wood fibre lignin and the subsequent evolution of lignin-degrading fungi gave a period of time where vast amounts of lignin-based organic material could accumulate.

3a631ce3111f.title: Carboniferous
3a631ce3111f.sentence: The second theory is that the geographical setting and climate of the Carboniferous were unique in Earth's history: the co-occurrence of the position of the continents across the humid equatorial zone, high biological productivity, and the low-lying, water-logged and slowly subsiding sedimentary basins that allowed the thick accumulation of peat were sufficient to account for the peak in coal formation.

b02eb2b67f25.title: Carboniferous
b02eb2b67f25.sentence: During glacial periods, low sea levels exposed large areas of the continental shelves.

d7e46a90d81e.title: Carboniferous
d7e46a90d81e.sentence: Major river channels, up to several kilometres wide, stretched across these shelves feeding a network of smaller channels, lakes and peat mires.

f39e53b0ce81.title: Carboniferous
f39e53b0ce81.sentence: These wetlands were then buried by sediment as sea levels rose during interglacials.

e86b1b5b50a6.title: Carboniferous
e86b1b5b50a6.sentence: During the Pennsylvanian, cyclothems were deposited in shallow, epicontinental seas across the tropical regions of Laurussia (present day western and central US, Europe, Russia and central Asia) and the North and South China cratons.

95c71299ce8b.title: Carboniferous
95c71299ce8b.sentence: The advance and retreat of ice sheets across Gondwana followed a 100 kyr Milankovitch cycle, and so each cyclothem represents a cycle of sea level fall and rise over a 100 kyr period.

0f4d322e3b6e.title: Carboniferous
0f4d322e3b6e.sentence: The rapid sea levels fluctuations they represent correlate with the glacial cycles of the Late Paleozoic Ice Age.

29282afc516f.title: Carboniferous
29282afc516f.sentence: Ideally, this sequence would be reversed as sea levels began to fall again; however, sea level falls tend to be protracted, whilst sea level rises are rapid, ice sheets grow slowly but melt quickly.

13183248c2f7.title: Mesozoic
13183248c2f7.sentence: The Triassic was generally dry, a trend that began in the late Carboniferous, and highly seasonal, especially in the interior of Pangaea.

fcf75c39bee0.title: Carboniferous
fcf75c39bee0.section: Climate > Effects of climate on biodiversity
fcf75c39bee0.sentence: Across the Carboniferous–Permian boundary interval, a rapid drop in CO2 levels and increasingly arid conditions at low-latitudes led to a permanent shift to seasonally dry woodland vegetation.

ab11efcd8237.title: Permian
ab11efcd8237.sentence: In addition to becoming warmer, the climate became notably more arid at the end of the Carboniferous and beginning of the Permian.

e7efaec225fc.title: Carboniferous
e7efaec225fc.section: Geochemistry > Strontium isotopic composition of seawater
e7efaec225fc.sentence: The decline towards the end of the Carboniferous is interpreted as a decrease in continental weathering due to the more arid conditions.

f90fc6cb450f.title: Carboniferous rainforest collapse
f90fc6cb450f.sentence: After the late Bashkirian glacial maximum of the Late Paleozoic Ice Age I, around 318 Ma, frequent shifts in seasonality from humid to arid times began.

7a0d3999a8d0.title: Carboniferous rainforest collapse
7a0d3999a8d0.sentence: In the latest Middle Pennsylvanian (late Moscovian) a cycle of aridification began, coinciding with abrupt faunal changes in marine and terrestrial species.

89f3897934b9.title: Carboniferous rainforest collapse
89f3897934b9.sentence: This change was recorded in paleosols, which reflect a period of overall decreased hydromorphy, increased free-drainage and landscape stability, and a shift in the overall regional climate to drier conditions in the Upper Pennsylvanian (Missourian).

dd95251c7952.title: Carboniferous rainforest collapse
dd95251c7952.sentence: This study found a Late Pennsylvanian extinction pulse that reflects drying climates and the transition of lycopod to tree fern-dominated land floras.

93095e40b706.title: Carboniferous
93095e40b706.sentence: These continued to dominate throughout the period, but during the late Carboniferous, several other groups, Cycadophyta (cycads), the Callistophytales (another group of "seed ferns"), and the Voltziales, appeared.

979e4aa84f4c.title: Silurian-Devonian Terrestrial Revolution
979e4aa84f4c.sentence: True gymnosperms like ginkgos (Ginkgophyta) and cycads (Cycadophyta) would appear slightly after the Devonian in the Carboniferous.

45094d38f6fa.title: Permian
45094d38f6fa.sentence: Early conifers appeared in the Late Carboniferous, represented by primitive walchian conifers, but were replaced with more derived voltzialeans during the Permian.
