c7df879b6b67.title: Carboniferous
c7df879b6b67.sentence: True coniferous trees (Walchia, of the order Voltziales) appear later in the Carboniferous, and preferred higher drier ground.

bb374f4b20d9.title: Carboniferous
bb374f4b20d9.sentence: Land arthropods such as arachnids (e.g. trigonotarbids and Pulmonoscorpius), myriapods (e.g. Arthropleura) and especially insects (particularly flying insects) also underwent a major evolutionary radiation during the late Carboniferous.

4c4716a47b95.title: Carboniferous
4c4716a47b95.sentence: Some arthropods grew to large sizes with the up to 2.6-meter-long (8.5 ft) millipede-like Arthropleura being the largest-known land invertebrate of all time.

9aafeda0bbe3.title: Millipede
9aafeda0bbe3.sentence: During the Carboniferous, Arthropleura became the largest known land-dwelling invertebrate on record, with a length exceeding 2 m (6+1⁄2 ft).

6959008b3197.title: Carboniferous rainforest collapse
6959008b3197.sentence: The rift formation coincides with the Moskovian/Kasimovian boundary and the Carboniferous rainforest collapse.

2c0b42a83ca7.title: Carboniferous
2c0b42a83ca7.sentence: Accretion of the island arc was complete by the Tournaisian, but subduction of the Ural Ocean between Kazakhstania and Laurussia continued until the Bashkirian when the ocean finally closed and continental collision began.

7172de54fe87.title: Carboniferous
7172de54fe87.sentence: Deformation continued into the Permian and during the late Carboniferous and Permian the region was extensively intruded by granites.

250046f5bdbd.title: Carboniferous
250046f5bdbd.sentence: From the Late Devonian to early Carboniferous, the Magnitogorsk island arc, which lay between Kazakhstania and Laurussia in the Ural Ocean, collided with the passive margin of northeastern Laurussia (Baltica craton).

8693ac625152.title: Mammal
8693ac625152.sentence: Synapsida, a clade that contains mammals and their extinct relatives, originated during the Pennsylvanian subperiod (~323 million to ~300 million years ago), when they split from the reptile lineage.

6df8e887cc6d.title: Mammal
6df8e887cc6d.sentence: These characteristics distinguish them from reptiles and birds, from which their ancestors diverged in the Carboniferous period over 300 million years ago.

61eb70031542.title: History of life
61eb70031542.sentence: The earliest fossils of the two surviving amniote groups, synapsids and sauropsids, date from around 313 Ma.

c75c392a2a98.title: Carboniferous
c75c392a2a98.sentence: By the end of the Carboniferous amniotes had already diversified into a number of groups, including several families of synapsid pelycosaurs, protorothyridids, captorhinids, saurians and araeoscelids.

3e501b09b76a.title: Fossil
3e501b09b76a.section: Fossilization processes > Casts and molds > Authigenic mineralization
3e501b09b76a.sentence: Nodules from the Carboniferous Mazon Creek fossil beds of Illinois, US, are among the best documented examples of such mineralization.

00fb5644bb2d.title: History of life
00fb5644bb2d.sentence: The Mazon Creek lagerstätten from the Late Carboniferous, about 300 Ma, include about 200 species, some gigantic by modern standards, and indicate that insects had occupied their main modern ecological niches as herbivores, detritivores and insectivores.

f670280f6ea3.title: Carboniferous
f670280f6ea3.sentence: In the early Kasimovian there was short-lived (<1 million years) intense period of glaciation, with atmospheric CO2 concentration levels dropping as low as 180 ppm.

409360c7f466.title: Carboniferous
409360c7f466.section: Geochemistry > Oxygen and carbon isotope ratios in seawater
409360c7f466.sentence: During the early Kasimovian there was a short (<1myr), intense glacial period, which came to a sudden end as atmospheric CO2 concentrations rapidly rose.

a96069b5e33e.title: Carboniferous
a96069b5e33e.section: Climate > Effects of climate on biodiversity
a96069b5e33e.sentence: There was a major restructuring of wetland forests during the Kasimovian glacial interval, with the loss of arborescent (tree-like) lycopisids and other wetland groups, and a general decline in biodiversity.

bfda1e14a396.title: Coal forest
bfda1e14a396.sentence: The Carboniferous rainforest collapse was caused by a cooler drier climate that initially fragmented, then collapsed the rainforest ecosystem.

4659fc93f68f.title: Carboniferous
4659fc93f68f.section: Climate > Effects of climate on biodiversity
4659fc93f68f.sentence: Although referred to as the Carboniferous rainforest collapse, this was a complex replacement of one type of rainforest by another, not a complete disappearance of rainforest vegetation.

a5432d14c4cf.title: Permian
a5432d14c4cf.sentence: The Carboniferous Rainforest Collapse would result in the replacement of lycopsid-dominated forests with tree-fern dominated ones during the late Carboniferous in Euramerica, and result in the differentiation of the Cathaysian floras from those of Euramerica.

1d12a87d8c15.title: Coal forest
1d12a87d8c15.sentence: At the very end of the Carboniferous, the coal forests underwent a resurgence, expanding mainly in eastern Asia, notably China; they never recovered fully in Laurasia.

4a5c4c906727.title: Tetrapod
4a5c4c906727.sentence: Amphibians and amniotes were affected by the Carboniferous rainforest collapse (CRC), an extinction event that occurred around 307 million years ago.

2d76b7f19e3a.title: History of life
2d76b7f19e3a.sentence: The Carboniferous Rainforest Collapse may have paved the way for amniotes to become dominant over amphibians.

4b99d7e3baf5.title: Carboniferous
4b99d7e3baf5.sentence: A minor marine and terrestrial extinction event, the Carboniferous rainforest collapse, occurred at the end of the period, caused by climate change.

c49927a082c5.title: Permian
c49927a082c5.sentence: The Carboniferous rainforest collapse left behind vast regions of desert within the continental interior.

d269d3b4fb8e.title: Extinction
d269d3b4fb8e.sentence: Particularly, the extinction of amphibians during the Carboniferous Rainforest Collapse, 305 million years ago.

03be3587f9ec.title: Seed plant
03be3587f9ec.sentence: - Glossopteris was the most prominent tree genus in the ancient southern supercontinent of Gondwana during the Permian period.

a16d8bbca783.title: Permian
a16d8bbca783.sentence: During the Permian, all the Earth's major landmasses were collected into a single supercontinent known as Pangaea, with the microcontinental terranes of Cathaysia to the east.

4fc4a434f33e.title: Permian
4fc4a434f33e.sentence: The Kazakhstania block collided with Baltica during the Cisuralian, while the North China Craton, the South China Block and Indochina fused to each other and Pangea by the end of the Permian.

464daf58dc86.title: Permian
464daf58dc86.sentence: The Permian climate was also extremely seasonal and characterised by megamonsoons, which produced high aridity and extreme seasonality in Pangaea's interiors.

26f6bed2b79b.title: Permian
26f6bed2b79b.sentence: The GSSP for the base of the Asselian is located in the Aidaralash River valley near Aqtöbe, Kazakhstan, which was ratified in 1996.

4d39411f316f.title: Carboniferous
4d39411f316f.sentence: The GSSP for the base of the Permian is located in the Aidaralash River valley near Aqtöbe, Kazakhstan and was ratified in 1996.

3ba5805c0528.title: Permian
3ba5805c0528.sentence: Insects, which had first appeared and become abundant during the preceding Carboniferous, experienced a dramatic increase in diversification during the Early Permian.

fb2974884911.title: Permian
fb2974884911.sentence: Mecoptera (sometimes known as scorpionflies) first appeared during the Early Permian, going on to become diverse during the Late Permian.

c8ab67cf486a.title: Permian
c8ab67cf486a.sentence: Primitive relatives of damselflies and dragonflies (Meganisoptera), which include the largest flying insects of all time, also declined during the Permian.

930c3f22e49b.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
930c3f22e49b.sentence: Palaeodictyopteroids (insects with piercing and sucking mouthparts) began to decline during the mid-Permian; these extinctions have been linked to a change in flora.

f6e56ec3218e.title: Permian
f6e56ec3218e.sentence: By the start of the Permian, there was already an active coevolutionary arms race between insects and plant reproductive structures, evidenced by both insect-caused damage in plants and defensive structures in plants aimed at minimising predation by insects.

4404891d76a2.title: Triassic
4404891d76a2.sentence: These terranes had rifted from northeastern Gondwana during the Permian.

a2ba7d7f017e.title: Triassic
a2ba7d7f017e.sentence: The narrow Cimmerian terranes that had rifted from the northern margin of Gondwana in the Permian continued to drift northwards; the Paleo-Tethys Ocean closing in front of them and the Neo-Tethys opening behind.

77a7dab6174a.title: Permian
77a7dab6174a.sentence: A new ocean was growing on its southern end, the Neotethys Ocean, an ocean that would dominate much of the Mesozoic Era.

9703a4a790d9.title: Permian
9703a4a790d9.sentence: Synapsids (the group that would later include mammals) thrived and diversified greatly during the Cisuralian.

2fe6b4ef19c6.title: History of life
2fe6b4ef19c6.sentence: During the Permian period, synapsids, including the ancestors of mammals, dominated the land.

8ddc274b6f97.title: Carboniferous
8ddc274b6f97.sentence: Synapsids quickly became huge and diversified in the Permian, only for their dominance to stop during the Mesozoic.

81e927c42346.title: Permian
81e927c42346.sentence: Early Permian terrestrial faunas of North America and Europe were dominated by primitive pelycosaur synapsids including the herbivorous edaphosaurids, and carnivorous sphenacodontids, diadectids and amphibians.

7a55b1fbaff3.title: History of life
7a55b1fbaff3.sentence: The synapsid pelycosaurs and their descendants the therapsids are the most common land vertebrates in the best-known Permian (298.9 to 251.9 Ma) fossil beds.

602da698a1df.title: Paleozoic
602da698a1df.sentence: By the Cisuralian Epoch, both oxygen and carbon dioxide had recovered to more normal levels.

afbbdcfdd0b5.title: Permian
afbbdcfdd0b5.sentence: The Central Pangean Mountains, which began forming due to the collision of Laurasia and Gondwana during the Carboniferous, reached their maximum height during the early Permian around 295 Ma, comparable to the present Himalayas, but became heavily eroded as the Permian progressed.

d3e0e8d754dc.title: Permian
d3e0e8d754dc.sentence: The earliest known beetles appeared at the beginning of the Permian.

394c8af1988a.title: Permian
394c8af1988a.sentence: Members of the modern orders Archostemata and Adephaga are known from the Late Permian.

c82243c5d0be.title: Permian
c82243c5d0be.sentence: Complex wood boring traces found in the Late Permian of China suggest that members of Polyphaga, the most diverse group of modern beetles, were also present by the Late Permian.

6bf10a5b982b.title: Permian
6bf10a5b982b.sentence: By 287 Ma, temperatures warmed and the South Pole ice cap retreated in what was known as the Artinskian Warming Event (AWE), though glaciers remained present in the uplands of eastern Australia, and perhaps also the mountainous regions of far northern Siberia.

b800d3a8dd3b.title: Permian
b800d3a8dd3b.sentence: Sea levels also rose notably in the Early Permian as the LPIA slowly waned.

c21805a1352a.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
c21805a1352a.section: Hypotheses about cause > Volcanism > Choiyoi Silicic Large Igneous Province
c21805a1352a.sentence: A second flood basalt event that produced the Choiyoi Silicic Large Igneous Province in southwestern Gondwana between around 286 Ma and 247 Ma has also been suggested as a significant additional extinction mechanism.

d99af276db34.title: Permian
d99af276db34.sentence: In the late Kungurian, cooling resumed, resulting in a cool glacial interval that lasted into the early Capitanian, though average temperatures were still much higher than during the beginning of the Cisuralian.

26951a6f1adc.title: Permian
26951a6f1adc.sentence: Bennettitales, which would go on to become in widespread the Mesozoic, first appeared during the Cisuralian in China.

0564f46f4441.title: Triassic
0564f46f4441.sentence: While having first appeared during the Permian, the extinct seed plant group Bennettitales first became a prominent element in global floras during the Late Triassic, a position they would hold for much of the Mesozoic.

75042112143e.title: Mesozoic
75042112143e.sentence: Bennettitales, an extinct group of gymnosperms with foliage superficially resembling that of cycads gained a global distribution during the Late Triassic, and represented one of the most common groups of Mesozoic seed plants.

5248a93b6326.title: Permian
5248a93b6326.sentence: Deserts seem to have been widespread on Pangaea.

4cb28362a314.title: Geologic time scale
4cb28362a314.sentence: Phanerozoic | Paleozoic | Permian | Cisuralian | Kungurian | Pangaea at its maximum extent. Ural and Alleghanian orogenies continue. Hunter-Bowen orogeny, eastern Australia; Sonoma orogeny, western Laurussia. Kazakhstania and Tarim collide with Siberia. Orogenic collapse of Variscan orogeny and early extension along the lines of the future Atlantic, Indian and Southern Oceans. Opening of Neo-Tethys Ocean as Cimmerian terranes rift from northeast Gondwana. Late Paleozoic Ice Age wanes and humid, icehouse climate give way to arid, greenhouse conditions. Global average temperatures rise from c. 12° to over 30° at Permo-Triassic boundary. Desert dune sands and evaporites dominate interior of Pangea. Coal swamps at high latitudes and humid coastal regions. Mosses, Coleoptera (beetles) and Diptera (two-winged flies) appear. Diapsids split into archosaurs (crocodiles and dinosaurs) and lepidosaurs (lizards and snakes). First marine reptiles. Therapsids and cynodonts evolve from synapsids. Guadalupian-Lopingian boundary mass extinction linked to eruption of Emeishan LIP, South China. At the Permo-Triassic boundary, eruption of the Siberian Traps LIP releases vast amounts of CO 2 leading to extreme global warming, and the end-Permian mass extinction. Anoxic waters from the deep ocean move up to the shallows, eliminating trilobites, rugose and tabulate corals, and placoderms. Brachiopods, ammonoids, sharks, bony fish, and crinoids see major reductions. On land, forests disappear. Palaeodictyopterida and many insect groups go extinct, as do all non-therapsid synapsids and most therapsid genera. | 283.3 ± 0.4

47c93422a05e.title: Permian
47c93422a05e.sentence: The Ceratitida originated from the family Daraelitidae within Prolecanitida during the mid-Permian, and extensively diversified during the Late Permian.

cf7719764d72.title: Permian
cf7719764d72.sentence: Amongst ammonoids, Goniatitida were a major group during the Early-Mid Permian, but declined during the Late Permian.

4f6b29c361fb.title: Permian
4f6b29c361fb.sentence: Brachiopods also served as important ecosystem engineers in Permian reef complexes.

3550906de987.title: Mammal
3550906de987.sentence: Early synapsids are referred to as "pelycosaurs." The more advanced therapsids became dominant during the Guadalupian.

0126d6294927.title: Permian
0126d6294927.sentence: Uncertain dating has led to suggestions that there is a global hiatus in the terrestrial fossil record during the late Kungurian and early Roadian, referred to as "Olson's Gap" that obscures the nature of the transition.

b950734028c1.title: Permian
b950734028c1.sentence: The Middle Permian faunas of South Africa and Russia are dominated by therapsids, most abundantly by the diverse Dinocephalia.

52d6a618c21c.title: Permian
52d6a618c21c.sentence: Another group of therapsids, the therocephalians (such as Lycosuchus), arose in the Middle Permian.

fd774e3ddb4a.title: Permian
fd774e3ddb4a.sentence: The sea level was stable at several tens of metres above present during the Early Permian, but there was a sharp drop beginning during the Roadian, culminating in the lowest sea level of the entire Palaeozoic at around present sea level during the Wuchiapingian, followed by a slight rise during the Changhsingian.

a9caec0accde.title: Paleozoic
a9caec0accde.sentence: The Lopingian Epoch is associated with falling sea levels, increased carbon dioxide and general climatic deterioration, culminating in the devastation of the Permian extinction.

3ddd69ee5501.title: Permian
3ddd69ee5501.sentence: The end of the Early Permian (Cisuralian) was marked by a major faunal shift as most lineages of primitive "pelycosaur" synapsids became extinct, being replaced by more advanced therapsids during the Middle Permian (Guadalupian), though the nature of this transition (which may have been an extinction event dubbed "Olson's Extinction") is poorly understood.

2529807dc1c8.title: Permian
2529807dc1c8.sentence: Temnospondyls reached a peak of diversity in the Cisuralian, with a substantial decline during the Guadalupian-Lopingian following Olson's extinction, with the family diversity dropping below Carboniferous levels.

3085661f89ac.title: Guadalupian
3085661f89ac.sentence: Extreme environments were observed from the Permian of Kansas which resulted from a combination of hot climate and acidic waters particularly coincident with Olson's Extinction.

45d1ed1d720e.title: Guadalupian
45d1ed1d720e.sentence: A mass extinction occurred 273 million years ago in the early Guadalupian before the larger Permian–Triassic extinction event.

ae2cbcdf4f7a.title: Triassic
ae2cbcdf4f7a.sentence: The counterclockwise rotation of Pangea precipitated dextral transpression across the NNE-SSW trending, west-dipping subduction zone, along the eastern Australian margin, which culminated in the Hunter-Bowen orogeny (c. 260-230 Ma).

b74a482997b0.title: Permian
b74a482997b0.sentence: The end of the Capitanian Stage at the end of the Middle Permian was marked by the major Capitanian mass extinction event, associated with the eruption of the Emeishan Traps.

15a8b996c19b.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
15a8b996c19b.sentence: The impact of the end-Guadalupian extinction on marine organisms appears to have varied between locations and between taxonomic groups – brachiopods and corals had severe losses.

aa26872ebef0.title: Permian
aa26872ebef0.sentence: Dinocephalians become extinct at the end of the Middle Permian, during the Capitanian mass extinction event.

20365de3cc41.title: Guadalupian
20365de3cc41.sentence: A significant mass extinction event (the End-Capitanian extinction event) occurred at the end of this epoch, which was associated with anoxia and acidification in the oceans and possibly caused by the volcanic eruptions that produced the Emeishan Traps.

414e49ea0f07.title: Permian
414e49ea0f07.sentence: Another cool period began around the middle Capitanian.

1b349886171c.title: Permian
1b349886171c.sentence: It was interrupted by the Emeishan Thermal Excursion in the late part of the Capitanian, around 260 million years ago, corresponding to the eruption of the Emeishan Traps.

423703404891.title: Permian
423703404891.sentence: During the early Wuchiapingian, following the emplacement of the Emeishan Traps, global temperatures declined as carbon dioxide was weathered out of the atmosphere by the large igneous province's emplaced basalts.

a75500389b87.title: Permian
a75500389b87.sentence: Cynodonts, the group of therapsids ancestral to modern mammals, first appeared and gained a worldwide distribution during the Late Permian.

8cd6cd340ee2.title: Guadalupian
8cd6cd340ee2.sentence: Global diversity rose dramatically by the end probably the result of disaster taxa filling empty guilds, only to fall again when the end-Guadalupian event caused a diversity drop in the Wuchiapingian.

4c2903da7a73.title: Permian
4c2903da7a73.sentence: Late Permian faunas are dominated by advanced therapsids such as the predatory sabertoothed gorgonopsians and herbivorous beaked dicynodonts, alongside large herbivorous pareiasaur parareptiles.

37c0f19c5c94.title: Permian
37c0f19c5c94.sentence: The Archosauromorpha, the group of reptiles that would give rise to the pseudosuchians, dinosaurs, and pterosaurs in the following Triassic, first appeared and diversified during the Late Permian, including the first appearance of the Archosauriformes during the latest Permian.

8c7656d44b44.title: Triassic
8c7656d44b44.sentence: Archosauromorph reptiles, which had already appeared and diversified to an extent in the Permian Period, exploded in diversity as an adaptive radiation in response to the Permian-Triassic mass extinction.

2ab173c80e3e.title: Permian
2ab173c80e3e.sentence: There were no flying vertebrates, though the extinct lizard-like reptile family Weigeltisauridae from the Late Permian had extendable wings like modern gliding lizards, and are the oldest known gliding vertebrates.

56937864215b.title: Permian
56937864215b.sentence: By the Late Permian, high thin forests had become widespread across the globe, as evidenced by the global distribution of weigeltisaurids.

25e894976cc3.title: Triassic
25e894976cc3.section: Paleogeography > Opening of the Central Atlantic
25e894976cc3.sentence: Beginning in the latest Permian, a broad zone of lithospheric extension developed across Pangea along the line of the future Central Atlantic Ocean.

38f88ad8581d.title: Triassic
38f88ad8581d.sentence: Major extensional tectonic movements, that began in the late Permian, continued across Laurussia from North/Central Europe in the east to eastern Canada in the west, with north-south trending graben systems developing across Europe, including further subsidence in the Northern and Southern Permian basins.

e32d0c112745.title: Permian
e32d0c112745.sentence: The Zechstein Sea, a hypersaline epicontinental sea, existed in what is now northwestern Europe.

fd087e8938f9.title: Carboniferous
fd087e8938f9.sentence: The Carboniferous climate was dominated by the Late Paleozoic Ice Age (LPIA), the most extensive and longest icehouse period of the Phanerozoic, which lasted from the Late Devonian to the Permian (365 Ma-253 Ma).

28f5a861f25b.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
28f5a861f25b.section: Hypotheses about cause > Volcanism > Siberian Traps
28f5a861f25b.sentence: A series of surges raised terrestrial and marine environmental mercury concentrations by orders of magnitude above normal background levels and caused mercury poisoning over periods of a thousand years each.

f02ca904a095.title: Permian
f02ca904a095.sentence: The end of the Permian is marked by a temperature excursion, much larger than the Emeishan Thermal Excursion, at the Permian-Triassic boundary, corresponding to the eruption of the Siberian Traps, which released more than 5 teratonnes of CO2, more than doubling the atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration.

2f8529b1cd3b.title: Paleontology
2f8529b1cd3b.sentence: Glaciation and subsequent global warming has been suggested as a cause for the Late Ordovician mass extinction, and the volcanic activity of the Siberian Traps large igneous province has been suggested as the primary cause for the Permian-Triassic mass extinction.

8458d5277665.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
8458d5277665.sentence: The Glossopteris-dominated flora that characterized high-latitude Gondwana collapsed in Australia around 370,000 years before the Permian-Triassic boundary, with this flora's collapse being less constrained in western Gondwana but still likely occurring a few hundred thousand years before the boundary.

eb32820a01ac.title: Triassic
eb32820a01ac.sentence: Immediately above the Permian–Triassic boundary the glossopteris flora was suddenly largely displaced by an Australia-wide coniferous flora.

da10acd4e29c.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
da10acd4e29c.sentence: A large, abrupt global decrease in δ13C, the ratio of the stable isotope carbon-13 to that of carbon-12, coincides with this extinction, and is sometimes used to identify the Permian–Triassic boundary and the Permian-Triassic Mass Extinction event (PTME) in rocks that are unsuitable for radiometric dating.

10a4dae7dde9.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
10a4dae7dde9.sentence: The negative carbon isotope excursion's magnitude was 4–7% and lasted for approximately 500,000 years, though estimating its exact value is challenging due to diagenetic alteration of many sedimentary facies spanning the boundary.

43743e66f393.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
43743e66f393.section: Hypotheses about cause > Methane clathrate gasification
43743e66f393.sentence: Massive release of methane from these clathrates may have contributed to the PTME, as scientists have found worldwide evidence of a swift decrease of about 1% in the 13C ⁄ 12C ratio in carbonate rocks from the end-Permian.

bf9096d45e26.title: Permian
bf9096d45e26.sentence: The frozen methane hypothesis helps explain the increase in carbon-12 levels found midway in the Permian–Triassic boundary layer.

2e735d225819.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
2e735d225819.section: Hypotheses about cause > Methane clathrate gasification
2e735d225819.sentence: The latest research suggests that greenhouse gas release during the extinction event was dominated by volcanic carbon dioxide, and while methane release had to have contributed, isotopic signatures show that thermogenic methane released from the Siberian Traps had consistently played a larger role than methane from clathrates and any other biogenic sources such as wetlands during the event.

793873b30660.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
793873b30660.sentence: Chemostratigraphic analysis of Permian-Triassic boundary sediments in Chaotian demonstrates that a methanogenic burst could be responsible for some percentage of the carbon isotopic fluctuations.

861851ff6617.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
861851ff6617.sentence: Chemostratigraphic analysis from sections in Finnmark and Trøndelag shows the terrestrial floral turnover occurred before the large negative δ13C shift during the marine extinction.

ef63b2756ea6.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
ef63b2756ea6.sentence: The level of atmospheric carbon dioxide rose from around 400 ppm to 2,500 ppm with approximately 3,900 to 12,000 gigatonnes of carbon being added to the ocean-atmosphere system during this period.

e391a84a4799.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
e391a84a4799.sentence: Further evidence for environmental change around the Permian-Triassic boundary suggests an 8 °C (14 °F) rise in temperature, and an increase in CO 2 levels to 2,500 ppm (for comparison, the concentration immediately before the Industrial Revolution was 280 ppm, and the amount today is about 426 ppm).

2a7f1431dbbb.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
2a7f1431dbbb.section: Hypotheses about cause > Volcanism > Siberian Traps
2a7f1431dbbb.sentence: During the latest Permian before the extinction, global average surface temperatures were about 18.2 °C, which shot up to as much as 35 °C, this hyperthermal condition lasting as long as 500,000 years.

d2ece2f42b85.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
d2ece2f42b85.section: Hypotheses about cause > Volcanism > Siberian Traps
d2ece2f42b85.sentence: In present-day Iran, tropical sea surface temperatures were between 27 and 33 °C during the Changhsingian but jumped to over 35 °C during the PTME.

34f1685c42a1.title: Permian
34f1685c42a1.sentence: This extremely rapid interval of greenhouse gas release caused the Permian-Triassic mass extinction, as well as ushering in an extreme hothouse that persisted for several million years into the next geologic epoch, the Triassic.

f4b8fc432b2a.title: Extinction event
f4b8fc432b2a.section: Causes > Most widely supported explanations > Global warming
f4b8fc432b2a.sentence: Furthermore, the Permian–Triassic extinction event has been suggested to have been caused by warming.

393646b7b090.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
393646b7b090.sentence: It is Earth's most severe known extinction event, with the extinction of 57% of biological families, 62% of genera, 81% of marine species, and 70% of terrestrial vertebrate species.

1858388520c4.title: Extinction event
1858388520c4.sentence: The worst Phanerozoic event, the Permian–Triassic extinction, devastated life on Earth, killing over 90% of species.

f47ecb96d3f4.title: Permian
f47ecb96d3f4.sentence: The Permian ended with the most extensive extinction event recorded in paleontology: the Permian–Triassic extinction event.

88bc2309d7bf.title: History of Earth
88bc2309d7bf.sentence: The era began with the Permian–Triassic extinction event, the most severe extinction event in the fossil record whereby 95% of species on Earth died out, and ended with the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event that wiped out the dinosaurs.

659445302499.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
659445302499.sentence: There is evidence for one to three distinct pulses, or phases, of extinction, with the major pulse of marine extinction occurring in a 60,000-100,000 year interval around 251.902 million years ago (mya) marking the boundary between the Permian and Triassic periods.

3e41d2782ade.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
3e41d2782ade.sentence: The extinction occurred between 251.941 ± 0.037 and 251.880 ± 0.031 million years ago, a duration of 60 ± 48 thousand years.

3d2e0533077b.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
3d2e0533077b.sentence: U–Pb zircon dates from five volcanic ash beds from the Global Stratotype Section and Point for the Permian–Triassic boundary at Meishan, China, establish a high-resolution age model for the extinction – allowing exploration of the links between global environmental perturbation, carbon cycle disruption, mass extinction, and recovery at millennial timescales.

b7abea6f5464.title: Paleozoic
b7abea6f5464.sentence: Radiometric dating of volcanic clay layers just above and below the boundary confine its age to a narrow range of 251.902 ± 0.024 Ma.

e3f6ab56d8e7.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
e3f6ab56d8e7.sentence: The scientific consensus is that the main cause of the extinction was the flood basalt eruptions that created the Siberian Traps, which released sulfur dioxide and carbon dioxide, resulting in euxinia (oxygen-starved, sulfurous oceans), elevated global temperatures, and acidified oceans.

e008e8966b3d.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
e008e8966b3d.sentence: The extinction primarily affected organisms with calcium carbonate skeletons, especially those that relied on stable CO2 levels to produce them.

dc6c2c2c658c.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
dc6c2c2c658c.sentence: Marine invertebrates suffered the greatest losses during the P–Tr extinction, although previous estimates of 90–96% marine species extinction were due to historical conflation with the end-Capitanian mass extinction, which occurred 7–10 million years earlier.

265b244e0c16.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
265b244e0c16.sentence: The end-Permian is the largest known mass extinction of insects; according to some sources, it may well be the only mass extinction to affect insect diversity significantly.

1d1f9ce9e7d2.title: History of life
1d1f9ce9e7d2.sentence: The Permian–Triassic extinction event wiped out almost all land vertebrates, as well as the great majority of other life.

9f840995a1f8.title: Triassic
9f840995a1f8.sentence: The Permian–Triassic extinction devastated terrestrial life.

27b445f3e44c.title: Vertebrate
27b445f3e44c.section: Evolutionary history > Mesozoic: Age of Dinosaurs
27b445f3e44c.sentence: At the onset of the Mesozoic, all larger vertebrate groups were devastated after the largest mass extinction in earth history.

f5cf6beea13c.title: Paleozoic
f5cf6beea13c.sentence: The Paleozoic Era ended with the largest extinction event of the Phanerozoic Eon, the Permian–Triassic extinction event.

fd1939b84a72.title: Mesozoic
fd1939b84a72.sentence: This era began in the wake of the Permian–Triassic extinction event, the largest mass extinction in Earth's history, and ended with the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event, another mass extinction whose victims included the non-avian dinosaurs, pterosaurs, mosasaurs, and plesiosaurs.

b20437f7a0cb.title: Permian
b20437f7a0cb.sentence: Recovery from the Permian–Triassic extinction event was protracted; on land, ecosystems took 30 million years to recover.

8556be677850.title: Extinction event
8556be677850.sentence: Recent research indicates that recovery did not begin until the start of the mid-Triassic, four to six million years after the extinction; and some writers estimate that the recovery was not complete until 30 million years after the P-T extinction, that is, in the late Triassic.

2b58f578d60c.title: Paleoclimatology
2b58f578d60c.section: Notable climate events in Earth history

297bef9b1d48.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
297bef9b1d48.section: Hypotheses about cause > Hypercapnia and acidification
297bef9b1d48.sentence: In addition, an increase in CO2 concentration is inevitably linked to ocean acidification, consistent with the preferential extinction of heavily calcified taxa and other signals in the rock record that suggest a more acidic ocean, such as a carbonate production crisis that occurred a few thousand years after volcanic greenhouse gas emissions began.

972d93bd9bc7.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
972d93bd9bc7.section: Hypotheses about cause > Hypercapnia and acidification
972d93bd9bc7.sentence: The decrease in ocean pH is calculated to be up to 0.7 units.

d433b5a99c66.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
d433b5a99c66.section: Hypotheses about cause > Hypercapnia and acidification
d433b5a99c66.sentence: Ocean acidification was most extreme at mid-latitudes, and the major marine transgression associated with the end-Permian extinction is believed to have devastated shallow shelf communities in conjunction with anoxia.

6c7a658b6537.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
6c7a658b6537.section: Hypotheses about cause > Hypercapnia and acidification
6c7a658b6537.sentence: The increasing acidification of rainwater caused increased soil erosion as a result of the increased acidity of forest soils, evidenced by the increased influx of terrestrially derived organic sediments found in marine sedimentary deposits during the end-Permian extinction.

d16fa0bbf898.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
d16fa0bbf898.section: Hypotheses about cause > Hypercapnia and acidification
d16fa0bbf898.sentence: The increased abundance of vermiculitic clays in Shansi, South China coinciding with the Permian-Triassic boundary strongly suggests a sharp drop in soil pH causally related to volcanogenic emissions of carbon dioxide and sulphur dioxide.

ae22ca9afe91.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
ae22ca9afe91.section: Hypotheses about cause > Anoxia and euxinia
ae22ca9afe91.sentence: Evidence for widespread ocean anoxia (severe deficiency of oxygen) and euxinia (presence of hydrogen sulfide) is found from the Late Permian to the Early Triassic.

2fc9221783f9.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
2fc9221783f9.section: Hypotheses about cause > Anoxia and euxinia
2fc9221783f9.sentence: Biogeochemical evidence also points to the presence of euxinia during the PTME.

4ad965aa2db5.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
4ad965aa2db5.section: Hypotheses about cause > Anoxia and euxinia
4ad965aa2db5.sentence: Throughout most of the Tethys and Panthalassic Oceans, evidence for anoxia appears at the extinction event, including small pyrite framboids, negative δ238U excursions, negative δ15N excursions, positive δ82/78Se isotope excursions, relatively positive δ13C ratios in polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, high Th/U ratios, positive Ce/Ce* anomalies, depletions of molybdenum, uranium, and vanadium from seawater, and fine laminations in sediments.

87aee31f63d0.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
87aee31f63d0.section: Hypotheses about cause > Anoxia and euxinia
87aee31f63d0.sentence: However, evidence for anoxia precedes the extinction at some other sites, including Spiti, India, Shangsi, China, Meishan, China, Opal Creek, Alberta, and Kap Stosch, Greenland.

0caa24b9827f.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
0caa24b9827f.section: Hypotheses about cause > Anoxia and euxinia
0caa24b9827f.sentence: A severe anoxic event at the end of the Permian would have allowed sulfate-reducing bacteria to thrive, causing the production of large amounts of hydrogen sulfide in the anoxic ocean, turning it euxinic.

ee2019ee397b.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
ee2019ee397b.section: Hypotheses about cause > Anoxia and euxinia
ee2019ee397b.sentence: Their abundance in sediments from the P–T boundary indicates that euxinic conditions were present even in the shallow waters of the photic zone.

3c3814661cd0.title: Extinction event
3c3814661cd0.section: Causes > Most widely supported explanations > Hydrogen sulfide emissions from the seas
3c3814661cd0.sentence: Kump, Pavlov and Arthur (2005) have proposed that during the Permian–Triassic extinction event the warming also upset the oceanic balance between photosynthesising plankton and deep-water sulfate-reducing bacteria, causing massive emissions of hydrogen sulfide, which poisoned life on both land and sea and severely weakened the ozone layer, exposing much of the life that still remained to fatal levels of UV radiation.

20085313c310.title: Extinction event
20085313c310.section: Causes > Most widely supported explanations > Oceanic overturn
20085313c310.sentence: It has been suggested that oceanic overturn caused or contributed to the late Devonian and Permian–Triassic extinctions.

62d6011d2775.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
62d6011d2775.section: Hypotheses about cause > Methane clathrate gasification
62d6011d2775.sentence: Adding to the evidence against methane clathrate release as the central driver of warming, the main rapid warming event is also associated with marine transgression rather than regression; the former would not normally have initiated methane release, which would have instead required a decrease in pressure, something that a retreat of shallow seas would generate.

6a907b69c357.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
6a907b69c357.sentence: Foraminiferans | 97% | Fusulinids died out, but were almost extinct before the catastrophe

ba1d7d2b8c86.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
ba1d7d2b8c86.sentence: The reasons why lagenides survived while fusulinoidean fusulinides went completely extinct may have been the greater range of environmental tolerance and greater geographic distribution of the former compared to the latter.

907940479b94.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
907940479b94.sentence: The caloneurodeans, paleodictyopteroids, protelytropterans, and protodonates became extinct by the end of the Permian.

b99bc586ea40.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
b99bc586ea40.sentence: Most fossil insect groups found after the Permian–Triassic boundary differ significantly from those before: Of Paleozoic insect groups, only the Glosselytrodea, Miomoptera, and Protorthoptera have been discovered in deposits from after the extinction.

5b99562aa0c8.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
5b99562aa0c8.sentence: Devonian reef-builders are entirely extinct in the modern day: Stromatoporoids died out in the end-Devonian Hangenberg event, while rugose and tabulate corals went extinct at the Permian-Triassic extinction.

9d5ca5a580e5.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
9d5ca5a580e5.sentence: Anthozoans | 96% | Tabulate and rugose corals died out

8a58d1711142.title: Permian
8a58d1711142.sentence: At the close of the Permian, lycopod and equisete swamps reminiscent of Carboniferous flora survived only in Cathaysia, a series of equatorial islands in the Paleo-Tethys Ocean that later would become South China.

0e252a12f42e.title: Permian
0e252a12f42e.sentence: Trilobites, which had thrived since Cambrian times, finally became extinct before the end of the Permian.

57e07272fe80.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
57e07272fe80.sentence: Trilobites | 100% | In decline since the Devonian; only 5 genera living before the extinction

d03c995617af.title: Paleozoic
d03c995617af.sentence: Near the end of the Permian, Pangaea grew drier.

a4fdbb518246.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
a4fdbb518246.sentence: Increasing continental aridity, a trend well underway even before the PTME as a result of the coalescence of the supercontinent Pangaea, was drastically exacerbated by terminal Permian volcanism and global warming.

22dced68246d.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
22dced68246d.sentence: In the Kuznetsk Basin of southwestern Siberia, an increase in aridity led to the demise of the humid-adapted Cordaites forests in the region a few hundred thousand years before the Permian-Triassic boundary.

6a0ac5e03761.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
6a0ac5e03761.sentence: However, suggestions that an asteroid impact was the trigger of the Permian-Triassic extinction are now largely rejected.

ba5c666de8de.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
ba5c666de8de.section: Hypotheses about cause > Asteroid impact > Possible impact sites
ba5c666de8de.sentence: Possible impact craters proposed as the site of an impact causing the P–Tr extinction include the 250 km (160 mi) Bedout structure off the northwest coast of Australia and the hypothesized 480 km (300 mi) Wilkes Land crater of East Antarctica.

101091078432.title: History of Earth
101091078432.sentence: Either the proposed Wilkes Land crater in Antarctica or Bedout structure off the northwest coast of Australia may indicate an impact connection with the Permian-Triassic extinction.

2a08f85d2a2e.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
2a08f85d2a2e.sentence: Reported evidence for an impact event from the P–Tr boundary level includes rare grains of shocked quartz in Australia and Antarctica; fullerenes trapping extraterrestrial noble gases; meteorite fragments in Antarctica; and grains rich in iron, nickel, and silicon, which an impact may have created.

1760cd366667.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
1760cd366667.sentence: Iridium levels in many sites straddling the Permian-Triassic boundaries are not anomalous, providing evidence against an extraterrestrial impact as the cause of the PTME.

fa58b361647a.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
fa58b361647a.sentence: Additionally, many sites spanning the Permian-Triassic boundary display a complete lack of evidence of an impact event.

6f9732a66341.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
6f9732a66341.section: Hypotheses about cause > Anoxia and euxinia
6f9732a66341.sentence: The persistence of anoxia through the Early Triassic may explain the slow recovery of marine life and low levels of biodiversity after the extinction, particularly that of benthic organisms.

432618e0a039.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
432618e0a039.sentence: Indeed, biomarker evidence for anaerobic photosynthesis by Chlorobiaceae (green sulfur bacteria) from the Late-Permian into the Early Triassic indicates that hydrogen sulphide did upwell into shallow waters because these bacteria are restricted to the photic zone and use sulfide as an electron donor.

298552d08111.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
298552d08111.section: Hypotheses about cause > Hypercapnia and acidification
298552d08111.sentence: The persistence of highly elevated carbon dioxide concentrations in the atmosphere and ocean during the Early Triassic would have impeded the recovery of biocalcifying organisms after the PTME.

280f87a7a06d.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
280f87a7a06d.section: Hypotheses about cause > Methane clathrate gasification
280f87a7a06d.sentence: - Rather than a sudden decline in sea level, intermittent periods of ocean-bottom hyperoxia and anoxia (high-oxygen and low- or zero-oxygen conditions) may have caused the 13C ⁄ 12C ratio fluctuations in the Early Triassic; and global anoxia may have been responsible for the end-Permian blip.

947c4a7de8b8.title: Permian
947c4a7de8b8.sentence: The diversity of coelacanths is relatively low throughout the Permian in comparison to other marine fishes, though there is an increase in diversity during the terminal Permian (Changhsingian), corresponding with the highest diversity in their evolutionary history during the Early Triassic.

5305daf4bbef.title: Triassic
5305daf4bbef.sentence: Coelacanths show their highest post-Devonian diversity in the Early Triassic.

8907e71c624b.title: Triassic
8907e71c624b.sentence: The Early Triassic was the hottest portion of the entire Phanerozoic, seeing as it occurred during and immediately after the discharge of titanic volumes of greenhouse gases from the Siberian Traps.

65d58aec5b70.title: Mesozoic
65d58aec5b70.sentence: The Early Triassic (251.902 to 247 Ma) was dominated by deserts in the interior of the Pangaea supercontinent.

593884c04110.title: Triassic
593884c04110.sentence: The Early Triassic began with the Permian-Triassic Thermal Maximum (PTTM) and was followed by the brief Dienerian Cooling (DC) from 251 to 249 Ma, which was in turn followed by the Latest Smithian Thermal Maximum (LSTT) around 249 to 248 Ma.

678e473cdd05.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
678e473cdd05.sentence: A tetrapod gap may have existed from the Induan until the early Spathian between ~30 °N and ~ 40 °S due to extreme heat making these low latitudes uninhabitable for these animals.

074067b5124b.title: Permian
074067b5124b.sentence: The earliest unequivocal members of Neopterygii appear during the Early Triassic, but a Permian origin is suspected.

43799e0c6ee5.title: Triassic
43799e0c6ee5.sentence: The earliest known neopterygian fish, including early holosteans and teleosts, appeared near the beginning of the Triassic, and quickly diversified to become among the dominant groups of fish in both freshwater and marine habitats.

9669242917ef.title: Triassic
9669242917ef.sentence: Ray-finned fishes (actinopterygians) went through a remarkable diversification in the beginning of the Triassic, leading to peak diversity during the Middle Triassic; however, the pattern of this diversification is still not well understood due to a taphonomic megabias.

4b5b0b878883.title: Triassic
4b5b0b878883.sentence: Predatory actinopterygians such as saurichthyids and birgeriids, some of which grew over 1.2 m (3.9 ft) in length, appeared in the Early Triassic and became widespread and successful during the period as a whole.

9e787ff282e0.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
9e787ff282e0.sentence: Lystrosaurus, a pig-sized herbivorous dicynodont therapsid, constituted as much as 90% of some earliest Triassic land vertebrate fauna, although some recent evidence has called into question its status as a post-PTME disaster taxon.

e8e2f95a0b2a.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
e8e2f95a0b2a.sentence: The evolutionary success of Lystrosaurus in the aftermath of the PTME is believed to be attributable to the dicynodont taxon's grouping behaviour and tolerance for extreme and highly variable climatic conditions.

feced785c52b.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
feced785c52b.sentence: Other likely factors behind the success of Lystrosaurus included extremely fast growth rate exhibited by the dicynodont genus, along with its early onset of sexual maturity.

ee8020d926ae.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
ee8020d926ae.sentence: Ichnological evidence from the earliest Triassic of the Karoo Basin shows dicynodonts were abundant in the immediate aftermath of the biotic crisis.

67ab4ed8ee63.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
67ab4ed8ee63.sentence: Microbial reefs were common across shallow seas for a short time during the earliest Triassic, predominating in low latitudes while being rarer in higher latitudes, occurring both in anoxic and oxic waters.

186bd037b0f4.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
186bd037b0f4.sentence: Microbial-metazoan reefs appeared very early in the Early Triassic; and they dominated many surviving communities across the recovery from the mass extinction.

c84e2932a0d6.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
c84e2932a0d6.sentence: Keratinous sponges were particularly noteworthy in their integral importance to Early Triassic microbial-metazoan reef communities, and they helped to create stability in heavily damaged ecosystems during early phases of biotic recovery.

a7e8527e99f3.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
a7e8527e99f3.sentence: Microbially induced sedimentary structures (MISS) from the earliest Triassic have been found to be associated with abundant opportunistic bivalves and vertical burrows, and it is likely that post-extinction microbial mats played a vital, indispensable role in the survival and recovery of various bioturbating organisms.

622bea470e46.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
622bea470e46.sentence: Microbially induced sedimentary structures (MISS) dominated North Chinese terrestrial fossil assemblages in the Early Triassic.

fb02cd86f0a6.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
fb02cd86f0a6.sentence: The disappearance of MISS later in the Early Triassic likely indicated a greater recovery of terrestrial ecosystems and specifically a return of prevalent bioturbation.

116be2b2e642.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
116be2b2e642.section: Hypotheses about cause > Volcanism > Siberian Traps
116be2b2e642.sentence: Carbon isotope fluctuations suggest that massive Siberian Traps activity recurred multiple times during the Early Triassic, a finding corroborated by mercury spikes, causing further extinction events during the epoch.

e4f91651de09.title: Triassic
e4f91651de09.sentence: Eruptions of the Siberian Traps Large Igneous Province (LIP) persisted into the Early Triassic and the Central Atlantic Magmatic Province (CAMP) were active by the Late Triassic as a prelude to seafloor spreading in the Central Atlantic at the boundary of the Triassic and Jurassic.

a5fb00d6312f.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
a5fb00d6312f.section: Hypotheses about cause > Methane clathrate gasification
a5fb00d6312f.sentence: Also, the pattern of isotope shifts expected to result from a massive release of methane does not match the patterns seen throughout the Early Triassic.

182a9f36b644.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
182a9f36b644.section: Hypotheses about cause > Methane clathrate gasification
182a9f36b644.sentence: Not only would such a cause require the release of five times as much methane as postulated for the PETM, but would it also have to be reburied at an unrealistically high rate to account for the rapid increases in the 13C ⁄ 12C ratio (episodes of high positive δ13C) throughout the early Triassic before it was released several times again.

ec8ee824d309.title: Extinction event
ec8ee824d309.sentence: It is thought that this long recovery was due to successive waves of extinction that inhibited recovery, as well as prolonged environmental stress that continued into the Early Triassic.

59eceb3525c7.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
59eceb3525c7.sentence: Seafloor communities maintained comparatively low diversity until the end of the Early Triassic, approximately 4-million years after the extinction event.

7f8aa5d0da4d.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
7f8aa5d0da4d.sentence: Continual episodes of extremely hot climatic conditions during the Early Triassic have been held responsible for the delayed recovery of oceanic life, in particular skeletonized taxa that are most vulnerable to high carbon dioxide concentrations.

d285924c3e8e.title: Permian
d285924c3e8e.sentence: It took well into the Triassic for life to recover from this catastrophe; on land, ecosystems took 30 million years to recover.

39ba5fe21ca3.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
39ba5fe21ca3.section: Hypotheses about cause > Hypercapnia and acidification
39ba5fe21ca3.sentence: As with many other environmental stressors, acidity on land episodically persisted well into the Triassic, stunting the recovery of terrestrial ecosystems.

041be95b6077.title: Guadalupian
041be95b6077.sentence: Estimates of recovery time vary, where some authors indicated recovery was prolonged, lasting 30 million years into the Triassic.

3876d846dbb0.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
3876d846dbb0.sentence: Land vertebrates took an unusually long time to recover from the P–Tr extinction, taking until the Middle Triassic; paleontologist Michael Benton estimated the recovery was not complete until 30 million years after the extinction, i.e. not until the Late Triassic, when the first dinosaurs had risen from bipedal archosaurian ancestors and the first mammals from small cynodont ancestors.

e097031373bc.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
e097031373bc.sentence: That recovery was slow in the Early Triassic can be explained by low levels of biological competition due to the paucity of taxonomic diversity, and that biotic recovery explosively accelerated in the Anisian can be explained by niche crowding, a phenomenon that would have drastically increased competition, becoming prevalent by the Anisian.

a205ae9b2d76.title: Mesozoic
a205ae9b2d76.sentence: Temnospondyls reached peak diversity during the early Triassic.

15a797569103.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
15a797569103.sentence: During the Induan, tupilakosaurids in particular thrived as disaster taxa, including Tupilakosaurus itself, though they gave way to other temnospondyls as ecosystems recovered.

b48a03287989.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
b48a03287989.sentence: Temnospondyls were reduced in size during the Induan, but their body size rebounded to pre-PTME levels during the Olenekian.

22ec65c99134.title: Triassic
22ec65c99134.sentence: Eustatic sea level in the Triassic was consistently low compared to the other geological periods.

da1897f90543.title: Triassic
da1897f90543.sentence: The beginning of the Triassic was around present sea level, rising to about 10–20 metres (33–66 ft) above present-day sea level during the Early and Middle Triassic.

e21f821721f8.title: Triassic
e21f821721f8.sentence: Sea level rise accelerated in the Ladinian, culminating with a sea level up to 50 metres (164 ft) above present-day levels during the Carnian.

313c94c087ca.title: Triassic
313c94c087ca.sentence: Three therapsid groups survived into the Triassic: dicynodonts, therocephalians, and cynodonts.

0faa806bd1e0.title: Triassic
0faa806bd1e0.sentence: Therapsids, the dominant vertebrates of the preceding Permian period, saw a brief surge in diversification in the Triassic, with dicynodonts and cynodonts quickly becoming dominant, but they declined throughout the period with the majority becoming extinct by the end.

f4a8dbcb5593.title: Triassic
f4a8dbcb5593.sentence: The cynodont Cynognathus was a characteristic top predator in the Olenekian and Anisian of Gondwana.

394a05b13ca4.title: Triassic
394a05b13ca4.sentence: Avemetatarsalians were a minor component of their ecosystems, but eventually produced the earliest pterosaurs and dinosaurs in the Late Triassic.

7cd410c6bb56.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
7cd410c6bb56.sentence: Around the Induan-Olenekian boundary, as paleocommunities recovered, a new Dicroidium flora was established, in which Umkomasiales continued to be prominent and in which Equisetales and Cycadales were subordinate forms.

bc6e72b95cc8.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
bc6e72b95cc8.sentence: The Dicroidium flora further diversified in the Anisian to its peak, wherein Umkomasiales and Ginkgoales constituted most of the tree canopy and Peltaspermales, Petriellales, Cycadales, Umkomasiales, Gnetales, Equisetales, and Dipteridaceae dominated the undergrowth.

1399f8a1f383.title: Jurassic
1399f8a1f383.sentence: Dicroidium, a corystosperm seed fern that was a dominant part of Gondwanan floral communities during the Triassic, also declined at the Triassic–Jurassic boundary, surviving as a relict in Antarctica into the Early Jurassic.

0f64936d79eb.title: Triassic
0f64936d79eb.sentence: The first Lissamphibians (modern amphibians) appear in the Triassic, with the progenitors of the first frogs already present by the Early Triassic.

922bff68a9a3.title: Tetrapod
922bff68a9a3.sentence: Temnospondyls briefly recovered in the Triassic, spawning the large aquatic stereospondyls and the small terrestrial lissamphibians (the earliest frogs, salamanders, and caecilians).

a4b0e0b5cf88.title: Jurassic
a4b0e0b5cf88.sentence: While the earliest salamander-line amphibians are known from the Triassic, crown group salamanders first appear during the Middle to Late Jurassic in Eurasia, alongside stem-group relatives.

177db94c02f7.title: Triassic
177db94c02f7.sentence: By the Middle Triassic, some ichthyopterygians were achieving very large body masses.

ff07928fb745.title: Triassic
ff07928fb745.sentence: Collisions between Annamia and South China (c. 246-230 Ma); between Sibumasu and South China–Annamia (c. 240-230 Ma); and, between Qiangtang and Lhasa (c. 250–230 Ma) resulted in the Indosinian orogeny and the formation of a single large Eastern Asian continent.

b9966e8dc4c9.title: Triassic
b9966e8dc4c9.sentence: South China collided with North China (c. 220 Ma), forming the Central China orogenic belt.

c3624bc555df.title: Triassic
c3624bc555df.sentence: At about the same time (c. 240-230 Ma), the final closure of the Paleoasian Ocean led to the collision of Tarim and North China with the Kazakhstan and Siberian regions of Pangea, to form the Central Asian orogenic belt.

c653e5f98d13.title: Triassic
c653e5f98d13.sentence: North China and Amuria, and South China were separated from Pangea by the Paleoasian Ocean, but this closed by the Late Triassic.

f83467fe9c20.title: Triassic
f83467fe9c20.sentence: The amalgamation of these East Asian blocks with Pangea in the Late Triassic maximised the land area of the supercontinent.

844041f5f877.title: Triassic
844041f5f877.sentence: It coincided with a period of dramatic climate change and the development of the megamonsoon, although the relationship between these is the subject of ongoing research.

855a0d670c1b.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
855a0d670c1b.sentence: Other explanations state that life was delayed in its recovery because grim conditions returned periodically over the course of the Early Triassic, causing further extinction events, such as the Smithian-Spathian boundary extinction.

6fab955f33b2.title: Extinction event
6fab955f33b2.section: Causes > Most widely supported explanations > Flood basalt events
6fab955f33b2.sentence: It is speculated that massive volcanism caused or contributed to the Kellwasser Event, the End-Guadalupian Extinction Event, the End-Permian Extinction Event, the Smithian-Spathian Extinction, the Triassic-Jurassic Extinction Event, the Toarcian Oceanic Anoxic Event, the Cenomanian-Turonian Oceanic Anoxic Event, also known as Bonarelli Event, the Cretaceous-Palaeogene Extinction Event, and the Palaeocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum.

773ffb49039b.title: Triassic
773ffb49039b.sentence: During the Latest Olenekian Cooling (LOC), from 248 to 247 Ma, temperatures cooled by about 6 °C.

20686905d983.title: Triassic
20686905d983.sentence: The Middle Triassic was cooler than the Early Triassic, with temperatures falling over most of the Anisian, with the exception of a warming spike in the latter portion of the stage.

63c9a4ac7d6f.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
63c9a4ac7d6f.sentence: Metazoan reefs became common again during the Anisian because the oceans cooled down then from their overheated state during the Early Triassic.

409e5d9bea5d.title: Triassic
409e5d9bea5d.section: Paleogeography > Opening of the Central Atlantic
409e5d9bea5d.sentence: Extension began in the northern Central Atlantic region in the Anisian, and in the southern Central Atlantic in the Carnian.

06f34900d24e.title: Triassic
06f34900d24e.sentence: Further south, during the Norian, the opening of the Central Atlantic led to the formation of narrow, deep water basins in the Eastern Mediterranean area.

5ff6058dc6d6.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
5ff6058dc6d6.sentence: The first scleractinian corals also appear in the late Anisian, although they would not become the dominant reef builders until the end of the Triassic period.

2a2b1466dbf7.title: Late Devonian mass extinction
2a2b1466dbf7.sentence: Mesozoic and modern reefs are based on scleractinian ("stony") corals, which would not evolve until the Triassic period.

b62e03948b2e.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
b62e03948b2e.sentence: Archosaurs (which included the ancestors of dinosaurs and crocodilians) were initially rarer than therapsids, but they began to displace therapsids in the mid-Triassic.

213c8259570a.title: History of life
213c8259570a.sentence: During the slow recovery from this catastrophe, estimated to have taken 30 million years, a previously obscure sauropsid group became the most abundant and diverse terrestrial vertebrates: a few fossils of archosauriformes ("ruling lizard forms") have been found in Late Permian rocks, but, by the Middle Triassic, archosaurs were the dominant land vertebrates.

a6cfe74ce2e8.title: Mammal
a6cfe74ce2e8.sentence: In the early Triassic, most medium to large land carnivore niches were taken over by archosaurs which, over an extended period (35 million years), came to include the crocodylomorphs, the pterosaurs and the dinosaurs; however, large cynodonts like Trucidocynodon and traversodontids still occupied large sized carnivorous and herbivorous niches respectively.

da2b141d6f88.title: Triassic
da2b141d6f88.sentence: Pseudosuchians were far more ecologically dominant in the Triassic, including large herbivores (such as aetosaurs), large carnivores ("rauisuchians"), and the first crocodylomorphs ("sphenosuchians").

9bf777dc7015.title: Jurassic
9bf777dc7015.sentence: On land, the fauna transitioned from the Triassic fauna, dominated jointly by dinosauromorph and pseudosuchian archosaurs to one dominated by dinosaurs alone.

0aa999c6a320.title: Dinoflagellate
0aa999c6a320.sentence: Dinoflagellates are mainly represented as fossils by dinocysts, which have a long geological record with lowest occurrences during the mid-Triassic, whilst geochemical markers suggest a presence to the Early Cambrian.

705fc9fcf4d8.title: Dinoflagellate
705fc9fcf4d8.sentence: Dinoflagellates show a classic radiation of morphologies during the Late Triassic through the Middle Jurassic.

acc516ab3170.title: Jurassic
acc516ab3170.sentence: Coccolithophores and dinoflagellates, which had first appeared during the Triassic, radiated during the Early to Middle Jurassic, becoming prominent members of the phytoplankton.

6e387421cdbf.title: Triassic
6e387421cdbf.sentence: These included the Sauropterygia, which featured pachypleurosaurs and nothosaurs (both common during the Middle Triassic, especially in the Tethys region), placodonts, the earliest known herbivorous marine reptile Atopodentatus, and the first plesiosaurs.

d7311a77d378.title: Mesozoic
d7311a77d378.sentence: Recent research indicates that it took much longer for the reestablishment of complex ecosystems with high biodiversity, complex food webs, and specialized animals in a variety of niches, beginning in the Middle Triassic 4 million to 6 million years after the extinction, and not fully proliferated until 30 million years after the extinction.

a2c4fdb5263a.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
a2c4fdb5263a.section: Hypotheses about cause > Methane clathrate gasification
a2c4fdb5263a.sentence: This is the first, largest, and fastest of a series of excursions (decreases and increases) in the ratio, until it abruptly stabilised in the middle Triassic, followed soon afterwards by the recovery of calcifying shelled sealife.

dca462531551.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
dca462531551.sentence: Though their taxonomic diversity remained relatively low, crinoids regained much of their ecological dominance by the Middle Triassic epoch.

1f28f6cff047.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
1f28f6cff047.sentence: Coprolitic evidence indicates that freshwater food webs had recovered by the early Ladinian, with a lacustrine coprolite assemblage from the Ordos Basin of China providing evidence of a trophically multileveled ecosystem containing at least six different trophic levels.

576a4872595d.title: Permian–Triassic extinction event
576a4872595d.sentence: Whereas most marine communities were fully recovered by the Middle Triassic, global marine diversity reached pre-extinction values no earlier than the Middle Jurassic, approximately 75-million years after the extinction event.

094133553b5b.title: Mesozoic
094133553b5b.sentence: The Middle Triassic (247 to 237 Ma) featured the beginnings of the breakup of Pangaea and the opening of the Tethys Ocean.

19e3a5fe3b76.title: Triassic
19e3a5fe3b76.sentence: The Monte San Giorgio lagerstätte, now in the Lake Lugano region of northern Italy and southern Switzerland, was in Middle Triassic times a lagoon behind reefs with an anoxic bottom layer, so there were no scavengers and little turbulence to disturb fossilization, a situation that can be compared to the better-known Jurassic Solnhofen Limestone lagerstätte.

18bf12ef005a.title: Triassic
18bf12ef005a.sentence: The remains of fish and various marine reptiles (including the common pachypleurosaur Neusticosaurus, and the bizarre long-necked archosauromorph Tanystropheus), along with some terrestrial forms like Ticinosuchus and Macrocnemus, have been recovered from this locality.

1b7f43930ca7.title: Triassic
1b7f43930ca7.sentence: All these fossils date from the Anisian and Ladinian ages (about 242 Ma ago).

ba4bae5e59a1.title: Triassic
ba4bae5e59a1.sentence: From 242 to 233 Ma, the Ladinian-Carnian Cooling (LCC) ensued.

76e80e225bae.title: Triassic
76e80e225bae.sentence: At the beginning of the Carnian, global temperatures continued to be relatively cool.

6683e233dbc5.title: Triassic
6683e233dbc5.sentence: The eruption of the Wrangellia Large Igneous Province around 234 Ma caused abrupt global warming, terminating the cooling trend of the LCC.

eef45a110350.title: Triassic
eef45a110350.sentence: As they drifted northwards through the Triassic, the Paleo-Tethys closed in front of them, and the Neotethys opened behind.

55ab0d344662.title: Triassic
55ab0d344662.sentence: The western Paleo-Tethys remained open until about 205 Ma, when the Iranian blocks collided with the Turan platform, on the southern margin of Eurasia, resulting in the Cimmerian orogeny.

e87e3f748728.title: Triassic
e87e3f748728.sentence: This extended from the Anatolian Plateau in the northwest, and merged with the Indosinian orogenic belt in the east.

8c21527df8be.title: Geologic time scale
8c21527df8be.sentence: Phanerozoic | Mesozoic | Triassic | Upper/Late | Rhaetian | Pangaea forms an arc extending from almost pole to pole. Siberian Traps eruptions wane, but hot house climate continues. Cimmerian terranes collide with Eurasia: Indosinian orogeny in east; Cimmerian orogeny in west. Sonoma (western Laurussia), and Hunter-Bowen (Australia) orogenies continue. Late Triassic, emplacement of the Central Atlantic magmatic province (CAMP) followed by seafloor spreading marks start of Pangaea break up. Archosaurs divide into pseudosuchia (crocodiles), and ornithodirans (dinosaurs and pterosaurs). Mammaliaformes evolve from cynodonts. Evidence of endothermy (warm-bloodedness) in dinosaurs and mammals. First teleosts (modern ray-finned fish). Ichthyosaurs, and sauropterygians plesiosaurs, nothosaurs, placodonts) appear. First scleractinian (hard coral) reefs. First wasps and stick insects. Late Triassic eruptions of Wrangellia LIP raises temperatures, intensifies Pangaea monsoons and increases rainfall (Carnian pluvial episode). Bennettitales, modern ferns and conifers appear. First Lepidoptera (moths and butterflies). Modern groups of phytoplankton appear. Manicouagan bolide impact reduces global temperatures, before CAMP eruptions increases them and triggers Triassic-Jurassic mass extinction. Major loss of reef ecosystems, reduction in marine genera, conodonts die out. Major changes in terrestrial flora. Loss of vertebrate genera, including non-mammalian therapsids. Crocodylomorphs only pseudosuchians to survive. | ~205.7

213e14a6bfc2.title: Himalayas
213e14a6bfc2.sentence: Qiangtang, a geological region in what is today northern Tibet, had done so in Late Triassic (237–201 Mya).

921ccffc587c.title: Jurassic
921ccffc587c.sentence: The oldest known lepidopterans (the group containing butterflies and moths) are known from the Triassic–Jurassic boundary, with wing scales belonging to the suborder Glossata and Micropterigidae-grade moths from the deposits of this age in Germany.

7aaaf191f687.title: Jurassic
7aaaf191f687.sentence: As part of the Nevadan orogeny, which began during the Triassic, the Cache Creek Ocean closed, and various terranes including the large Wrangellia Terrane accreted onto the western margin of North America.

6e5ca529e09e.title: Triassic
6e5ca529e09e.sentence: This warming was responsible for the Carnian Pluvial Event and resulted in an episode of widespread global humidity.

fa5a9313aeab.title: Triassic
fa5a9313aeab.sentence: The best-studied of such episodes of humid climate, and probably the most intense and widespread, was the Carnian Pluvial Event.

479613757bd2.title: Triassic
479613757bd2.sentence: A specialized group of archosaurs, called dinosaurs, first appeared in the Late Triassic but did not become dominant until the succeeding Jurassic Period.

254b8d97fd59.title: Jurassic
254b8d97fd59.sentence: Quadrupedal sauropomorphs appeared during the Late Triassic.

f7f8b8981353.title: Triassic
f7f8b8981353.sentence: Triassic dinosaurs evolved in the Carnian and include early sauropodomorphs and theropods.

8fb41ca767ad.title: Jurassic
8fb41ca767ad.sentence: Advanced theropods belonging to Neotheropoda first appeared in the Late Triassic.

af53f3302372.title: Triassic
af53f3302372.sentence: Early long-tailed pterosaurs appeared in the Norian and quickly spread worldwide.

9657cf2bd891.title: Triassic
9657cf2bd891.sentence: It seems likely then that there was some sort of end-Carnian extinction, when several herbivorous archosauromorph groups died out, while the large herbivorous therapsids—the kannemeyeriid dicynodonts and the traversodont cynodonts—were much reduced in the northern half of Pangaea (Laurasia).

eda2b5c48e6d.title: Triassic
eda2b5c48e6d.sentence: At the end of the Carnian, a reef crisis occurred in South China.

4d40af96e9f7.title: Jurassic
4d40af96e9f7.sentence: Rhynchocephalians (the sole living representative being the tuatara) had achieved a global distribution by the beginning of the Jurassic, and represented the dominant group of small reptiles during the Jurassic globally.

70c3dcfb0b3f.title: Triassic
70c3dcfb0b3f.sentence: In the Petrified Forest of northeast Arizona there is a unique sequence of late Carnian-early Norian terrestrial sediments.

f6aedda88328.title: Triassic
f6aedda88328.sentence: Most Triassic dinosaurs were small predators and only a few were common, such as Coelophysis, which was 1 to 2 metres (3.3 to 6.6 ft) long.

4fe2ef1f0668.title: Triassic
4fe2ef1f0668.sentence: Sea level began to decline in the Norian, reaching a low of 50 metres (164 ft) below present sea level during the mid-Rhaetian.

11d307919b8e.title: Triassic
11d307919b8e.sentence: Low global sea levels persisted into the earliest Jurassic.

255341c669ce.title: Triassic
255341c669ce.sentence: A lack of evidence for Triassic continental ice sheets suggest that glacial eustasy is unlikely to be the cause of these changes.

1ff0bf07c750.title: Jurassic
1ff0bf07c750.sentence: At the end of the Triassic, there was a marine transgression in Europe, flooding most parts of central and western Europe transforming it into an archipelago of islands surrounded by shallow seas.

fc17209bbc29.title: Mesozoic
fc17209bbc29.sentence: During the Late Triassic, some advanced cynodonts gave rise to the first Mammaliaformes.

5f042b8936f4.title: Triassic
5f042b8936f4.sentence: During the Carnian (early part of the Late Triassic), some advanced cynodonts gave rise to the first mammals.

615ed7cc19fc.title: History of life
615ed7cc19fc.sentence: While the archosaurs and dinosaurs were becoming more dominant in the Triassic, the mammaliaform successors of the therapsids evolved into small, mainly nocturnal insectivores.

a6e76adc39a9.title: History of Earth
a6e76adc39a9.sentence: The first true mammals evolved in the shadows of dinosaurs and other large archosaurs that filled the world by the late Triassic.

086f99d090af.title: Mammal
086f99d090af.sentence: - The dentary gradually became the main bone of the lower jaw which, by the Triassic, progressed towards the fully mammalian jaw (the lower consisting only of the dentary) and middle ear (which is constructed by the bones that were previously used to construct the jaws of reptiles).

248cfabf7021.title: Jurassic
248cfabf7021.sentence: Mammaliaformes, including mammals, having originated from cynodonts at the end of the Triassic, diversified extensively during the Jurassic.

173e1f267b03.title: Triassic
173e1f267b03.sentence: From 227 to 217 Ma, there was a relatively cool period known as the Early Norian Cool Interval (ENCI), after which occurred the Mid-Norian Warm Interval (MNWI) from 217 to 209 Ma.

5a0fd35432ab.title: Triassic
5a0fd35432ab.sentence: The CPE ushered in the Mid-Carnian Warm Interval (MCWI), which lasted from 234 to 227 Ma.

3184e807fa5b.title: Triassic
3184e807fa5b.sentence: At the Carnian-Norian boundary occurred a positive δ13C excursion believed to signify an increase in organic carbon burial.

c61adb500cc1.title: Jurassic
c61adb500cc1.sentence: Stem-group teleosts, which make up over 99% of living Actinopterygii, had first appeared during the Triassic in the western Tethys; they underwent a major diversification beginning in the Late Jurassic, with early representatives of modern teleost clades such as Elopomorpha and Osteoglossoidei appearing during this time.

4c57b76345cf.title: Triassic
4c57b76345cf.sentence: The MNWI was briefly interrupted around 214 Ma by a cooling possibly related to the Manicouagan impact.

b5844419de99.title: Triassic
b5844419de99.sentence: Around 212 Ma, a 10 Myr eccentricity maximum caused a paludification of Pangaea and a reduction in the size of arid climatic zones.

176afd508146.title: Triassic
176afd508146.sentence: Among other reptiles, the earliest turtles, like Proganochelys and Proterochersis, appeared during the Norian Age (Stage) of the Late Triassic Period.

220be155e236.title: Triassic
220be155e236.sentence: The Rhaetian Cool Interval (RCI) lasted from 209 to 201 Ma.

5d812670af86.title: Triassic
5d812670af86.sentence: At the terminus of the Triassic, there was an extreme warming event referred to as the End-Triassic Thermal Event (ETTE), which was responsible for the Triassic-Jurassic mass extinction.

273ae78d0c29.title: Jurassic
273ae78d0c29.sentence: Plesiosaurs originated at the end of the Triassic (Rhaetian).

3f7cc451595f.title: Jurassic
3f7cc451595f.sentence: At least six lineages of plesiosaur crossed the Triassic–Jurassic boundary.

8b41b20c4bd2.title: Triassic
8b41b20c4bd2.sentence: It was accompanied by huge volcanic eruptions that occurred as the supercontinent Pangaea began to break apart about 202 to 191 million years ago (40Ar/39Ar dates), forming the Central Atlantic Magmatic Province (CAMP), one of the largest known inland volcanic events since the planet had first cooled and stabilized.

ccef7d984354.title: Triassic
ccef7d984354.section: Paleogeography > Opening of the Central Atlantic
ccef7d984354.sentence: The period of rifting came to an end with the emplacement of the Central Atlantic Magmatic Province (CAMP) around 201 Ma.

8aeba4716ef1.title: Triassic
8aeba4716ef1.sentence: Bubbles of carbon dioxide in basaltic rocks dating back to the end of the Triassic indicate that volcanic activity from the Central Atlantic Magmatic Province helped trigger climate change in the ETTE.

82be8dd4368d.title: Triassic
82be8dd4368d.section: Paleogeography > Opening of the Central Atlantic
82be8dd4368d.sentence: This was followed by longer-term climate warming and ocean acidification, which caused the end-Triassic mass extinction.

94cce17fedcf.title: Jurassic
94cce17fedcf.sentence: The beginning of the Jurassic was likely marked by a thermal spike corresponding to the Triassic–Jurassic extinction and eruption of the Central Atlantic magmatic province.

03d093f9eb2e.title: Jurassic
03d093f9eb2e.sentence: During the end-Triassic extinction, 46%–72% of all marine genera became extinct.

ee04e89b7172.title: Mesozoic
ee04e89b7172.sentence: The period is bracketed between the Permian–Triassic extinction event and the Triassic–Jurassic extinction event, two of the "big five", and it is divided into three major epochs: Early, Middle, and Late Triassic.

267f563c711c.title: Mesozoic
267f563c711c.sentence: All this climatic change, however, resulted in a large die-out known as the Triassic–Jurassic extinction event, in which many archosaurs (excluding pterosaurs, dinosaurs and crocodylomorphs), most synapsids, and almost all large amphibians became extinct, as well as 34% of marine life, in the Earth's fourth mass extinction event.

24dc856a3cb4.title: Triassic
24dc856a3cb4.sentence: Though the end-Triassic extinction event was not equally devastating in all terrestrial ecosystems, several important clades of crurotarsans (large archosaurian reptiles previously grouped together as the thecodonts) disappeared, as did most of the large labyrinthodont amphibians, groups of small reptiles, and most synapsids.

fe03861ecfd9.title: Jurassic
fe03861ecfd9.sentence: The start of the Jurassic was marked by the major Triassic–Jurassic extinction event, associated with the eruption of the Central Atlantic Magmatic Province (CAMP).

7a110121ca13.title: Extinction event
7a110121ca13.sentence: The dinosaurs themselves had been beneficiaries of a previous mass extinction, the end-Triassic, which eliminated most of their chief rivals, the crurotarsans.

49dd113e3a43.title: Triassic
49dd113e3a43.sentence: The end of the period was marked by yet another major mass extinction, the Triassic–Jurassic extinction event, that wiped out many groups, including most pseudosuchians, and allowed dinosaurs to assume dominance in the Jurassic.

7b09912ccdac.title: Ocean acidification
7b09912ccdac.section: Measured and estimated values > Geologic past
7b09912ccdac.sentence: The end-Triassic biotic crisis is still the most well-established example of a marine mass extinction due to ocean acidification, because (a) carbon isotope records suggest enhanced volcanic activity that decreased the carbonate sedimentation which reduced the carbonate compensation depth and the carbonate saturation state, and a marine extinction coincided precisely in the stratigraphic record, and (b) there was pronounced selectivity of the extinction against organisms with thick aragonitic skeletons, which is predicted from experimental studies.

e9e786916a98.title: Ocean acidification
e9e786916a98.section: Measured and estimated values > Geologic past
e9e786916a98.sentence: Decreased CaCO3 saturation due to seawater uptake of volcanogenic CO2 has been suggested as a possible kill mechanism during the marine mass extinction at the end of the Triassic.

29a4b320ba3c.title: Pennsylvanian (geology)
