94c5b1c6ea31.title: Cretaceous
94c5b1c6ea31.sentence: Beginning in the Santonian, near the end of the MKH, the global climate began to cool, with this cooling trend continuing across the Campanian.

2cce00b09516.title: Cretaceous
2cce00b09516.sentence: Tropical SSTs declined from around 35 °C in the early Campanian to around 28 °C in the Maastrichtian.

fc4728ab6348.title: Mesozoic
fc4728ab6348.sentence: The Late Cretaceous (100.5 to 66 Ma) featured a cooling trend that would continue in the Cenozoic Era.

892de75c4690.title: Extinction event
892de75c4690.section: Causes > Most widely supported explanations > Sea-level fall
892de75c4690.sentence: Sea-level falls are associated with most of the mass extinctions, including all of the "Big Five"—End-Ordovician, Late Devonian, End-Permian, End-Triassic, and End-Cretaceous, along with the more recently recognised Capitanian mass extinction of comparable severity to the Big Five.

f33e2e3b524f.title: Bird
f33e2e3b524f.section: Evolution and classification > Diversification of modern birds
f33e2e3b524f.sentence: The discovery in 2005 of Vegavis from the Maastrichtian, the last stage of the Late Cretaceous, proved that the diversification of modern birds started before the Cenozoic era.

d9f8855ce44d.title: Bird
d9f8855ce44d.section: Evolution and classification > Diversification of modern birds
d9f8855ce44d.sentence: In 2020, Asteriornis from the Maastrichtian was described, it appears to be a close relative of Galloanserae, the earliest diverging lineage within Neognathae.

9723890c2204.title: Cretaceous
9723890c2204.sentence: - The latter warming interval, occurring at the very end of the Cretaceous, was triggered by the activity of the Deccan Traps.

26a42a0fa28f.title: History of Earth
26a42a0fa28f.sentence: In 66 Ma, a 10-kilometer (6.2 mi) asteroid struck Earth just off the Yucatán Peninsula—somewhere in the southwestern tip of then Laurasia—where the Chicxulub crater is today.

4c2cc9dda0c0.title: Extinction event
4c2cc9dda0c0.section: Causes > Most widely supported explanations > Extraterrestrial threats > Impact events
4c2cc9dda0c0.sentence: Nonetheless, in October 2019, researchers reported that the Cretaceous Chicxulub asteroid impact that resulted in the extinction of non-avian dinosaurs 66 Ma, also rapidly acidified the oceans, producing ecological collapse and long-lasting effects on the climate, and was a key reason for end-Cretaceous mass extinction.

a310209d670c.title: History of Earth
a310209d670c.sentence: The fifth and most recent mass extinction was the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event.

b3bce2711b1b.title: Extinction event
b3bce2711b1b.sentence: The end-Cretaceous mass extinction removed the non-avian dinosaurs and made it possible for mammals to expand into the large terrestrial vertebrate niches.

fbb165b92239.title: Extinction
fbb165b92239.sentence: The Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event (K–Pg) occurred 66 million years ago, at the end of the Cretaceous period; it is best known for having wiped out non-avian dinosaurs, among many other species.

ea4b25afe315.title: Cretaceous
ea4b25afe315.sentence: The Cretaceous (along with the Mesozoic) ended with the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event, a large mass extinction in which many groups, including non-avian dinosaurs, pterosaurs, and large marine reptiles, died out; it is widely thought to have been caused by the impact of a large asteroid that formed the Chicxulub crater in the Gulf of Mexico.

4df8f968a6d1.title: Cenozoic
4df8f968a6d1.sentence: The Paleogene spans from the extinction of non-avian dinosaurs, 66 million years ago, to the dawn of the Neogene, 23.03 million years ago.

0e3dae012f5a.title: History of life
0e3dae012f5a.sentence: After the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event 66 Ma killed off the non-avian dinosaurs, mammals increased rapidly in size and diversity.

62cfffac4cfd.title: Mammal
62cfffac4cfd.sentence: Mammals achieved their modern diversity in the Paleogene and Neogene periods of the Cenozoic era, after the extinction of non-avian dinosaurs, and have been the dominant terrestrial animal group from 66 million years ago to the present.

8061e6dc2db3.title: Impact event
8061e6dc2db3.sentence: The prehistoric Chicxulub impact, 66 million years ago, is believed to be the cause not only of the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event but acceleration of the evolution of mammals, leading to their dominance and, in turn, setting in place conditions for the eventual rise of humans.

50fbbdc7e063.title: Mammal
50fbbdc7e063.sentence: The earliest undisputed fossils of placentals come from the early Paleocene, after the extinction of the non-avian dinosaurs.

f4e3fe5ff627.title: Himalayas
f4e3fe5ff627.sentence: Before the India-Eurasia collision in Middle Paleocene (60 Mya) and subsequent Himalayan orogeny, two other landmasses, the Qiangtang terrane and Lhasa terrane, had drifted up from Gondwana.

1c46f2c8ce6e.title: Ice sheet
1c46f2c8ce6e.section: In geologic timescales > Antarctic ice sheet during geologic timescales
1c46f2c8ce6e.sentence: The icing of Antarctica began in the Late Palaeocene or middle Eocene between 60 and 45.5 million years ago and escalated during the Eocene–Oligocene extinction event about 34 million years ago.

7afc913b0ec3.title: Impact event
7afc913b0ec3.section: Impacts and the Earth > Earth impacts in history > Cenozoic > Paleogene
7afc913b0ec3.sentence: Analysis of the Hiawatha Glacier reveals the presence of a 31 km wide impact crater dated at 58 million years of age, less than 10 million years after the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event, scientists believe that the impactor was a metallic asteroid with a diameter in the order of 1.5 kilometres (0.93 miles).

0c48c22bbde0.title: Abrupt climate change
0c48c22bbde0.sentence: By contrast, the Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum may have initiated anywhere between a few decades and several thousand years.

4e7274f57e88.title: Extinction event
4e7274f57e88.section: Causes > Most widely supported explanations > Global warming
4e7274f57e88.sentence: The most dramatic example of sustained warming is the Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum, which was associated with one of the smaller mass extinctions.

f52068076566.title: Eocene
f52068076566.sentence: At about the beginning of the Eocene Epoch (55.8–33.9 Ma) the amount of oxygen in the Earth's atmosphere more or less doubled.

92bfca29c119.title: Eocene
92bfca29c119.sentence: At the beginning of the Eocene, several new mammal groups arrived in North America.

a8df45bf148e.title: Eocene
a8df45bf148e.sentence: The oldest known fossils of most of the modern mammal orders appear within a brief period during the early Eocene.

26bf90d2c7b0.title: Eocene
26bf90d2c7b0.sentence: These modern mammals, like artiodactyls, perissodactyls, and primates, had features like long, thin legs, feet, and hands capable of grasping, as well as differentiated teeth adapted for chewing.

690002d7cace.title: Eocene
690002d7cace.sentence: All the members of the new mammal orders were small, under 10 kg; based on comparisons of tooth size, Eocene mammals were only 60% of the size of the primitive Palaeocene mammals that preceded them.

6ef50af00b40.title: Eocene
6ef50af00b40.sentence: Several rich fossil insect faunas are known from the Eocene, notably the Baltic amber found mainly along the south coast of the Baltic Sea, amber from the Paris Basin, France, the Fur Formation, Denmark, and the Bembridge Marls from the Isle of Wight, England.

386307da6e14.title: Mammal
386307da6e14.sentence: The earliest-known ancestor of primates is Archicebus achilles from around 55 million years ago.

6c3b0c9013db.title: Geologic time scale
6c3b0c9013db.sentence: Phanerozoic | Cenozoic | Paleogene | Eocene | Ypresian | Greenland separates from Eurasia and Eurasian Basin opens in Arctic. Greater India collides with southern Eurasia, beginning Himalayan orogeny. North Atlantic LIP eruptions continue. Major reorganisation of plate motions across Pacific region initiates Izu-Bonin-Mariana and Tonga-Kermadec subduction zones. Greenhouse temperatures continue from Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum (PETM) as climate affected by North Atlantic LIP eruptions, but global cooling begins from about 50 Ma with changing paleogeography and oceanography conditions. Angiosperms (flowering plants) evolve larger fruits. First songbirds, parrots and woodpeckers. Primates divide into strepsirrhines (lemurs and lorises) and haplorhines (tarsiers and anthropoids). Artiodactyls (even-toed ungulates) appear and split into Cetruminantia (ruminants, whales and dolphins), Suina (pigs), and Tylopoda (camels and relatives). First Carnivora (meat-eating mammals). Mice, rats, bats and tapirs appear. Eohippus earliest member of horse family. Marsupials reach Australia. | 56 *

df7e755bc34d.title: Eocene
df7e755bc34d.sentence: Many modern bird orders first appeared in the Eocene.

acd0a9d959fd.title: Tibetan Plateau
acd0a9d959fd.sentence: India began drifting northward from Gondwana in the Upper Cretaceous, about 70 million years ago (Mya), moving at about 15 cm (6 in) per year; its collision with the Eurasian plate is most commonly dated to around 55–50 Mya, near the Paleocene–Eocene boundary, though the exact timing remains debated.

cb87b28eee14.title: Himalayas
cb87b28eee14.sentence: The irregular northern margin of the Indian continental crust first came into contact with Eurasia along its northwestern corner, approximately 55 Ma.

94399467d693.title: Tibetan Plateau
94399467d693.sentence: By about 50 Mya, the fast-moving Indo-Australian plate had completely closed the Tethys Ocean, the existence of which has been determined by sedimentary rocks settled on the ocean floor and the volcanoes that fringed its edges.

84dea3512e81.title: Eocene
84dea3512e81.sentence: The incipient subcontinent collided with the Kohistan–Ladakh Arc around 50.2 Ma and with Karakoram around 40.4 Ma, with the final collision between Asia and India occurring ~40 Ma.

75210d2cc298.title: Oligocene
75210d2cc298.sentence: One recent hypothesis is that a separate microcontinent collided with south Asia in the early Eocene, and India itself did not collide with south Asia until the end of the Oligocene.

a44101539190.title: Eocene
a44101539190.sentence: These Early Eocene hyperthermals produced a sustained period of extremely hot climate known as the Early Eocene Climatic Optimum (EECO).

e270278ff6ee.title: Paleoclimatology
e270278ff6ee.sentence: The warmest climate state since the time of the dinosaur extinction, "Hothouse", endured from 56 Mya to 47 Mya and was ~14 °C warmer than average modern temperatures.

7f4139f7e69e.title: Oligocene
7f4139f7e69e.sentence: The early Eocene climate was very warm, with crocodilians and temperate plants thriving north of the Arctic Circle.

fb4e983c45ec.title: Eocene
fb4e983c45ec.sentence: Palm trees were growing as far north as Alaska and northern Europe during the early Eocene, although they became less abundant as the climate cooled.

7929f710c0a6.title: Eocene
7929f710c0a6.section: Climate > Early Eocene > Equable climate problem
7929f710c0a6.sentence: Using all different ranges of greenhouse gasses that occurred during the early Eocene, models were unable to produce the warming that was found at the poles and the reduced seasonality that occurs with winters at the poles being substantially warmer.

65f82eee16db.title: Eocene
65f82eee16db.sentence: The hyperthermals in the early Eocene, notably the Palaeocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum (PETM), the Eocene Thermal Maximum 2 (ETM2), and the Eocene Thermal Maximum 3 (ETM3), were analyzed and found that orbital control may have had a role in triggering the ETM2 and ETM3.

6d07a3347cb8.title: Eocene
6d07a3347cb8.sentence: Basilosaurus is a well-known Eocene whale, but whales as a group had become very diverse during the Eocene, which is when the major transitions from being terrestrial to fully aquatic in cetaceans occurred.

e03e983aa4ec.title: Paleontology
e03e983aa4ec.sentence: Discoveries within the Eocene of fossil mammals have allowed for the evolution of whales to be nearly completely understood, with the fully terrestrial mesonychids becoming gradually amphibious before becoming aquatic swimmers.

e7fced515563.title: Mammal
e7fced515563.sentence: For example, the earliest-known bat dates from about 50 million years ago, only 16 million years after the extinction of the non-avian dinosaurs.

7b08d9e72188.title: Eocene
7b08d9e72188.sentence: The transition from a warming climate into a cooling climate began at around 49 Ma.

61064bae612d.title: Eocene
61064bae612d.sentence: Cooling after this event, part of a trend known as the Middle-Late Eocene Cooling (MLEC), continued due to continual decrease in atmospheric carbon dioxide from organic productivity and weathering from mountain building.

d9eb934fcd34.title: Eocene
d9eb934fcd34.sentence: However, modeling results call into question the thermal isolation model for late Eocene cooling, and decreasing carbon dioxide levels in the atmosphere may have been more important.

fa9cd28fbcb0.title: Cenozoic
fa9cd28fbcb0.sentence: This epoch was marked by ice ages as a result of the cooling trend that started in the Mid-Eocene.

c1c6713101f7.title: Azolla event
c1c6713101f7.sentence: During the early Eocene, the continental configuration was such that the Arctic Sea was almost entirely cut off from the wider oceans.

32984de2b6ff.title: Eocene
32984de2b6ff.sentence: With the equable climate during the early Eocene, warm temperatures in the arctic allowed for the growth of azolla, which is a floating aquatic fern, on the Arctic Ocean.

f7580610b379.title: Eocene
f7580610b379.sentence: Compared to current carbon dioxide levels, these azolla grew rapidly in the enhanced carbon dioxide levels found in the early Eocene.

a177ff3f59b1.title: Azolla event
a177ff3f59b1.sentence: The plant can grow at great speed in favourable conditions – modest warmth and 20 hours of sunlight, both of which were in evidence at the poles during the early Eocene – and can double its biomass over two to three days in such a climate.

16e15d30ef46.title: Azolla event
16e15d30ef46.sentence: As the fern died and sank to the stagnant sea floor, it were incorporated into the sediment over a period of about 800,000 years; the resulting draw-down of carbon dioxide has been speculated to have helped reverse the planet from the "greenhouse Earth" state of the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum, when the planet was hot enough for turtles and palm trees to prosper at the poles, to the current icehouse Earth known as the Late Cenozoic Ice Age.

8ac847a41d6e.title: Azolla event
8ac847a41d6e.sentence: The event coincides precisely with a catastrophic decline in carbon dioxide levels, which fell from 3500 ppm in the early Eocene to 650 ppm during this event.

5dfcc24e87bc.title: Azolla event
5dfcc24e87bc.sentence: A geologically rapid decrease in temperature between 49 and 47 million years ago, around the Azolla event, is evident; dropstones (which are taken as evidence for the presence of glaciers) are common in Arctic sediments thereafter.

7bb3cd9f2e92.title: Rhine
7bb3cd9f2e92.sentence: From the Eocene onward, the ongoing Alpine orogeny caused a north–south rift system to develop in this zone.

380c0b44f00e.title: Eocene
380c0b44f00e.sentence: The newly evolved grasses began to expand during the climatic cooling and drying following the extreme warmth of the EECO, with subhumid savannas being known from South America since the Middle Eocene.

2c17f07daab6.title: Oligocene
2c17f07daab6.sentence: Open plains and deserts became more common and grasses expanded from their water-bank habitat in the Eocene moving out into open tracts.

abd9dd728d77.title: Eocene
abd9dd728d77.sentence: Fossils and even preserved remains of trees such as swamp cypress and dawn redwood from the Eocene have been found on Ellesmere Island in the Arctic.

dc4874d13b21.title: Eocene
dc4874d13b21.sentence: Fossils of subtropical and even tropical trees and plants from the Eocene also have been found in Greenland and Alaska.

527cc766de78.title: Eocene
527cc766de78.sentence: Pollen found in Prydz Bay from the Eocene suggest taiga forest existed there.

7ad709e212e4.title: Eocene
7ad709e212e4.sentence: When Australia split from the southern continent around 45 Ma, the warm equatorial currents were routed away from Antarctica, and an isolated cold water channel developed between the two continents.

5f7b7daa2191.title: Eocene
5f7b7daa2191.sentence: For Drake Passage, sediments indicate the opening occurred ~41 Ma while tectonics indicate that this occurred ~32 Ma.

8b7c5ccab0cc.title: Eocene
8b7c5ccab0cc.sentence: The cooling during the initial stages of the opening of the Drake Passage ~38.5 Ma was not global, as evidenced by an absence of cooling in the North Atlantic.

85ab27e90895.title: Eocene
85ab27e90895.sentence: This warming event, signifying a sudden and temporary reversal of the cooling conditions, is known as the Middle Eocene Climatic Optimum (MECO).

997d00b8715b.title: Eocene
997d00b8715b.sentence: The warming is considered to be primarily due to carbon dioxide increases, because carbon isotope signatures rule out major methane release during this short-term warming.

3d3b76d4d353.title: Eocene
3d3b76d4d353.sentence: A sharp increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide was observed with a maximum of 4,000 ppm: the highest amount of atmospheric carbon dioxide detected during the Eocene.

ab0101d67d55.title: Eocene
ab0101d67d55.sentence: Other studies suggest a more modest rise in carbon dioxide levels.

50fc0c037d36.title: Eocene
50fc0c037d36.sentence: Eurasia was separated in three different landmasses 50 Ma; Western Europe, Balkanatolia and Asia.

bdffa9b6c1eb.title: Eocene
bdffa9b6c1eb.sentence: About 40 Ma, Balkanatolia and Asia were connected, while Europe was connected 34 Ma.

3d1d6cae7a0a.title: Ring of Fire
3d1d6cae7a0a.section: North America > North American Cordillera > United States
3d1d6cae7a0a.sentence: Volcanism in the arc began about 37 million years ago, but most of the present-day Cascade volcanoes are less than 2 million years old, and the highest peaks are less than 100,000 years old.

25eabdb2c98f.title: Miocene
25eabdb2c98f.sentence: There is evidence from oxygen isotopes at Deep Sea Drilling Program sites that ice began to build up in Antarctica about 36 Ma during the Eocene.

c53f0ee5cf9e.title: Cenozoic
c53f0ee5cf9e.sentence: Around 35 million years ago, permanent ice began to build up on Antarctica.

9edf8975ec11.title: Eocene
9edf8975ec11.sentence: In western North America, the Laramide Orogeny came to an end in the Eocene, and compression was replaced with crustal extension that ultimately gave rise to the Basin and Range Province.

d49fd25b6dcc.title: Ring of Fire
d49fd25b6dcc.section: Tectonic plate configurations > Past plate configurations
d49fd25b6dcc.sentence: About 35 million years ago, the Kula and Farallon plates had been subducted and the Pacific plate was subducting around its rim in a configuration closely resembling the outline of the present-day Ring of Fire.

5dc12b287c55.title: Ring of Fire
5dc12b287c55.sentence: As plate configurations gradually changed, the current subduction zones of Indonesia and New Guinea were created (about 70 million years ago), followed finally by the New Zealand subduction zone (about 35 million years ago).

f8c729775732.title: Cenozoic
f8c729775732.sentence: India collided with Asia 55 to 45 million years ago creating the Himalayas; Arabia collided with Eurasia, closing the Tethys Ocean and creating the Zagros Mountains, around 35 million years ago.

0a43b205bacd.title: Eocene
0a43b205bacd.sentence: Cooling and the carbon dioxide drawdown continued through the late Eocene and into the Eocene–Oligocene transition around 34 Ma.

80d395592e96.title: Oligocene
80d395592e96.section: Climate > Eocene-Oligocene transition and Oi1 event
80d395592e96.sentence: Ice-rafted debris in the Norwegian-Greenland Sea indicated that glaciers had appeared in Greenland by the start of the Oligocene.

d7885ecf0de1.title: Eocene
d7885ecf0de1.sentence: The end is set at a major extinction event called the Grande Coupure (the "Great Break" in continuity) or the Eocene–Oligocene extinction event, which may be related to the impact of one or more large bolides in Siberia and in what is now Chesapeake Bay.

c84fc6636c3c.title: Cenozoic
c84fc6636c3c.sentence: The end of the Eocene was marked by the Eocene–Oligocene extinction event, the European face of which is known as the Grande Coupure.

467e96d83614.title: Eocene
467e96d83614.sentence: During this decrease, ice began to reappear at the poles, and the Eocene–Oligocene transition is the period of time when the Antarctic ice sheet began to rapidly expand.

08ec77501627.title: Eocene
08ec77501627.sentence: Multiple proxies, such as oxygen isotopes and alkenones, indicate that at the Eocene–Oligocene transition, the atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration had decreased to around 750–800 ppm, approximately twice that of present levels.

3a3879e696b1.title: Oligocene
3a3879e696b1.sentence: The cooling of central North America at the Eocene-Oligocene transition resulted in a large turnover of gastropods, amphibians, and reptiles.

f0da713ea5bc.title: Oligocene
f0da713ea5bc.section: Climate > Eocene-Oligocene transition and Oi1 event
f0da713ea5bc.sentence: The causes of the Eocene-Oligocene transition are not yet fully understood.

feceb7221fa8.title: Eocene
feceb7221fa8.sentence: The end of the Eocene and beginning of the Oligocene is marked with the massive expansion of area of the Antarctic ice sheet that was a major step into the icehouse climate.

fca0190ac5cc.title: Oligocene
fca0190ac5cc.sentence: The cooling trend that began in the middle Eocene continued into the Oligocene, bringing both poles well below freezing for the first time in the Phanerozoic.

dc6a0e7997df.title: Oligocene
dc6a0e7997df.sentence: The Alps were rapidly rising in Europe as the African plate continued to push north into the Eurasian plate, isolating the remnants of the Tethys Sea.

bf0d812a95cc.title: Oligocene
bf0d812a95cc.sentence: The Andes first became a major mountain chain in the Oligocene, as subduction became more direct into the coastline.

9147b20264f7.title: Oligocene
9147b20264f7.sentence: Carnivores such as dogs, nimravids, bears, weasels, and raccoons began to replace the creodonts that had dominated the Paleocene in the Old World.

69b4f74a8ab9.title: Oligocene
69b4f74a8ab9.sentence: Early desmostylians, like Behemotops, are known from the Oligocene.

0bcce6f6d02c.title: Oligocene
0bcce6f6d02c.sentence: Major changes during the Oligocene included a global expansion of grasslands, and a regression of tropical broad leaf forests to the equatorial belt.

630003e138e3.title: Miocene
630003e138e3.sentence: As in the Oligocene before it, grasslands continued to expand, and forests to dwindle.

640faab900e0.title: Oligocene
640faab900e0.sentence: The decline in pCO2 favored C4 photosynthesis, which is found only in angiosperms and is particularly characteristic of grasses.

ebc3920f97dc.title: Oligocene
ebc3920f97dc.sentence: However, even at the end of the period, grass was not quite common enough for modern savannas.

cc8d31135ae9.title: Oligocene
cc8d31135ae9.sentence: The Obik Sea, which had separated Europe from Asia, retreated early in the Oligocene, creating a persistent land connection between the continents.

843b1e252795.title: Oligocene
843b1e252795.sentence: The lowering of sea levels closed the Turgai Strait across the Obik Sea, which had previously separated Asia from Europe.

38451ed324ce.title: Oligocene
38451ed324ce.sentence: This allowed Asian mammals, such as rhinoceroses and ruminants, to enter Europe and drive endemic species to extinction.

b9d5469652a6.title: Oligocene
b9d5469652a6.section: Climate > Middle Oligocene climate and the Oi2 event
b9d5469652a6.sentence: There were several pulses of glaciation in middle Oligocene, about the time of the Oi2 oxygen isotope shift.

f5a1ce47cadf.title: Oligocene
f5a1ce47cadf.section: Climate > Middle Oligocene climate and the Oi2 event
f5a1ce47cadf.sentence: This led to the largest drop of sea level in past 100 million years, by about 75 meters (246 ft).

27bf03f58e11.title: Oligocene
27bf03f58e11.section: Climate > Middle Oligocene climate and the Oi2 event
27bf03f58e11.sentence: This is reflected in a mid-Oligocene incision of continental shelves and unconformities in marine rocks around the world.

ac34637ca410.title: Oligocene
ac34637ca410.sentence: Lesser faunal turnovers occurred simultaneously with the Oi2 event and towards the end of the Oligocene.

f804d3246aae.title: Black Sea
f804d3246aae.sentence: During this time sand shed off the rising Balkanide, Pontide and Caucasus mountains trapped organic material in the Maykop Suite of rocks through the Oligocene and early Miocene.

309b0db49cc1.title: Oligocene
309b0db49cc1.sentence: The start of the Oligocene is marked by a notable extinction event called the Grande Coupure; it featured the replacement of European fauna with Asian fauna, except for the endemic rodent and marsupial families.

b06a17b24c0a.title: Atacama Desert
b06a17b24c0a.sentence: The Atacama Desert may be the oldest desert on earth, and has experienced hyper aridity since at least the Middle Miocene, since the establishment of a proto-Humboldt current in conjunction with the opening of the Tasmania-Antarctic passage ca. 33 million years ago (Ma).

55df3812a537.title: Atacama Desert
55df3812a537.sentence: Though there was a general lack of humid air after 33 Ma, there were punctuated intervals of increased humidity, such as between around 10.86 and 6.4 Ma, when the Tiliviche Palaeolake existed before turning into a salar sometime before the Middle Pliocene.

ef4f763e578b.title: Oligocene
ef4f763e578b.sentence: Australia had been very slowly drifting away from West Antarctica since the Jurassic, but the exact timing of the establishment of ocean channels between the two continents remains uncertain.

ccfd7279c80e.title: Oligocene
ccfd7279c80e.sentence: However, one estimate is that a deep channel was in place between the two continents by the end of the early Oligocene.

e443a1dc0ccd.title: Oligocene
e443a1dc0ccd.section: Oceans > Effects of oceanic gateways on circulation > Drake Passage
e443a1dc0ccd.sentence: As the South American continent moved north, the Drake Passage opened and enabled the formation of the Antarctic Circumpolar Current (ACC), which would have kept the cold waters of Antarctica circulating around that continent and strengthened the formation of Antarctic Bottom Water (ABW).

14ad9f1cd1ed.title: Oligocene
14ad9f1cd1ed.section: Oceans > Effects of oceanic gateways on circulation > Drake Passage
14ad9f1cd1ed.sentence: Even so, many theories agree that at the Eocene/Oligocene (E/O) boundary, a yet shallow flow existed between South America and Antarctica, permitting the start of an Antarctic Circumpolar Current.

96a4a1794de7.title: Oligocene
96a4a1794de7.section: Oceans > Effects of oceanic gateways on circulation > Drake Passage
96a4a1794de7.sentence: Despite the shallow flow between South America and Antarctica, there was not enough of a deep water opening to allow for significant flow to create a true Antarctic Circumpolar Current.

4f00f2bd3016.title: Oligocene
4f00f2bd3016.section: Climate > Eocene-Oligocene transition and Oi1 event
4f00f2bd3016.sentence: Deep sea cores from south of New Zealand suggest that cold deep-sea currents were present by the early Oligocene.

f460249ea76d.title: Oligocene
f460249ea76d.sentence: Between 31 and 26 mya, the Ethiopia-Yemen Continental Flood Basalts were emplaced by the East African large igneous province, which also initiated rift formation along the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.

ba888bb1cc0f.title: East African Rift

977d2edaa15e.title: Miocene

049298ac063d.title: Apodiformes

049b6cdf8454.title: Middle Pleistocene

04b0e07c02ed.title: Geology of Scotland

04b5c1736751.title: Quilotoa

04d489325edd.title: Lake Idaho

04d6e76cbc79.title: Iberian plate

04ddadb2dbdb.title: Mammoth steppe

0571acf011a7.title: Shatsky Rise

0bc37ec9683d.title: Australian plate

0bdd1923e65f.title: Kačák event

0be06da88883.title: Choristodera

0be386480ac3.title: Sierra Madre Occidental

0bebd19c7abb.title: Nadir crater

0c0a8509df3c.title: Ediacaran biota

0c2c28045bc8.title: Lau event

0c32d1de4bb9.title: Wrangellia terrane

0c3559e984f7.title: Ganderia

0c6552d6b0f7.title: Denisovan

0c65d71eec7a.title: Aso Caldera

0c6b0905f596.title: Keeling Curve

0c730deb0919.title: Traquairaspidiformes

0ceca1376356.title: Saale glaciation

0cf4d9544c0a.title: Xianren Cave

31b0ff6514a0.title: Middle Miocene disruption

31d26bf5f7fa.title: Last Glacial Maximum

31d849e91caf.title: Multituberculata

3f06223f1821.title: Zechstein

3f0c5f612600.title: Komatiite

It is the largest world's single largest repository of fossil insects.

428ea69a6e08.title: Colorado orogeny
428ea69a6e08.sentence: The Colorado orogen, formerly called the Colorado province, is a >500-km-wide belt of oceanic arc rock (1.78–1.65 Ga) that extends southward into New Mexico and composes a major part of the Proterozoic provinces of southwestern United States.

429374f1990d.title: Little Ice Age

429b567b5c6c.title: Late Paleozoic icehouse
429b567b5c6c.sentence: These Early Mississippian glaciations were transient and minor, with them sometimes being considered discrete glaciations separate from and preceding the LPIA proper.

42a654225f73.title: Boring Billion

42b846d8ef27.title: Baltic Ice Lake
42b846d8ef27.sentence: The beginning of the Holocene is close in time to the end of the ice lake.

42b94e4db290.title: Last Glacial Maximum
42b94e4db290.sentence: Over most of the Chiloé Archipelago, glacier advance peaked 26,000 years ago, forming a long north–south moraine system along the eastern coast of Chiloé Island (41.5–43° S).

42c96156f903.title: 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora
42c96156f903.sentence: This eruption, with a volcanic explosivity index (VEI) of 7, ejected 37–45 km3 (8.9–10.8 cubic miles) of dense-rock equivalent (DRE) material into the atmosphere, and was the most recent confirmed VEI-7 eruption.

42ca9459f5ef.title: Llandovery Epoch
42ca9459f5ef.sentence: Biodiversity, with the sustained re-flooding of continental shelves at the onset of the Silurian, rebounded within the surviving orders.

42ce3f0d24bc.title: List of Permian tetrapods
42ce3f0d24bc.sentence: Synapsids became the dominant type of animal, represented by the Pelycosaurs during the Early Permian and Therapsids during the Middle and Late Permian, and distinguished by the appearance and possession of mammal-like characteristics (hence the old term "mammal-like reptiles").

42d42fecdcdc.title: 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora
42d42fecdcdc.sentence: Impact | 10,000 to 11,000 deaths from direct volcanic effects; 49,000 to 90,000 deaths from post-eruption famine and epidemic diseases on Sumbawa, Lombok and Bali; reduced global temperatures in the following year which led to famine in numerous regions

42f1a1faeee6.title: Oldest Dryas
42f1a1faeee6.sentence: During the Oldest Dryas, Europe was treeless and similar to the Arctic tundra, but much drier and grassier than the modern tundra.

42fd70a5d0f4.title: Ardipithecus ramidus
42fd70a5d0f4.sentence: In 2001, 6.5- to 5.5-million-year-old fossils from the Middle Awash were classified as a subspecies of A. ramidus by Ethiopian paleoanthropologist Yohannes Haile-Selassie.

431429adce51.title: Homo naledi

4318b5e26cf8.title: Congo Craton

4322f409fd44.title: Meltwater pulse 1A
4322f409fd44.sentence: MWP1a occurred in a period of rising sea level and rapid climate change at the end of the Last Glacial Period, known as Termination I. Several researchers have narrowed the period of the pulse to between 14,300 and 14,650 years ago.

432348c55034.title: Paleoarchean
432348c55034.sentence: The Strelley Pool Chert, also located in the Pilbara Craton, contains stromatolites that may have been created by bacteria 3.4 billion years ago.

4323d6a29b92.title: Capricorn orogeny
4323d6a29b92.sentence: The Capricorn orogeny was an orogenic event in what is now Western Australia, following the collision of the Pilbara Craton and the Glenburgh Terrane with the Yilgarn craton during the Glenburgh orogeny.

4327c03e455a.title: Barberton Greenstone Belt
4327c03e455a.sentence: The Barberton area underwent two tectonic episodes of terrane accretion at about 3.5 and 3.2 Ga.

432f5f2795cc.title: Tunguska event

4331382640c7.title: Charnia
4331382640c7.sentence: The living organism grew on the sea floor, 570 to 550 million years ago, and is believed to have fed on nutrients in the water.

43446cedef77.title: Deicke and Millbrig bentonite layers
43446cedef77.sentence: Researchers are very interested in the eruptions that formed these bentonite layers because they are thought to be some of the largest volcanic eruptions in the last 600 million years of Earth history, and the resulting ash layer for each eruption individually was greater in volume than the Toba eruption.

4359d5976094.title: Middle Paleolithic
4359d5976094.sentence: The Middle Paleolithic was succeeded by the Upper Paleolithic subdivision which first began between 50,000 and 40,000 years ago.

436a63d3e51c.title: Catskill Formation
436a63d3e51c.sentence: The rocks of the Catskill are a clastic wedge of predominantly red sandstone, indicating a large-scale terrestrial deposition during the Acadian orogeny.

436b0eb12908.title: Diprotodon

436fb10009d6.title: Evolution of photosynthesis
436fb10009d6.sentence: Fossils of what are thought to be filamentous photosynthetic organisms have been dated at 3.4Gy, consistent with recent studies of photosynthesis.

437a9cbf7fc8.title: Cascadia subduction zone
437a9cbf7fc8.sentence: All along British Columbia, Washington State, and Oregon, the coast had fallen due to a violent earthquake and been covered by sand from the subsequent tsunami.

4392d3c139f0.title: Kola Alkaline Province
4392d3c139f0.sentence: The province is made up of alkaline-ultramafic rock complexes often associated to carbonatites and stand-alone dykes and pipes made up of carbonatites, kimberlites and similar rocks.

43b960812eaf.title: Guiyang biota
43b960812eaf.sentence: The Guiyang biota is an exceptionally preserved Early Triassic (approximately 250.8 million years ago) fossil assemblage from the Daye Formation near Guiyang (China), discovered between 2015 and 2019 and first reported in 2023.

43c4696e98c8.title: Great Ordovician Biodiversification Event
43c4696e98c8.sentence: The acritarch record (the majority of acritarchs were probably marine algae) displays the Ordovician radiation beautifully; both diversity and disparity peaked in the middle Ordovician.

43e51a1f6f0d.title: Lhasa terrane
43e51a1f6f0d.sentence: Contact with Indian plate began along the Yarlung–Zangbo suture around 50 Ma during the Eocene, and the two continents continue to converge.

43ea2f9ac3d2.title: Arctodus
43ea2f9ac3d2.sentence: Today considered to be an enormous omnivore, Arctodus simus is believed to be one of the largest known terrestrial carnivorans that has ever existed.

43efd0d0af79.title: Huronian glaciation
43efd0d0af79.sentence: The Huronian glaciation (or Makganyene glaciation) refers to a series of three ancient glacial periods approximately 2.4 to 2.1 billion years ago, during the Siderian and Rhyacian periods of the Paleoproterozoic era.

43f8fb82e4ba.title: Yavapai orogeny
43f8fb82e4ba.sentence: Age and isotope data show that southern North America is composed of a series of northeast-trending provinces representing island arc terranes accreted onto the 1800 Mya core of Laurentia.

440105b893c3.title: Paratethys
440105b893c3.sentence: Paratethys was at times reconnected with the Tethys or its successors (the Mediterranean Sea or the Indian Ocean) during the Oligocene and the early and middle Miocene times, but at the onset of the late Miocene epoch, the tectonically trapped sea turned into a megalake from the eastern Alps to what is now Kazakhstan.

44079afb85a3.title: Kaali crater
44079afb85a3.sentence: The estimates of the age of the Kaali impact structure (Saaremaa Island, Estonia) provided by different authors vary by as much as 6,000 years, ranging from ~6,400 to ~400 years before current era (BCE).

4408bc698e59.title: Pan-African orogeny
4408bc698e59.sentence: The Mozambique ocean began closing between Madagascar-India and the Congo–Tanzania craton between 700 and 580 million years ago, with closure between 600 and 500 million years ago.

440fd95f3cdc.title: Lagomorpha
440fd95f3cdc.sentence: A 2008 study by evolutionary biologist Kenneth D. Rose and colleagues suggests an Indian origin for the lagomorph order, having possibly evolved in isolation when India was an island continent in the Paleocene.

44196f944a6c.title: Acheulean
44196f944a6c.sentence: In Athirampakkam at Chennai in Tamil Nadu the Acheulean age started at 1.51 mya and it is also prior than North India and Europe.

442ed4c357c5.title: Aptian-Albian Cold Snap

443a0e470410.title: Evolution of photosynthesis

44655906bd32.title: Coquimbo Formation

446d79d3d466.title: Geology of the Grand Canyon area

447aeafc37b2.title: Vredefort impact structure
447aeafc37b2.sentence: The 40-kilometre-diameter (25 mi) centre of the Vredefort impact structure consists of a granite dome (where it is not covered by much younger rocks belonging to the Karoo Supergroup) which is an exposed part of the Kaapvaal craton, one of the oldest microcontinents which formed on Earth 3.9 billion years ago.

448773bc1154.title: Early human migrations
448773bc1154.section: Homo sapiens > Coastal migration > Nearby Oceania
448773bc1154.sentence: This migration is believed to have happened around 50,000 years ago, before Australia and New Guinea were separated by rising sea levels approximately 8,000 years ago.

449146d1a47e.title: Cynodontia

449e67475af8.title: Snowball Earth

44c1ca8ec6c2.title: Coral bleaching

44fe1d51f4ef.sentence: In North America, Hipparion and its relatives (Cormohipparion, Nannippus, Neohipparion, and Pseudhipparion), proliferated into many kinds of equids, at least one of which managed to migrate to Asia and Europe during the Miocene epoch.

45e34c1f7e7b.title: Oruanui eruption

462123ba41f7.title: Acheulean

4625d64916b8.title: Temnospondyli

467a3f05bb41.sentence: Placoderms (from Ancient Greek πλάξ [plax, plakos] 'plate' and δέρμα [derma] 'skin') are vertebrate animals of the class Placodermi, an extinct group of prehistoric fish known from Paleozoic fossils during the Silurian and the Devonian periods.

Partial B. priscus remains are hard to distinguish anatomically from B. bonasus, which muddles the timeframe of its extinction in Europe and Western Siberia; often the species B. priscus was assigned to Late Pleistocene remains and B. bonasus to Holocene remains without further discussion. However B. priscus is both genetically distinct and known to have survived into the middle Holocene of North America. Remains of either B. priscus or B. bonasus were dated in the Angara River basin to 2550-2440 BCE, and a small bison persisted in the Baikal region until the 7th-10th century CE (considered B. priscus by Boeskorov and B. bonasus by Sipko ).

7c9ac8cd6a93.title: Persian Gulf

7d3d623c1fff.title: Gorgonopsia

7d4660bd155b.title: Stromatoporoidea

7d54bb5a8119.title: Oldowan

9005518f0afc.sentence: 40 Ma | Modern-type butterflies and moths appear. Extinction of Gastornis. Basilosaurus, one of the first of the giant whales, appeared in the fossil record.

901380ccb762.title: Great American Interchange
901380ccb762.sentence: The formation of the Isthmus of Panama led to the last and most conspicuous wave, the Great American Biotic Interchange (GABI), starting around 2.7 Ma ago.

901be2cb33e9.title: Tunguska event
901be2cb33e9.sentence: The cataclysm occurred in a remote and sparsely populated region of the taiga, near the Podkamennaya Tunguska River after which it is named.

90266c69e129.title: Woolly mammoth
90266c69e129.sentence: Trackways made by a woolly mammoth herd 11,300–11,000 years ago have been found in the St. Mary Reservoir in Canada, showing that in this case, almost equal numbers of adults, subadults, and juveniles were found.

902f68ca0a55.title: Nevadan orogeny
902f68ca0a55.section: Timing of events in the Sierra Nevada and Klamath Mountains
902f68ca0a55.sentence: As the Nevadan Orogeny progressed, the Tuolumne River Terrane was accreted to the Sierra Nevada at approximately the same time as the formation of the Josephine Ophiolite in the Klamath Mountains (150-155 Ma).

9045b05652e0.title: Carnian pluvial episode
9045b05652e0.sentence: The earliest dinosaurs (which include the ancestors of birds), lepidosaurs (the ancestors of modern-day lizards, snakes, and the tuatara) and potentially mammaliaforms (ancestors of mammals) all diversified during the event.

9046929cef6b.title: Neoglaciation
9046929cef6b.sentence: Neoglaciation had been marked by a retreat from the warm conditions of the Climatic Optimum and the advance or reformation of glaciers that had not existed since the last ice age.

9048ca3d02ce.title: Gelasian
9048ca3d02ce.sentence: Similarly, the top of the Gelasian is magnetostratigraphically defined as the end of the Olduvai (C2n) chronozone, and faunally as the extinction level of the calcareous nannofossil Discoaster brouweri (base of biozone CN13).

9052715aa2ff.title: Perissodactyla
9052715aa2ff.sentence: Finds of Cambaytherium and Kalitherium in the Cambay shale of western India indicate an origin in Asia dating to the Lower Eocene roughly 54.5 million years ago.

9054bf83b212.title: Cryogenian
9054bf83b212.sentence: The superocean Mirovia began to close while the superocean Panthalassa began to form.

9055ac3319b1.title: Basin and Range Province
9055ac3319b1.sentence: Total lateral displacement in the Basin and Range varies from 60 to 300 km since the onset of extension in the Early Miocene with the southern portion of the province representing a greater degree of displacement than the north.

905a96ce233d.title: Tendaguru Formation
905a96ce233d.section: Description > Paleogeography and depositional environment > Paleogeography
905a96ce233d.sentence: The Tendaguru fauna was stable through the Late Jurassic.

905c9b85830e.title: Paleocene
905c9b85830e.sentence: Turtles experienced a decline in the Campanian (Late Cretaceous) during a cooling event, and recovered during the PETM at the end of the Paleocene.

9063685a253e.title: Late Heavy Bombardment
9063685a253e.sentence: Other researchers doubt the heavy bombardment, arguing for example that the apparent clustering of lunar impact-melt ages is a statistical artifact produced by sampling rocks scattered from a single large impact.

906f2445477b.title: Castile Formation
906f2445477b.sentence: The formation lies on the Bell Canyon Formation and in turn is overlain by the Salado Formation, which is characterized in the subsurface by a thick sequence of halite beds.

906f3a966898.title: Geomagnetic reversal
906f3a966898.section: Geomagnetic polarity time scale > Changing frequency over time > Superchrons
906f3a966898.sentence: The magnetic field had reversed polarity.

907b7758c93b.title: Geology of the Himalayas
907b7758c93b.sentence: The change of the relative speed between the Indian and Asian plates from very fast (18-19.5 cm/yr) to fast (4.5 cm/yr) at about 55 Ma is circumstantial support for collision then.

908127f0ab53.title: Pan-African orogeny
908127f0ab53.sentence: The Pan-African orogeny was a series of major Neoproterozoic orogenic events which related to the formation of the supercontinents Gondwana and Pannotia about 600 million years ago.

9098dd176a93.title: Late Pleistocene extinctions
9098dd176a93.sentence: It has been shown that the prevailing climate at the time of extinction (40,000–50,000 BP) was similar to that of today, and that the extinct animals were strongly adapted to an arid climate.

90a61dfe82fc.title: Gorgonopsia
90a61dfe82fc.sentence: Gorgonopsia (from the Greek Gorgon, a mythological monster, and óps 'aspect') is an extinct clade of sabre-toothed therapsids from the Middle to the Upper Permian, roughly between 270 and 252 million years ago.

90bba14ee633.title: Kačák event
90bba14ee633.sentence: Within the Old Red Sandstone continent, it is represented by the Achanarras lake, the deepest and most widespread lake that developed within the Orcadian Basin.

90bd09905114.title: Early Triassic
90bd09905114.section: Early Triassic life > Fauna and flora > Aquatic biota
90bd09905114.sentence: Typical Triassic ray-finned fishes, such as Australosomus, Birgeria, Bobasatrania, Boreosomus, Pteronisculus, Parasemionotidae and Saurichthys appeared close to the Permian-Triassic boundary, whereas neopterygians (including stem teleosts) diversified later during the Triassic, though the pattern of the Triassic diversification of bony fishes is not well understood due to a taphonomic megabias (Spathian-Bithynian Gap, SBG) in the late Early Triassic and early Middle Triassic.

90c00d479174.title: Popigai impact structure
90c00d479174.sentence: It is tied with the Acraman impact structure as the fourth largest verified impact structure on Earth.

90d6ce26f2bc.title: Cambrian
90d6ce26f2bc.section: Oceanic life > Porifera, Cnidaria and Ctenophora > Porifera
90d6ce26f2bc.sentence: Cyanobacteria and other calcimicrobes precipitated calcium carbonate, which encrusted Archaeocyatha skeletons, binding them together to form the framework of the reef.

90e15d951a13.title: Paleoarchean
90e15d951a13.sentence: The Buck Reef chert and the Josefsdal chert, two rock formations in the Barberton Greenstone Belt, both contain microbial mats with fossilized bacteria from the Paleoarchean era.

90e2df0d61a1.title: Komatiite
90e2df0d61a1.sentence: This restriction in age is thought to be due to cooling of the mantle, which may have been 100–250 °C (212–482 °F) hotter during the Archaean.

90ef67b0badd.title: Timeline of Earth
90ef67b0badd.section: Phanerozoic Eon > Mesozoic Era > Cretaceous Period
90ef67b0badd.sentence: Carnosaurs (comprising megalosaurids, allosaurids and carcharodontosaurids) go extinct.

910609efb850.title: Canadian Arctic Rift System
910609efb850.section: Geology > Tectonic evolution > Eurekan Rifting Episode
910609efb850.sentence: Seafloor spreading commenced in the southern Labrador Sea 75–60 million years ago, during which Greenland moved north relative to mainland North America.

910c79e11949.title: Laacher See
910c79e11949.sentence: The current best estimates for the age of the Laacher See eruption are 12,880 ± 40 years BP or 13,006 ± 9 calibrated years before present, depending on whether the radiocarbon date was affected by magmatic carbon dioxide.

910ff04734e0.title: Yavapai orogeny
910ff04734e0.sentence: Quartzite-rhyolite successions associated with extensional basins include the Vadito Group and Hondo Group in New Mexico and the Mazatzal Group in Arizona, deposited during the transition from the Yavapai to the Mazatzal orogens at 1700 Mya.

911e8a0ce7ea.title: Uralian orogeny
911e8a0ce7ea.sentence: As Baltica collided with Laurentia to form Laurussia, island arcs and other microcontinents were accreted to Baltica in the Late Devonian-Early Carboniferous.

9120763c7bf3.title: Meridiolestida
9120763c7bf3.sentence: The latest surviving meridiolestidan was the mole-like burrowing insectivore Necrolestes from the Miocene of Patagonia.

9128c21630e4.title: Rodinia
9128c21630e4.sentence: The result was the formation of Gondwana.

9151c354c447.title: Sundaland
9151c354c447.sentence: During the Last Glacial Maximum the sea level fell by approximately 120 meters, and the entire Sunda Shelf was exposed.

9154e920ba98.title: Dresser Formation
9154e920ba98.sentence: The Dresser Formation stromatolites apparently formed predominantly within these hydrothermally influenced shallow-marine lagoonal conditions, with geological and geochemical evidence indicating that some also formed in close proximity to subaerial (land-based) hot springs.

91617a44f74a.title: Moldanubian Zone
91617a44f74a.sentence: The Moldanubian Zone is in the regional geology of Europe a tectonic zone formed during the Variscan or Hercynian Orogeny (400 to 300 million years ago, during the Devonian and Carboniferous periods).

91663d5a4316.title: Cambrian
91663d5a4316.section: Geochemistry > Isotope excursions > Cambrian Stage 4 to early Miaolingian
91663d5a4316.sentence: The beginning of the eruptions of the Kalkarindji LIP basalts during Stage 4 and the early Miaolingian released large quantities of carbon dioxide, methane and sulphur dioxide into the atmosphere.

91679d798c8f.title: Paleocene
91679d798c8f.sentence: Multituberculates declined in the late Paleocene and went extinct at the end of the Eocene, possibly due to competition from newly evolving rodents.

916933ca5f33.title: Timeline of life
916933ca5f33.section: Detailed timeline > Phanerozoic Eon > Mesozoic Era
916933ca5f33.sentence: 90 Ma | Extinction of ichthyosaurs. Earliest snakes and nuculanid bivalves. Large diversification in angiosperms: magnoliids, rosids, hamamelidids, monocots, and ginger. Earliest examples of ticks. Probable origins of placental mammals (earliest undisputed fossil evidence is 66 Ma).

91718d79451e.title: Cave bear
91718d79451e.sentence: In 2019, the results of a large scale study of 81 bone specimens (resulting in 59 new sequences) and 64 previously published complete mitochondrial genomes of cave bear mitochondrial DNA remains found in Switzerland, Poland, France, Spain, Germany, Italy and Serbia, indicated that the cave bear population drastically declined starting around 40,000 years ago at the onset of the Aurignacian, coinciding with the arrival of anatomically modern humans.

9176a5613c99.title: Mesoarchean
9176a5613c99.sentence: The Mesoarchean atmosphere contained high levels of atmospheric methane and carbon dioxide, which could be an explanation for the high temperatures during this era.

917d2284b061.title: North American land mammal age
917d2284b061.sentence: Irvingtonian | 1.4 Ma. | Early Pleistocene | C1r.2r – C1n | The ice age continues. Mammoths expand south of Alaska.

917ea0909fff.title: Timeline of Earth
917ea0909fff.section: Proterozoic Eon > Paleoproterozoic Era > Orosirian Period
917ea0909fff.sentence: - c. 1,830 Ma – Capricorn Orogeny (1.83–1.78 Gyr) stabilizes central and northern Gascoyne Complex: formation of pelitic and psammitic schists known as Morrissey Metamorphics and depositing Pooranoo Metamorphics an amphibolite facies

918782100d49.title: Neoproterozoic oxygenation event
918782100d49.sentence: Chromium isotopes also show that during the Cryogenian interglacial interval, between the Sturtian and Marinoan glaciations, oxygenation of the ocean and atmosphere was slow and subdued; this interval marked a lull in the NOE.

9190882bfd7e.title: Early human migrations
9190882bfd7e.section: Homo sapiens > Dispersal throughout Eurasia > East, Southeast and North Asia
9190882bfd7e.sentence: "Tianyuan man", an individual who lived in China c. 40,000 years ago, showed substantial Neanderthal admixture.

919b6686ea40.title: Isthmus of Panama
919b6686ea40.sentence: However exchange of surface water so as to maintain western Atlantic salinity at eastern Pacific values continued until about 4.6 Ma, with current Caribbean values being reached by about 4.2 Ma, although there seems to have been a last definite temporary breach as recently as 2.45 Ma.

91a27c952eb2.title: Skhul and Qafzeh hominins
91a27c952eb2.sentence: In 2018, modern human fossils from Misliya Cave (also around Mount Carmel) were dated to 177,000 years ago, which could indicate modern human populations fluctuated in and out of the Levant several times (maybe in response to environmental stressors), possibly even before 200,000 years ago.

91af24c37c94.title: Late Paleozoic icehouse
91af24c37c94.sentence: The second glacial period occurred from the late Gzhelian across the Carboniferous-Permian boundary to the early Sakmarian; ice sheets expanded from a core in Australia and India.

91be8ab156ea.title: Kerguelen Plateau
91be8ab156ea.sentence: In contrast, the magmatism that produced the Australia–India breakup 136–158 Ma created the Wallaby Plateau, but no known hotspot has been linked to this event.

91c0b6659320.title: Evolution of fish
91c0b6659320.section: Jawed fish > Bony fish > Lobe-finned fish
91c0b6659320.sentence: The heyday of the former was the Late Devonian and Carboniferous, from 385 to 299 Mya, as they were more common during those periods than in any other period in the Phanerozoic; coelacanths still live today in the oceans (genus Latimeria).

91c648401ed1.title: Wilkes Land crater
91c648401ed1.sentence: The complete absence of a well-defined impact ejecta layer associated with the Permian–Triassic boundary at its outcrops within Victoria Land and the central Transantarctic Mountains argues against there having been any impact capable of creating a crater the size of the hypothesized Wilkes Land impact crater within Antarctica at the Permian–Triassic boundary.

91c718eac201.title: Past sea level
91c718eac201.section: Geological influences > Changes through geologic time > Sea level rise since the last glacial maximum
91c718eac201.sentence: Recently, it has become widely accepted that late Holocene, 3,000 calendar years ago to present, sea level was nearly stable prior to an acceleration of the rate of rise that is variously dated between 1850 and 1900 AD.

91c9af3c33e3.title: Stegodon
91c9af3c33e3.sentence: The last records of Stegodon florensis date to around 50,000 years ago, around the time of arrival of modern humans to Flores (the earliest evidence of which dates to 46,000 years ago), suggesting that effects of modern human activity were likely the cause of their extinction.

91d25cc91a93.title: Nördlinger Ries
91d25cc91a93.sentence: The tektite melt originated from a sand-rich surface layer that was ejected to distances up to 450 km (280 mi) downrange of the crater.

91d5ea307b87.title: Outburst flood
91d5ea307b87.section: Examples > Tectonic basins > English Channel floods
91d5ea307b87.sentence: At some time, probably around 425,000 years ago and again around 225,000 years later, the barrier failed or was overtopped, loosing a catastrophic flood that permanently diverted the Rhine into the English Channel and replacing the "Isthmus of Dover" watershed by a much lower watershed running from East Anglia east then southeast to the Hook of Holland and (as at modern sea level) separated Britain from the continent of Europe; a sonar study of the sea bed of the English Channel published in Nature, July 2007, revealed the discovery of unmistakable marks of a megaflood on the English Channel seabed: deeply eroded channels and braided features have left the remnants of streamlined islands among deeply gouged channels where the collapse occurred.

91d9d2430b52.title: North American land mammal age
91d9d2430b52.sentence: Hemingfordian | 18.5 Ma. | Early Miocene | C5Er – C5Cn | Savanna and other grassy habitats dominate the landscape. Grazing horse species become more common than browsing species. Miocene variants of oreodonts, camels, and rhinos are well-established, though White River hallmarks are practically extinct. More carnivorans spread into North America, including procyonids (racoon relatives), ailurids (red panda relatives), amphicyonine bear dogs, and true cats, which end the " cat gap ". Near the end of this age, the Middle Miocene Climatic Optimum leads to a brief resurgence of warm forests.

91dc13b3aed7.title: Ichthyosauria
91dc13b3aed7.sentence: Indeed, likely a radiation during the Early Cretaceous occurred due to an increase of coastlines when the continents further broke up.

91dd8b1dfde4.title: Neoproterozoic oxygenation event
91dd8b1dfde4.sentence: Unlike the GOE, it is unclear whether the NOE was a synchronous, global event or a series of asynchronous, regional oxygenation intervals with unrelated causes.

91e851ed17b6.title: Delaware Basin
91e851ed17b6.sentence: Sedimentation continued to fill the Delaware Basin into the Ochoan Epoch of the upper Permian, periodically cutting the basin off from its source of seawater.

91e9a50c4549.title: Paleocene
91e9a50c4549.sentence: There is also evidence this occurred again 300,000 years later in the early Thanetian dubbed MPBE-2.

91ec5b6ba8ab.title: Qinling orogenic belt
91ec5b6ba8ab.section: Geology of Qinling > Mianlue suture zone
91ec5b6ba8ab.sentence: The Mianlue suture zone was evolved from Mianlue oceanic basin, which was closed at the Mid-Triassic and developed into suture zone.

9200326224af.title: Mount Vesuvius
9200326224af.sentence: The eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD destroyed the Roman cities of Pompeii, Herculaneum, Oplontis, Stabiae and other settlements.

92058990c9de.title: List of possible impact structures on Earth
92058990c9de.sentence: A 2022 study using Argon–Argon dating of shocked zircon crystals in impact melt rocks found outwash less than 10 km downstream of the glacier pushed the estimate back to around 57.99 ± 0.54 million years ago, during the late Paleocene.

9209cc7081e3.title: Youngest Toba eruption
9209cc7081e3.section: Eruption > Climatic effects > Climate at the time of the eruption
9209cc7081e3.sentence: Southern Hemisphere glaciation grew to its maximum extent during MIS 4.

9229e6a5c0a6.title: Peopling of the Americas
9229e6a5c0a6.section: Environment during the latest glaciation > Glaciers
9229e6a5c0a6.sentence: The ice-free corridor to the interior of North America opened between 13,000 and 12,000 BP.

9235d5da1264.title: Sinsk Event
9235d5da1264.section: Ecological impact and aftermath > Recovery and refugia
9235d5da1264.sentence: Motile, unattached taxa with broad depth tolerances and diversified feeding modes (notably trilobites, helcionelloida molluscs, hyolitha, protoconodonts, and brachiopods) diversified rapidly in the aftermath, while sessile, heavily calcified, shallow-water filter-feeders either failed to recover or went extinct in the following few million years.

923d1ffa055e.title: Scandinavian Mountains
923d1ffa055e.sentence: During the Last Glacial Maximum (ca. 20 ka BP) all the Scandinavian Mountains were covered by the Fennoscandian Ice Sheet, which extended well beyond the mountains into Denmark, Germany, Poland and the former USSR.

923d65d67364.title: Evolution of the horse
923d65d67364.section: Eocene and Oligocene: early equids > Eohippus
923d65d67364.sentence: Eohippus appeared in the Ypresian (early Eocene), about 52 mya (million years ago).

923e1d08f83c.title: Columbian mammoth
923e1d08f83c.sentence: They are, therefore, considered to be the distinct species M. exilis, the pygmy mammoth (or a subspecies, M. c. exilis).

9246a21c3cae.title: Aegyptosaurus
9246a21c3cae.sentence: North Africa, during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, bordered the Tethys Sea, which transformed the region into a mangrove-dominated coastal environment filled with vast tidal flats and waterways.

9259ef79bb09.title: Lagerstätte
9259ef79bb09.sentence: Burmese amber | 101-99 Ma (latest Albian/earliest Cenomanian) | Myanmar | More than 1,000 species of taxa have been described from ambers from Hukawng Valley. While it is important for understanding the evolution of biota, mainly insects, during the Cretaceous period, it is also extremely controversial by facing ethical issues due to its association with conflicts and labor conditions.

92615685f3c7.title: Dilophosaurus
92615685f3c7.sentence: In 1971, Welles reported dinosaur footprints from the Kayenta Formation of northern Arizona, on two levels 14 m (45 ft) and 112 m (367 ft) below where the original Dilophosaurus specimens were found.

9268506c39b9.title: Carnian pluvial episode
9268506c39b9.sentence: In the oceans, carbonate minerals such as limestone saw reduced deposition, leaving mud-rich layers as prominent geological markers.

927c076bd75e.title: Stromatoporoidea
927c076bd75e.sentence: Actinostromatids, stromatoporellids, and stromatoporids were next in line, with their diversity and reef extent collapsing at the end of the Frasnian in accordance with the Kellwasser event (Late Devonian mass extinction).

928c1fb8186e.title: Upper Paleolithic
928c1fb8186e.sentence: Anatomically modern humans are known to have expanded northward into Siberia as far as the 58th parallel by about 45 ka (Ust'-Ishim man).

9299be101545.title: Timeline of Earth
9299be101545.section: Phanerozoic Eon > Cenozoic Era > Paleogene Period
9299be101545.sentence: - c. 55 Ma – the island of the Indian subcontinent collides with Asia, thrusting up the Himalayas and the Tibetan Plateau.

92b2266a64c6.title: Shungite
92b2266a64c6.sentence: It is found within a sequence of Palaeoproterozoic meta-sedimentary and meta-volcanic rocks that are preserved in a synform.

92b28d7c1c39.title: Geological history of Earth
92b28d7c1c39.section: Phanerozoic > Cenozoic Era > Paleogene Period > Eocene Epoch
92b28d7c1c39.sentence: But when Australia split from the southern continent around 45 Ma, the warm equatorial currents were deflected away from Antarctica, and an isolated cold water channel developed between the two continents.

92bfc6590631.title: Sauropod hiatus
92bfc6590631.sentence: The sauropod hiatus ended shortly before the end of the Cretaceous, with the appearance of Alamosaurus, most likely an immigrant from South America, in the southwestern parts of North America.

92c542787a1e.title: La Venta (Colombia)
92c542787a1e.sentence: These animals lived some 13.8 to 12 million years ago in the Laventan age, which was named after La Venta.

92c81b26c08a.title: Evolution of insects
92c81b26c08a.sentence: By the Pennsylvanian and well into the Permian, by far the most successful were primitive Blattoptera, or relatives of cockroaches.

92d6f28cbed9.title: Late Cenozoic Ice Age
92d6f28cbed9.sentence: With the exception of this small amount of Neanderthal DNA that exists today, Neanderthals became extinct 30,000 years ago.

92df44dc88ba.title: Ichthyosauria
92df44dc88ba.sentence: Ichthyosaur extinction was thus a pair of abrupt events rather than a long decline, probably related to the environmental upheavals and climatic changes in the Cenomanian and Turonian.

92e589bdf56b.title: Clovis culture
92e589bdf56b.sentence: The type site is Blackwater Draw locality No. 1 near Clovis, New Mexico, where stone tools were found alongside the remains of Columbian mammoths in 1929.

92e8048abb39.title: Miralga impact structure
92e8048abb39.sentence: Spherules formed from condensed impact vapour within the Antarctic Creek Member do record unambiguous evidence of an approximately 3.5-billion-year-old impact event within the rocks of the North Pole Dome, but spherules can be transported long distances away from the impact site, so it does not represent clear evidence of a nearby impact.

92e910c3583a.title: Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event
92e910c3583a.section: Causes > Chicxulub impact > Effects of impact
92e910c3583a.sentence: The end-Cretaceous event is the only mass extinction definitively known to be associated with an impact, and other large extraterrestrial impacts, such as the Manicouagan Reservoir impact, do not coincide with any noticeable extinction events.

92e9fbd02663.title: Timeline of Earth
92e9fbd02663.section: Phanerozoic Eon > Mesozoic Era > Cretaceous Period
92e9fbd02663.sentence: - c. 93 Ma - Cenomanian-Turonian boundary event causes the extinction of ichthyosaurs and pliosaurs.

92ee9f06b099.title: Gomphotherium land bridge
92ee9f06b099.sentence: More recent analysis found that the Gomphotherium land bridge may have formed slightly earlier, around 20 Ma, which resulted in the Great Old World Biotic Interchange.

92f4aedffef2.title: Late Cenozoic Ice Age
92f4aedffef2.sentence: Around 850,000 ± 50,000 years ago, the degree of orbital eccentricity became the main driver of glacial and interglacial periods rather than the degree of tilt, and this pattern continues to present-day.

92f545655bf9.title: Danuvius guggenmosi
92f545655bf9.sentence: The remains of Danuvius were discovered in the Hammerschmiede clay pit near the town of Pforzen in southern Germany, magnetostratigraphically dated to 11.62 million years ago (mya) at the Serravallian-Tortonian boundary (the Astaracian–Vallesian boundary in ELMA), and were unearthed between 2015 and 2018.

92fc087db1e7.title: Cryogenian
92fc087db1e7.sentence: The end of the period also saw the origin of heterotrophic plankton, which would feed on unicellular algae and prokaryotes, ending the bacterial dominance of the oceans.

93028e88f211.title: Glyptodon
93028e88f211.sentence: Glyptodon and Glyptotherium evolved in the Pliocene, starting around 3.9 million years ago.

930efb0a5c07.title: Ordovician
930efb0a5c07.sentence: All Late Cambrian trilobite orders persisted, joined by the new order Phacopida.

9314927122ff.title: Flood basalt
9314927122ff.sentence: However, the eruption produced just 14 cubic kilometers (3.4 cu mi) of lava, which is tiny compared with the Roza Member of the Columbia River Plateau, erupted in the mid-Miocene, which contained at least 1,500 cubic kilometers (360 cu mi) of lava.

9317d7d9370b.title: Middle Miocene Climatic Optimum
9317d7d9370b.sentence: Estimates derived from Mg/Ca palaeothermometry in the benthic foraminifer Oridorsalis umbonatus suggest the onset of the MMCO occurred at 16.9 Ma, peak warmth at 15.3 Ma, and the end of the MMCO at 13.8 Ma.

9318d835c003.title: European Cenozoic Rift System
9318d835c003.sentence: The largest volcanic centres were located to the southwest of the Limagne and Bresse Grabens, the Massif Central, at the rift triple junction at the northern end of the Upper Rhine Graben, the Vogelsberg Mountains and around the Eger Graben.

931bf2fa67a6.title: Tornquist Sea
931bf2fa67a6.sentence: It probably formed at the same time (c. 600 Ma) as the Iapetus Ocean.

931c865a2da1.title: Western Interior Seaway
931c865a2da1.sentence: During the late Cretaceous, the Western Interior Seaway went through multiple periods of anoxia, when the bottom water was devoid of oxygen and the water column was stratified.

93308c068baf.title: Holocene climatic optimum
93308c068baf.sentence: The Amery Ice Shelf retreated approximately 80 kilometres landward during this warm interval.

933932eeb4c3.title: Batomorphi
933932eeb4c3.sentence: Fossil denticles (tooth-like scales in the skin) resembling those of today's chondrichthyans date at least as far back as the Ordovician, with the oldest unambiguous fossils of cartilaginous fish dating from the middle Devonian.

933da3586aa9.title: Cryogenian
933da3586aa9.sentence: Between the Sturtian and Marinoan glaciations was a so-called "Cryogenian interglacial period" marked by relatively warm climate and anoxic oceans, along with marine transgression.

9341be2fbd7a.title: Livyatan

The peak likelihood for thylacine extinction was from the late 1980s through the early 2000s. There is extensive evidence for thylacines in mainland Australia from paleontology and rock art. 9aa97ddef093.sentence: Gondwana and Laurasia formed the Pangaea supercontinent during the Carboniferous.

9aad9999552d.title: Mammoth

9ab571efd70d.title: Paleocene

9ab9b00a0351.title: Australopithecus africanus

9abc744307d5.title: Mount Pinatubo

9ac8b9ee8d45.title: Solnhofen Limestone

9acde83590f7.title: Cambrian
9acde83590f7.sentence: The early Cambrian was a period of rapid evolution, known as the Cambrian Explosion, which saw the appearance of animals with biomineralised skeletons, the development of increasing complex animal morphology, behaviour and lifestyles, changes in the sea floor substrate with the advent of burrowing, and the opening up of new biodiverse ecosystems.

9ace3921842b.title: Mount Okmok

9aea6c3cda74.title: Paleolithic

9afabaf15245.title: Gauss–Matuyama reversal

9b02ed3753e1.title: Sivapithecus

9b087b261613.title: Triassic Boreal Ocean Delta Plain
9b087b261613.sentence: The formation of what would become the TBO Delta plain began soon after the Permian-Triassic Event when the Triassic Boreal Ocean experienced rapid sediment deposition, resulting in the formation of a shallow basin by the Early Triassic.

9b0ec1041a45.title: Gondwana

9b1e3b189655.title: Pangaea

9b2df93d49c8.title: Clovis culture

9b2ff342b869.sentence: These extinctions were staggered over tens of thousands of years, spanning from around 50,000 years Before Present (BP) to around 10,000 years BP, with temperate adapted species like the straight-tusked elephant and the narrow-nosed rhinoceros generally going extinct earlier than cold adapted species like the woolly mammoth and woolly rhinoceros.

cc3458ad67ff.title: Last Interglacial

cc6543b0277c.title: Choristodera

cc998b4000a7.title: Evolution of fish
cc998b4000a7.sentence: Vertebrates, in other words the first fish, originated about 530 million years ago during the Cambrian explosion, which saw the rise in animal diversity.

cc9eb7596a43.section: Causes > Emeishan Traps > Criticism of the volcanic cause hypothesis
cc9eb7596a43.sentence: A 2015 study called into question whether the Capitanian mass extinction event was global in nature at all or merely a regional biotic crisis limited to South China and a few other areas, finding no evidence for terrestrial or marine extinctions in eastern Australia linked to the Emeishan Traps or to any proposed extinction triggers invoked to explain the biodiversity drop in low-latitudes of the Northern Hemisphere.

cca1fab5a416.title: Sevier orogeny

ccb6a52e44c5.title: Francevillian biota
ccb6a52e44c5.sentence: A 2023 review suggested that the structures were potentially artifacts of diagenesis, and that reliably distinguishing between biogenic and abiogenic structures in Paleoproterozoic rocks could be "extremely difficult", and therefore the Francevillian Biota and other supposed multicellular fossils of a similar age "currently fail to pass the stringent criteria for these structures to be viewed as bona fide fossils".

ccba3b190030.title: Mogollon-Datil volcanic field
ccba3b190030.sentence: The volcanic activity of the Mogollon-Datil began near present-day Las Cruces, New Mexico about 36.2 million years ago (mya) with the eruption of the Cueva Tuff from the Organ Caldera.

ccbad1ab77f9.title: Mongol-Okhotsk Ocean
ccbad1ab77f9.sentence: Paleomagnetic data collected between 1987 and 2010 suggest that the Mongol-Okhotsk oceanic crust subducted under the terranes of Mongolia in the Late Jurassic or Early Cretaceous.

ccc28d74f911.title: Magdalenian
ccc28d74f911.sentence: Around 14-12,000 years ago, the Western Hunter-Gatherer cluster (which predominantly descended from the Villabruna cluster, with possible ancestry related to the Goyet-Q2 cluster), expanded northwards across the Alps, largely replacing the Goyet-Q2 cluster associated Magdalenian groups in Western Europe.

ccecc23bd399.title: North China Craton
ccecc23bd399.section: Tectonic evolution > Phanerozoic history (539 million years ago to present time)
ccecc23bd399.sentence: Scientists proposed four important deformation events that could possibly lead to or contributed to craton destruction, namely subduction and closure of Paleo-Asian Ocean in Carboniferous to Jurassic (324–236 million years ago), late Triassic collision of the Yangtze Craton and North China Craton (240–210 million years ago), Jurassic subduction of the Paleo-Pacific Plate (200–100 million years ago) and Cretaceous collapse of orogens (130–120 million years ago).

ccf9ffe4f548.title: Paleogene
ccf9ffe4f548.sentence: During the mid to late Eocene (50–35 Ma), plate convergence rates decreased and the dip of the Farallon slab began to steepen.

cd0176da3c88.title: Phanerozoic

cd0176da3c88.sentence: By the Middle Devonian, shrub-like forests existed: lycophytes, horsetails and progymnosperm.

cd093b7f6d1e.title: Dinosaur
cd093b7f6d1e.sentence: The fossil record shows that birds are feathered dinosaurs, having evolved from earlier theropods during the Late Jurassic epoch, and are the only dinosaur lineage known to have survived the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event approximately 66 mya.

cd0cea39670c.title: Krakatoa
cd0cea39670c.sentence: With an estimated volcanic explosivity index of 6, the eruption was equivalent to 200 megatons of TNT (840 PJ)—about 13,000 times the nuclear yield of the Little Boy bomb (13 to 16 kt) dropped on Hiroshima, Japan, during World War II, and four times the yield of Tsar Bomba, the most powerful nuclear device ever detonated at 50 Mt.

cd13caa7f1ee.title: Acraman impact structure
cd13caa7f1ee.sentence: Some authors estimate an original diameter of up to 85 to 90 kilometres (53 to 56 mi), while other suggest a smaller size, perhaps only 35 to 40 kilometres (22 to 25 mi), closer to that of the depression in which Lake Acraman is centred.

cd1ff9817d53.title: Morrison Formation
cd1ff9817d53.sentence: According to radiometric dating, the Morrison Formation dates from 156.3 ± 2 million years old (Ma) at its base, to 146.8 ± 1 million years old at the top, which places it in the earliest Kimmeridgian, and early Tithonian stages of the late Jurassic.

cd3fa6e47a83.title: Zuñi sequence

cd403bee35d8.title: Tumblagooda Sandstone

cd6b689dac22.title: Homo erectus

ce2f221ce3dd.title: Triassic–Jurassic extinction
ce2f221ce3dd.sentence: Though spore turnovers are observed across the Triassic-Jurassic boundary, the abruptness of this transition and the relative abundances of given spore types both before and after the boundary are highly variable from one region to another, pointing to a global ecological restructuring rather than a mass extinction of plants.

ce41d1b9db80.title: Cape Fold Belt

ce550add70db.sentence: The impact of the Capitanian extinction event on marine ecosystems is still heavily debated by palaeontologists.

ce68f8cbfe26.sentence: The area was an open grassland dotted with woodlands inhabited by mammoths and giant ground sloths.

ce7245c3e4e8.title: Gorgonopsia

ce8173b68fcb.title: Zuñi sequence
ce8173b68fcb.sentence: The Zuñi sequence was the major cratonic sequence after the Absaroka sequence that began in the latest Jurassic, peaked in the late Cretaceous, and ended by the start of the following Paleocene.

ce8aa9ca7e8e.title: African humid period
ce8aa9ca7e8e.sentence: The Blue Nile basin became less moist with a noticeable decrease of Nile discharge about 4,000 years ago.

ce8c26880e84.title: Pilbara Craton
ce8c26880e84.sentence: Evidence of the earliest known life on land may have been found in 3.48-billion-year-old geyserite and other related mineral deposits (often found around hot springs and geysers) uncovered in the Dresser Formation in the Pilbara Craton.

ce92de9907c4.title: Baltica
ce92de9907c4.sentence: Sarmatia and Volgo-Uralia formed a proto-craton (sometimes called "Proto-Baltica") at c. 2.0 Ga which collided with Fennoscandia c. 1.8–1.7 Ga.

ce97cc9ef183.title: Last Glacial Maximum
ce97cc9ef183.sentence: Based on changes in position of ice sheet margins dated via terrestrial cosmogenic nuclides and radiocarbon dating, the growth of ice sheets in the southern hemisphere commenced around 33,000 years ago and maximum coverage has been estimated to have occurred sometime between 26,500 years ago and 20,000 years ago.

ce9c02642c79.title: Sima de los Huesos hominins
ce9c02642c79.sentence: The Sima de los Huesos fossils illustrated the range of anatomical variation that could be present in a given population of Middle Pleistocene Europe across gender and age lines, clarifying the relationships among Middle Pleistocene European fossils and the evolution of Neanderthals.

cea639de18c9.title: List of largest volcanic eruptions
cea639de18c9.sentence: Eruptions the size of that at Lake Toba 74,000 years ago, at least 2,800 cubic kilometres (670 cu mi), or the Yellowstone eruption 640,000 years ago, around 1,000 cubic kilometres (240 cu mi), occur worldwide every 50,000 to 100,000 years.

cea9ca0cba9b.title: Carnosauria
cea9ca0cba9b.sentence: Allosauroids first appeared in the Middle Jurassic period and were the first giant taxa (weighing more than 2 tons) in theropod history.

ceab850ce9a9.title: Macroraptorial sperm whale
ceab850ce9a9.sentence: A 30 cm (12 in) tooth found in Australia indicates macroraptorials still existed 5 mya in the Pliocene.

ceb28ca4cba1.title: Past sea level
ceb28ca4cba1.section: Geological influences > Changes through geologic time
ceb28ca4cba1.sentence: During the most recent ice age (at its maximum about 20,000 years ago) the world's sea level was about 130 m lower than today, due to the large amount of sea water that had evaporated and been deposited as snow and ice, mostly in the Laurentide Ice Sheet.

cec61f56a7ee.title: Long Valley Caldera
cec61f56a7ee.sentence: All but one of these volcanoes, 1–2-million-year-old Glass Mountain (made of obsidian), were destroyed by the major (VEI-7) eruption of the area 760,000 years ago, which released 600 cubic kilometers (144 cu mi) of material from vents just inside the margin of the caldera.

ced2ae5e3b8b.title: Obolon' crater
ced2ae5e3b8b.sentence: One estimate puts the age at 169 ± 7 million years (Middle Jurassic).

ced2cbcec126.title: Beringia

cedc21b6c06f.title: Indian Ocean Geoid Low
