cedc21b6c06f.sentence: As this cold dense Tethys slab reached the bottom of the mantle, it churned the African LLVP (Large Low-Velocity Province), giving rise to mantle plumes of hot low-density material.

cee60c72525c.title: Gondwana
cee60c72525c.section: Break-up > Mesozoic > Opening of western Indian Ocean
cee60c72525c.sentence: Gondwana began to break up in the early Jurassic following the extensive and fast emplacement of the Karoo-Ferrar flood basalts c. 184 Ma.

cf02a54d36f5.title: AL 333
cf02a54d36f5.sentence: Discovered in 1975 by Donald Johanson's team in Hadar, Ethiopia, the "First Family" is estimated to be about 3.2 million years old and consists of the remains of at least thirteen individuals of different ages.

cf08f6f19b34.title: Australopithecus afarensis
cf08f6f19b34.sentence: If correct, this would make it the oldest evidence of sharp-edged stone tool use at 3.4 million years old, and would be attributable to A. afarensis as it is the only hominin species known within the time and place.

cf10b020db0a.title: Ireviken event
cf10b020db0a.sentence: It occurred at the Llandovery/Wenlock boundary (mid Silurian, 432.9 ± 1.2 million years ago).

cf213c3cba70.title: Dnieper-Donets Rift
cf213c3cba70.sentence: The Dniepr-Donets Paleorift was the site of Devonian magmatic activity that begun in Late Frasnian and peaked in the Famennian caused by a mantle plume.

cf252aa6d946.title: Boring Billion
cf252aa6d946.sentence: In 2013, geochemist Grant Young used the term "Barren Billion" to refer to a period of apparent glacial stagnation and lack of carbon isotope excursions from 1.8 to 0.8 Ga.

cf27efc6d06b.title: Beringia
cf27efc6d06b.sentence: The ANA lineage was estimated as having been formed between 20,000 and 25,000 years ago by a mixture of East Asian (~65%) and Ancient North Eurasian (~35%) lineages, consistent with the model of the peopling of the Americas via Beringia during the Last Glacial Maximum.

cf324862e452.title: Austroalpine nappes
cf324862e452.section: Eoalpine formation of the Austroalpine nappes and the Eastern Alps
cf324862e452.sentence: The Austroalpine nappes of the Eastern Alps were formed in the first, early, Eo-Alpine orogeny in the Early Cretaceous, 140-84 Ma (millions years ago).

cf39fcb2636c.title: Mesozoic marine revolution
cf39fcb2636c.sentence: The Mesozoic marine revolution (MMR) refers to the increase in shell-crushing (durophagous) and boring predation in shallow-sea (neritic) and some deep-sea marine organisms throughout the Mesozoic era (251 Mya to 66 Mya), along with bulldozing and sediment remodelling in benthic marine habitats.

cf3f15f57a20.title: Marine Isotope Stage 11

d2b5ef475f65.sentence: Eurypterids were most diverse and abundant between the Middle Silurian and the Early Devonian, with an absolute peak in diversity during the Pridoli epoch, 423 to 419.2 million years ago, of the very latest Silurian.

d2bcb18b0789.title: Krakatoa
d2bcb18b0789.sentence: Ash was propelled to a height of 80 km (260,000 ft).

d2bea8ea5650.title: Ordovician
d2bea8ea5650.sentence: By the late Early Ordovician, the Earth cooled, giving way to a more temperate climate in the Middle Ordovician, with the Earth likely entering the Early Palaeozoic Ice Age during the Sandbian, and possibly as early as the Darriwilian or even the Floian.

d2d26808bd6d.title: Paleogene
d2d26808bd6d.sentence: The Caribbean plate is largely composed of oceanic crust of the Caribbean Large Igneous Province that formed during the Late Cretaceous.

d2d29712cc3b.title: Cambrian
d2d29712cc3b.section: Geochemistry > Isotope excursions > Cambrian Stages 2 and 3
d2d29712cc3b.sentence: However, during the early Cambrian, a series of linked δ13C and δ34S excursions indicate high burial rates of both organic carbon and pyrite in biologically productive yet anoxic ocean floor waters.

d2e58798cd35.title: Moenkopi Formation
d2e58798cd35.sentence: The Moenkopi Formation is a geological formation that is spread across the U.S. states of New Mexico, northern Arizona, Nevada, southeastern California, eastern Utah and western Colorado.

d2e8109d7ae8.title: Cowie Formation
d2e8109d7ae8.sentence: The age of this formation is controversial, originally estimated at the Middle Silurian, specifically Wenlock to Ludlow, but zircon geochronology points to the Early Devonian, Lochkovian instead.

d2ea4ebc1b8f.title: Lake Ojibway
d2ea4ebc1b8f.sentence: The lake likely drained approximately 8,200 years BP.

d2ee4012009e.title: Tauranga Volcanic Centre
d2ee4012009e.sentence: The Waiteariki ignimbrite erupted 2.1 million years ago. but there are at least eight other large eruptions that occurred in the Tauranga Volcanic Centre in its period of activity.

d2f2e69f9760.title: Agnostida
d2f2e69f9760.sentence: Agnostidan diversity severely declined during the Cambrian-Ordovician transition, and the last agnostidans went extinct in the Late Ordovician.

d3088d845aa3.title: Earliest known life forms
d3088d845aa3.sentence: Therefore, the earliest time for the origin of life on Earth is at least 3.5 billion years ago and possibly as early as 4.1 billion years ago—not long after the oceans formed 4.5 billion years ago and after the formation of the Earth 4.54 billion years ago.

d30b5f0142e2.title: Trilobite
d30b5f0142e2.section: Evolution > Divergence and extinction > Silurian and Devonian
d30b5f0142e2.sentence: The Middle-Late Devonian was a decisive turning point in trilobite history, with the Taghanic event during the Givetian sharply decreasing trilobite diversity, particularly in shallow water environments, which was followed by the Late Devonian mass extinction/Kellwasser event (involving a combination of sea level change and marine anoxia) at the Frasnian–Famennian boundary, widely regarded as one of the most significant mass extinction events in Earth's history, decimating the group's diversity including the extinction of the orders Corynexochida, Harpetida and Odontopleurida, with the low trilobite diversity in its aftermath in the Famennian, consisting only of the orders Phacopida and Proetida, being again strongly impacted by the Hangenberg event (also called the end-Devonian mass extinction) at the end of the Devonian, with both shallow water and deep water trilobites being affected.

d30ee3d01aba.title: Arctodus
d30ee3d01aba.sentence: This was followed by a decrease around 48,000 BP (correlated with expanding Yukon forests circa the MIS 3 interstadial), which continued until the local extinction of Beringian A. simus by near 23,000 BP during the last glacial maximum.

d311f91ab953.title: Pangaea
d311f91ab953.section: Formation > Collision of Gondwana with Euramerica
d311f91ab953.sentence: In the Early Carboniferous, northwest Africa had touched the southeastern coast of Euramerica, creating the southern portion of the Appalachian Mountains, the Meseta Mountains, and the Mauritanide Mountains, an event called the Variscan orogeny.

d31825ffaf7b.title: Skagerrak-Centered Large Igneous Province
d31825ffaf7b.sentence: The SCLIP covered an area of at least 0.5×10^6 km2 (0.19×10^6 sq mi) and includes the Oslo and Skagerrak grabens, areas in south-western Sweden, Scotland, northern England, and the central North Sea.

d32056d7be0c.title: Timeline of Earth
d32056d7be0c.sentence: - c. 4,250 Ma – The Earliest evidence for life appears as unusually high amounts of light isotopes of carbon, a common sign of life, are found in Earth's oldest mineral deposits located in the Jack Hills of Western Australia.

d3230106525b.title: Dwyka Group
d3230106525b.sentence: The result was the development of the Permo-Carboniferous glacial environment where massive ice sheets entombed the early Karoo Basin in the surrounding highlands and permanent, floating glaciers in the lowlands.

d3247cfbc36a.title: Mid-Tertiary ignimbrite flare-up
d3247cfbc36a.sentence: The Mid-Tertiary ignimbrite flare-up, was a dramatic period of volcanic eruptions in mid-Cenozoic time, approximately 25–40 million years ago, centered in the western United States.

d326d5b63e52.title: Dmanisi Paleolithic site
d326d5b63e52.sentence: The earliest securely documented occupations date to approximately 1.8 million years ago, while the hominin-bearing deposits formed around 1.77 million years ago.

d33add0e4b4b.title: Tectonic evolution of Patagonia
d33add0e4b4b.sentence: Following the period of late Paleozoic convergence that led to the collision of Patagonia with Gondwana, a transition to extensional tectonics in the Triassic period induced rifting within Patagonia.

d3619ba61d6d.title: Ordovician
d3619ba61d6d.sentence: Molluscs became ubiquitous, particularly bivalves, gastropods, and nautiloid cephalopods, the latter diversifying from shallow waters to occupy pelagic niches across all latitudes.

d36813fe3bad.title: Early Triassic
d36813fe3bad.section: Early Triassic life > Fauna and flora > Aquatic biota
d36813fe3bad.sentence: Hupehsuchia, Ichthyopterygia and Sauropterygia are among the first marine reptiles to enter the scene in the Olenekian (e.g. Cartorhynchus, Chaohusaurus, Utatsusaurus, Hupehsuchus, Grippia, Omphalosaurus, Corosaurus).

d3732b9d11e9.title: Magnetostratigraphy
d3732b9d11e9.sentence: The C (for Cenozoic) sequence ends in the Cretaceous Normal Superchron termed C34n which on age calibration occurred at 120.964 Ma and lasted to Chron C33r at 83.650 Ma that defined the Santonian geologic age.

d378d4472144.title: Denisovan

d381e12dbcc3.title: Paisley Caves

d38f68043b14.title: Red Wing crater
d38f68043b14.sentence: It has been suggested by Geophysicist David Rowley of the University of Chicago, working with John Spray of the University of New Brunswick and Simon Kelley of the Open University, that the Red Wing crater may have been part of a hypothetical multiple impact event which also formed the Manicouagan impact structure in northern Quebec, Rochechouart impact structure in France, Saint Martin crater in Manitoba, and Obolon' crater in Ukraine.

d39267ad22eb.title: High Arctic Large Igneous Province
d39267ad22eb.sentence: The BLIP intrusions could have released perhaps 9,000 Gt (8.9×1012 long tons; 9.9×1012 short tons) of carbon from the contact aureoles which could have triggered the Aptian oceanic anoxic event (OAE1a) at 120 Ma.

d3970cef557b.title: Paris biota
d3970cef557b.sentence: The organisms of the Paris biota lived in a shallow marine epicontinental sea (western USA basin) on the western coast of Pangea.

d3d77d92355e.title: Heinrich event

d3e612133938.title: Paleoarchean
d3e612133938.sentence: The most powerful of the impacts such as the S2 impact, which dates to 3.26 billion years ago, probably caused extremely strong earthquakes worldwide, megatsunamis thousands of meters high, as well as boiling the surface of the oceans, resulting in tens of meters of global ocean evaporation.

d3f335ebb55f.title: Shuram excursion
d3f335ebb55f.sentence: It was first noticed in the Wonoka Formation in South Australia in 1990 and later in the Clemente Formation of Mexico in 1992 and the Shuram Formation in Oman in 1993.

d400cad7b611.title: Paleolithic
d400cad7b611.sentence: The Lower Paleolithic Homo erectus possibly invented rafts (c. 840,000 – c. 800,000 BP) to travel over large bodies of water, which may have allowed a group of Homo erectus to reach the island of Flores and evolve into the small hominin Homo floresiensis.

d405ad6e7baa.title: Dinosaur
d405ad6e7baa.sentence: The surviving lineages of neornithine birds, including the ancestors of modern ratites, ducks and chickens, and a variety of waterbirds, diversified rapidly at the beginning of the Paleogene period, entering ecological niches left vacant by the extinction of Mesozoic dinosaur groups such as the arboreal enantiornithines, aquatic hesperornithines, and even the larger terrestrial theropods (in the form of Gastornis, eogruiids, bathornithids, ratites, geranoidids, mihirungs, and "terror birds").

d40989228075.title: List of lagerstätten
d40989228075.sentence: Fur Formation | 55–53 Ma | Fur & Mors, Denmark | Preserves abundant fossil fish, insects, reptiles, birds, and plants. The Fur Formation was deposited about 55 Ma, just after the Palaeocene - Eocene boundary, and its tropical or subtropical flora indicates that the climate following the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum was moderately warm (approximately 4-8 degrees warmer than today).

d40a7976ac0b.title: Rudists
d40a7976ac0b.sentence: The rudists became extinct at the end of the Cretaceous, apparently as a result of the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.

d411374e542b.title: Neolithic Revolution
d411374e542b.section: Centers of agricultural origin > West Asia
d411374e542b.sentence: The wear traces indicate that tools were used for harvesting near-ripe semi-green wild cereals, shortly before grains are ripe and disperse naturally.

d414db0ff758.title: Geology of the Appalachians
d414db0ff758.sentence: - The Alleghanian orogeny began 325 Ma and lasted 65 million years.

d41d5a120ab2.title: Rivera plate
d41d5a120ab2.sentence: The Rivera plate is believed to have separated from the Cocos plate located to its southeast about 5–10 million years ago.

d41f0d3621e2.title: Algoman orogeny
d41f0d3621e2.sentence: The timing of initiation of plate tectonics is still debated, but if modern-day tectonics were operative in the Archean, higher heat fluxes might have caused tectonic processes to be more active.

d432f51deda7.title: Gomphotherium land bridge

d432f51deda7.sentence: Elephantimorphs, a clade of proboscideans that includes mastodons and modern elephants, first appeared in the Late Oligocene.

d43ad8f8577f.title: Marine Isotope Stage 11
d43ad8f8577f.sentence: Sedimentary deposits from Greenland suggest a near-complete deglaciation of south Greenland, and a subsequent sea level rise of 4.5 to 6 metres of sea-level-equivalent volume during MIS 11, around 410,000 to 400,000 years ago.

d464fda355f9.title: Morokweng impact structure
d464fda355f9.sentence: Its age is estimated to be 146.06 ± 0.16 million years, placing it within the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic, several million years before the Jurassic–Cretaceous boundary.

d466cc452525.title: Chesapeake Bay impact crater
d466cc452525.sentence: Continued slumping of sediments over the rubble of the crater has helped shape the Chesapeake Bay.

d46b314b692a.title: Stegodon
d46b314b692a.sentence: It was originally assigned to the family Elephantidae along with modern elephants but is now placed in the extinct family Stegodontidae.

d47249456a79.title: Late Antique Little Ice Age
d47249456a79.sentence: The cooling period contributed to the migrations of the Lombards and the early Slavs into Roman territory in Italy and the Balkans.

d47eda234816.title: Sturgeon Lake Caldera
d47eda234816.sentence: Episodes of subaerial and subaqueous explosive felsic volcanism created rhyodacitic to rhyolitic tuffs and lapilli tuffs.

d47f31ec3398.title: Gunflint chert
d47f31ec3398.sentence: Finally, dating of interbedded ash layers within the Gunflint Iron Formation yielded ages between 1.86 and 1.99 Ga, which are most similar to the current consensus age of 1.878 Ga ± 1.3 Ma.

d48235e50d34.title: Dikika
d48235e50d34.sentence: Papers also propose the earliest evidence of stone tool use at this site in the form of cut marks on animal bone.

d49d8cd640af.title: Toarcian Oceanic Anoxic Event
d49d8cd640af.sentence: Toarcian anoxia was responsible for the deposition of commercially extracted oil shales, particularly in China.

d4b672722dc9.sentence: The basin initially developed in an extensional setting during the Early Permian before evolving into a retroarc foreland basin during the Late Permian as a result of contraction and uplift associated with the New England Orogen and Hunter–Bowen orogeny.

d4cded88e3e4.title: Cooksonia
d4cded88e3e4.sentence: The earliest Cooksonia date from the middle of the Silurian (the Wenlock epoch); the group continued to be an important component of the flora until the end of the Early Devonian, a total time span of 433 to 393 million years ago.

d4ceead4933f.title: Ireviken event

d4dbc069c1e7.title: Kupferschiefer

d4ef8afe4f1f.title: Timeline of life

d4f18887e348.title: Antarctic land bridge
d4f18887e348.sentence: Thus, a narrow connection between South America, Antarctica, and Australia existed between ~96 to 50 million years ago, and South America and Antarctica (but not Australia) remained connected up to 28 million years ago.

d50778aa2018.title: North American land mammal age
d50778aa2018.sentence: Rancholabrean | 0.210 Ma. | Middle Pleistocene | C1n | The ice age continues. Bison expand south of Alaska alongside other northerly specialists such as caribou, muskoxen, moose, and woolly mammoths.

d51c4319c9dc.title: Siderian
d51c4319c9dc.sentence: In the region pertaining to present-day Scotland, the Scourie dike swarm penetrated the Lewisian Gneiss Complex from about 2418 to 2375 Ma, while the Widgiemooltha dike swarm intruded into the Yilgarn Craton in Australia at around 2410 Ma.

d51d5c9d6d59.title: Large igneous province

d51d5c9d6d59.sentence: The eruption of basaltic LIPs onto the earth's surface releases large volumes of sulfate gas, which forms sulfuric acid in the atmosphere; this absorbs heat and causes substantial cooling (e.g., the Laki eruption in Iceland, 1783).

d51ec15c0ba8.title: Pleistocene wolf
d51ec15c0ba8.sentence: The Ice Age reached its peak during the Last Glacial Maximum, when ice sheets commenced advancing from 33,000 years BP and reached their maximum positions 26,500 years BP.

d5271b45f221.title: Eastern Pilbara Craton
d5271b45f221.sentence: Within the Eastern Pilbara Craton there are 2 distinct lithologic divisions: (1), early Earth crust (3.8–3.53 Ga); (2), intrusive granitic domes along with greenstone belts (3.53–3.23 Ga).

d53075f0e004.title: Petalonamae
d53075f0e004.sentence: The petalonamids (Petalonamae) or frondomorphs are an extinct group of archaic animals typical of the Ediacaran biota, dating from around 635 million years ago to 516 million years ago.

d532c60f07bf.title: Šilalė Event
d532c60f07bf.sentence: The Šilalė Event, first identified in the Milaičiai-103 core in southwestern Lithuania, is marked by a negative carbon isotope excursion in carbonate rocks known as the Šilalė Negative Carbon Isotope Event.

d53fdbb2d99b.title: Paratethys
d53fdbb2d99b.sentence: From the Pliocene epoch onward (after 5 million years ago), Paratethys became progressively shallower.

d54b30eb9a35.title: Early expansions of hominins out of Africa

d54d2f3e6cf8.title: Mulde event

d55919059305.title: Earliest known life forms

d56244c0f75c.title: Homo erectus

d57528ccfb4c.title: Central Skåne Volcanic Province
d57528ccfb4c.sentence: Beneath a lahar deposit at Korsaröd (Djupadal Formation), Early Jurassic plant fossils including wood, pollen and spores have been exceptionally well preserved.

d5760f53fbd0.title: Middle Jurassic
d5760f53fbd0.sentence: The first crown-group mammals appeared in the late Early Jurassic.

d57f08b9e933.title: Megalodon

d586d6dbc1d9.title: Santa María (volcano)
d586d6dbc1d9.sentence: The first eruption of Santa María in recorded history occurred in October 1902.

d589225b8745.title: Clovis culture
d589225b8745.sentence: While historically, many scholars held to a "Clovis First" model, where Clovis represented the earliest inhabitants in the Americas, today this is generally rejected, with several generally accepted sites across the Americas being dated to at least a thousand years earlier than the oldest Clovis sites, including Monte Verde II, Cooper's Ferry, Paisley Caves, Page-Ladson, and Buttermilk Creek (Gault and Friedkin sites).

d598c5e04cb4.title: KNM-ER 406
d598c5e04cb4.sentence: The same age of 1.7 million years ago means that different species were on the scene in Africa at the same time.

d5a1f0878d2c.title: Vredefort impact structure

d5a584248a60.title: Orrorin
d5a584248a60.sentence: O. tugenensis appears to have developed bipedalism 6 million years ago.

d5ad318f6efb.title: Topper site
d5ad318f6efb.sentence: In 2004, Albert Goodyear of the University of South Carolina announced that carbonized plant remains, found as a dark stain in the light soil at the lowest excavated level at the Topper Site, had been radiocarbon dated to approximately 50,000 years ago, or approximately 37,000 years before the Clovis people.

d5ade0e2b3af.title: Central Andean Pluvial Event
d5ade0e2b3af.sentence: The first is wetter and begins in the late glacial (17,500-15,900 years ago); the second is drier and continued into the early Holocene (until 9,700-8,500 years ago).

d5b4fedb44bb.sentence: Proterozoic stromatolite microfossils (preserved by permineralization in silica) include cyanobacteria and possibly some forms of the eukaryote chlorophytes (that is, green algae).

d5f3d1da5e78.title: Stegodon
d5f3d1da5e78.sentence: The survival of the Asian elephant as opposed to Stegodon orientalis in Southeast Asia and South China has been suggested to be due to its more flexible diet in comparison to S. orientalis.

d5f827bcb831.title: Orogeny

d6112d58331d.sentence: Shungite-bearing deposits that retain sedimentary structures are interpreted as metamorphosed oil source rocks.

d622ce7fa264.title: Paleo-Tethys Ocean

d679ae41c576.title: Eocene Thermal Maximum 2

e5ec174df841.title: Long Valley Caldera

e5f0ad42e179.title: Ontong Java Plateau

e64451a975e5.title: Baltica
e64451a975e5.sentence: The allochthons were accreted to Baltica during the closure of the Iapetus Ocean c. 430–410 Ma; Baltica's basement and the allochthons were then subducted to UHP depth c. 425–400 Ma; and they were finally exhumed to their present location c. 400–385 Ma.

e645f31db4d5.title: Pannotia
e645f31db4d5.sentence: Pannotia (from Greek: pan-, "all", -nótos, "south"; meaning "all southern land"), also known as the Vendian supercontinent, Greater Gondwana, and the Pan-African supercontinent, is a proposed relatively short-lived Neoproterozoic supercontinent that may have formed at the end of the Precambrian during the Pan-African orogeny (650–500 Ma), during the Cryogenian period, and broke apart 560 Ma with the opening of the Iapetus Ocean, in the late Ediacaran and early Cambrian.

e6470048f2f8.title: Laurasia

e65b00783ef4.title: Clovis culture

e65ebd91f9ff.title: Early Holocene sea level rise

e66095e50465.title: Phoenix plate
e66095e50465.sentence: Although active subduction occurred for over 100 million years, it slowed dramatically or stopped entirely about 3.3 million years ago when seafloor spreading on the Antarctic–Phoenix Ridge ceased, leaving a small remnant of the former Phoenix plate incorporated in the Antarctic plate.

e668dfe5af03.title: Paleogene
e668dfe5af03.sentence: A rapid decrease in velocity to c. 5 cm/yr in the early Eocene records the collision of the Tethyan (Tibetan) Himalayas, the leading edge of Greater India, with the Lhasa terrane of Tibet (southern Eurasian margin), along the Indus-Yarling-Zangbo suture zone.

e672101e56df.title: Lake Lahontan
